hi_nuance: Learners often say 'do the shirt' or 'set the shirt' translating from Hindi 'shirt karna/set karna'; the correct fixed verb here is 'iron', as in 'iron a shirt' or 'iron your shirt'. Note this is distinct from the appliance entry — here the focus is the specific daily task.

examples.en: I always iron my shirt the night before an important meeting.
examples.hi: मैं ज़रूरी मीटिंग से एक रात पहले हमेशा अपनी शर्ट प्रेस करता हूँ।

examples.en: Could you iron this shirt for me? I'm running late.
examples.hi: क्या तुम मेरे लिए यह शर्ट प्रेस कर सकते हो? मुझे देर हो रही है।

examples.en: He ironed his shirt quickly before the video call.
examples.hi: उसने वीडियो कॉल से पहले जल्दी से अपनी शर्ट प्रेस की।

examples.en: Ironing a shirt properly takes more time than you think.
examples.hi: शर्ट को ठीक से प्रेस करने में सोचने से ज़्यादा समय लगता है।

examples.en: She showed me the right way to iron a shirt collar.
examples.hi: उसने मुझे शर्ट के कॉलर को सही तरीके से प्रेस करना दिखाया।

common_mistake.wrong: I will set my shirt before going out.
common_mistake.right: I will iron my shirt before going out.
common_mistake.why: 'Set the shirt' is a literal translation of a Hindi/Hinglish phrase; English uses the specific verb 'iron' for removing creases from clothes with a hot iron, not 'set'.

cloze.sentence: I need to ____ this white shirt before the interview tomorrow.

en_def: a narrow folding table with a padded top used for ironing clothes
hi_def: कपड़े प्रेस करने के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाली एक संकरी, पैडेड मेज़, जो मोड़ी जा सकती है
hi_nuance: Many small Indian households iron directly on a bed or the floor with a cloth underneath, so 'ironing board' may not be a familiar object; learners sometimes just say 'table' for it. In English it has its own specific name, 'ironing board', distinct from a regular table.

examples.en: Set up the ironing board near the window for good light.
examples.hi: अच्छी रोशनी के लिए खिड़की के पास आयरनिंग बोर्ड लगाओ।

examples.en: The ironing board collapsed while she was pressing a saree.
examples.hi: साड़ी प्रेस करते समय आयरनिंग बोर्ड गिर गया।

examples.en: We don't have an ironing board, so I iron on the bed.
examples.hi: हमारे पास आयरनिंग बोर्ड नहीं है, इसलिए मैं बिस्तर पर प्रेस करता हूँ।

examples.en: Fold the ironing board and keep it behind the door.
examples.hi: आयरनिंग बोर्ड मोड़कर दरवाज़े के पीछे रख दो।

examples.en: The cover on the ironing board is burnt in one corner.
examples.hi: आयरनिंग बोर्ड के कवर का एक कोना जला हुआ है।

common_mistake.wrong: I keep my iron on the table.
common_mistake.right: I keep my iron on the ironing board.
common_mistake.why: Learners default to the generic word 'table' because a dedicated ironing board is less common at home in India; English distinguishes this specific folding surface with its own name.

cloze.sentence: She unfolded the ____ and plugged in the iron.

en_def: having small folds or creases, especially in cloth or skin
hi_def: सिलवटों वाला या मुड़ा-तुड़ा (कपड़े या त्वचा के लिए)
hi_nuance: Learners often say 'the shirt has folds' instead of 'the shirt is wrinkled', because 'sikan' in Hindi is translated as 'fold' rather than the more natural adjective 'wrinkled' or 'creased'. British English also commonly uses 'creased' for clothes; American English leans more on 'wrinkled'.

examples.en: Your shirt looks wrinkled; you should iron it.
examples.hi: तुम्हारी शर्ट में सिलवटें हैं; तुम्हें इसे प्रेस करना चाहिए।

examples.en: The clothes came out of the bag all wrinkled.
examples.hi: बैग से निकलते ही कपड़ों में सिलवटें पड़ गई थीं।

examples.en: I hate wearing a wrinkled shirt to office.
examples.hi: मुझे ऑफिस में सिलवटों वाली शर्ट पहनना पसंद नहीं है।

examples.en: Hang the shirt properly so it doesn't get wrinkled.
examples.hi: शर्ट को ठीक से टांगो ताकि उसमें सिलवटें न पड़ें।

examples.en: This fabric wrinkles easily, so it needs frequent ironing.
examples.hi: यह कपड़ा जल्दी सिकुड़ता है, इसलिए इसे बार-बार प्रेस करना पड़ता है।

common_mistake.wrong: My shirt has many folds, I need to press it.
common_mistake.right: My shirt is wrinkled, I need to iron it.
common_mistake.why: 'Folds' in English usually means deliberate folding (like folding paper), not the messy creases from being packed or worn; the correct adjective for messy creases in cloth is 'wrinkled' or 'creased'.

cloze.sentence: Take that ____ jacket off and hang it up properly.

en_def: a line or fold made in cloth or paper, either by accident (a wrinkle) or on purpose (like a trouser crease)
hi_def: कपड़े या कागज़ पर पड़ी एक रेखा या मोड़, जो गलती से (सिलवट) या जानबूझकर (जैसे पैंट की क्रीज़) बनाई जाती है
hi_nuance: This word is tricky because it can mean both an unwanted wrinkle and a deliberately pressed line, like the sharp line down the front of trousers. Indian English speakers usually know 'crease' from tailoring context ('crease nikalo'), but forget it can also mean an accidental wrinkle in British English usage.

examples.en: Iron a sharp crease down the front of your trousers.
examples.hi: अपनी पैंट के आगे एक तेज़ क्रीज़ बनाओ।

examples.en: There's a crease across the back of your shirt from sitting.
examples.hi: बैठने की वजह से तुम्हारी शर्ट की पीठ पर एक सिलवट है।

examples.en: The tailor pressed a neat crease into the trousers.
examples.hi: दर्ज़ी ने पैंट में एक साफ क्रीज़ बना दी।

examples.en: Fold along this line to avoid an ugly crease later.
examples.hi: बाद में बदसूरत सिलवट से बचने के लिए इस रेखा पर मोड़ो।

examples.en: The photo got a crease when it was folded in the wallet.
examples.hi: बटुए में मुड़ने से फोटो पर एक क्रीज़ पड़ गई।

common_mistake.wrong: Make a fold in your pant while ironing.
common_mistake.right: Press a sharp crease into your trousers while ironing.
common_mistake.why: Learners use 'fold' for this deliberate tailoring line, but the specific English word for the neat pressed line on trousers is 'crease', which sounds sharper and more precise than the generic word 'fold'.

cloze.sentence: The tailor ironed a perfect ____ down the front of the trousers.

en_def: a mark left on a surface or fabric by a substance such as food, oil, or ink; or to leave such a mark
hi_def: किसी वस्तु या कपड़े पर पड़ने वाला दाग, जैसे खाने, तेल या स्याही से; या दाग लगाना
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often use the borrowed word 'daag' interchangeably for both stains and scars, but in English 'stain' is only for marks from substances (on fabric, carpet, etc.), while 'scar' is used for marks on skin from a wound. Mixing these up is a common error.

examples.en: There's an oil stain on your shirt sleeve.
examples.hi: तुम्हारी शर्ट की बांह पर तेल का दाग है।

examples.en: This detergent removes tough stains easily.
examples.hi: यह डिटर्जेंट कठिन दाग आसानी से हटा देता है।

examples.en: The turmeric stained the white tablecloth yellow.
examples.hi: हल्दी ने सफेद मेज़पोश को पीला दाग दिया।

examples.en: Try to treat the stain before it dries.
examples.hi: दाग सूखने से पहले उसे साफ करने की कोशिश करो।

examples.en: Red wine leaves a stubborn stain on carpets.
examples.hi: रेड वाइन कालीन पर एक जिद्दी दाग छोड़ती है।

common_mistake.wrong: I got a stain on my hand while cooking.
common_mistake.right: I burnt my hand while cooking.
common_mistake.why: Learners sometimes use 'stain' for any mark on the body, but a mark from a burn or wound on skin is called a 'burn' or 'scar', not a 'stain'; 'stain' is reserved for marks on fabric or surfaces.

cloze.sentence: There is a curry ____ on the front of my white shirt.

en_def: a special cleaning product used to remove marks from fabric before washing
hi_def: कपड़ों से धोने से पहले दाग हटाने के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाला विशेष उत्पाद
hi_nuance: This is a fairly modern retail product name that many Indian households substitute with home remedies (soap bar, baking soda), so learners may not know the compound noun. Note it's always 'stain remover' as one item, not 'remover of stain'.

examples.en: Spray some stain remover on the ink mark before washing.
examples.hi: धोने से पहले स्याही के निशान पर थोड़ा स्टेन रिमूवर स्प्रे करो।

examples.en: This stain remover works well on grease and oil.
examples.hi: यह स्टेन रिमूवर ग्रीस और तेल पर अच्छे से काम करता है।

examples.en: Keep a bottle of stain remover handy for the kids' clothes.
examples.hi: बच्चों के कपड़ों के लिए स्टेन रिमूवर की एक बोतल पास रखो।

examples.en: I couldn't find stain remover for blood stains at the shop.
examples.hi: दुकान पर मुझे खून के दाग के लिए स्टेन रिमूवर नहीं मिला।

examples.en: Test the stain remover on a small hidden area first.
examples.hi: स्टेन रिमूवर को पहले किसी छिपी हुई छोटी जगह पर आज़माओ।

common_mistake.wrong: Use remover of the stain on this shirt.
common_mistake.right: Use stain remover on this shirt.
common_mistake.why: Hindi word order often gets carried over ('daag hatane wala'), producing 'remover of stain'; English compound nouns for products are usually formed as noun+noun, so it must be 'stain remover', not 'remover of stain'.

cloze.sentence: Dab a little ____ on the tomato sauce mark before it sets.

en_def: a strong chemical used to whiten fabric or kill germs, or the act of using it
hi_def: एक तेज़ रसायन जो कपड़ों को सफेद करने या कीटाणु मारने के लिए इस्तेमाल होता है; या उसका प्रयोग करना
hi_nuance: Many Indian households know bleach mainly as a floor/toilet cleaner brand and don't associate it with laundry, so learners may not connect the word to whitening clothes. Warn learners: bleach can damage coloured clothes, so it is normally used only on whites.

examples.en: Don't use bleach on coloured clothes; it will ruin them.
examples.hi: रंगीन कपड़ों पर ब्लीच मत इस्तेमाल करो; यह उन्हें खराब कर देगा।

examples.en: She soaked the white shirt in bleach to remove the stains.
examples.hi: उसने दाग हटाने के लिए सफेद शर्ट को ब्लीच में भिगोया।

examples.en: Bleach has a very strong, sharp smell.
examples.hi: ब्लीच की बहुत तेज़, तीखी गंध होती है।

examples.en: Always wear gloves when handling bleach.
examples.hi: ब्लीच संभालते समय हमेशा दस्ताने पहनो।

examples.en: The label says this fabric cannot be bleached.
examples.hi: लेबल पर लिखा है कि इस कपड़े को ब्लीच नहीं किया जा सकता।

common_mistake.wrong: I used bleach on my blue shirt to clean it and it turned white patches.
common_mistake.right: I accidentally used bleach on my blue shirt and it left white patches.
common_mistake.why: Learners often don't realise bleach is only safe for white fabrics; using the word 'clean' without warning misses the key nuance that bleach chemically strips colour, unlike ordinary detergent.

cloze.sentence: Never mix ____ with other cleaning chemicals; the fumes can be dangerous.

en_def: to put washed clothes outside or on a line to dry
hi_def: धुले हुए कपड़ों को सूखने के लिए बाहर या रस्सी पर टांगना
hi_nuance: 'Washing' here is a noun meaning 'clothes that have been or need to be washed', which confuses learners used to 'washing' only as a verb form; also, in India people often say 'dry the clothes' instead, which is understandable but 'hang out the washing' is the more idiomatic British phrase.

examples.en: I need to hang out the washing before it rains.
examples.hi: बारिश होने से पहले मुझे कपड़े टांगने होंगे।

examples.en: She hangs out the washing on the terrace every morning.
examples.hi: वह हर सुबह छत पर कपड़े टांगती है।

examples.en: Can you hang out the washing while I cook lunch?
examples.hi: जब मैं दोपहर का खाना बनाऊं, क्या तुम कपड़े टांग सकते हो?

examples.en: We hang out the washing on a line strung between two poles.
examples.hi: हम दो खंभों के बीच बंधी रस्सी पर कपड़े टांगते हैं।

examples.en: It's too humid today to hang out the washing outside.
examples.hi: आज बहुत उमस है, बाहर कपड़े टांगना ठीक नहीं होगा।

collocations: hang out the washing to dry
hang the washing on the line

common_mistake.wrong: I will hang the wash on the terrace.
common_mistake.right: I will hang out the washing on the terrace.
common_mistake.why: Learners drop 'out' and use 'wash' as a noun, but the natural fixed phrase in English is 'hang out the washing', where 'washing' (not 'wash') is the standard noun for clothes being laundered.

cloze.sentence: As soon as the cycle finishes, please ____ before it gets dark.

en_def: a shaped piece of wood, plastic, or metal used to hang clothes so they keep their shape
hi_def: कपड़े टांगने के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाला लकड़ी, प्लास्टिक या धातु का आकार वाला टुकड़ा
hi_nuance: The full term is 'clothes hanger' or 'coat hanger', but 'hanger' alone is completely standard and widely used; learners sometimes overcorrect and always add 'clothes' before it, which is unnecessary in casual speech.

examples.en: Put your shirt on a hanger so it doesn't crease.
examples.hi: अपनी शर्ट को हैंगर पर टांगो ताकि सिलवट न पड़े।

examples.en: We ran out of hangers in the wardrobe.
examples.hi: अलमारी में हैंगर खत्म हो गए हैं।

examples.en: The wire hanger bent under the weight of the coat.
examples.hi: कोट के वज़न से तार का हैंगर मुड़ गया।

examples.en: I bought a pack of wooden hangers for my new flat.
examples.hi: मैंने अपने नए फ्लैट के लिए लकड़ी के हैंगर का एक पैकेट खरीदा।

examples.en: Hang the wet shirt on a hanger near the fan.
examples.hi: गीली शर्ट को पंखे के पास हैंगर पर टांगो।

common_mistake.wrong: Put the shirt on stand.
common_mistake.right: Put the shirt on a hanger.
common_mistake.why: Learners sometimes use 'stand' generically for anything you hang things on, but the specific object used to hang clothes in a wardrobe is called a 'hanger', not a 'stand'.

cloze.sentence: There are no empty ____ left in the cupboard.

en_def: a small clip used to fasten wet clothes to a line so they don't fall or blow away
hi_def: गीले कपड़ों को रस्सी पर टांगकर रखने के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाली छोटी क्लिप
hi_nuance: British English says 'clothes peg' or just 'peg'; American English says 'clothespin'. In India both are understood, but if Balvant travels or reads American material, he should recognise 'clothespin' as the same object.

examples.en: Use a clothes peg so the shirt doesn't blow off the line.
examples.hi: क्लॉथ्स पेग का इस्तेमाल करो ताकि शर्ट रस्सी से न गिरे।

examples.en: We lost half our clothes pegs in the storm last week.
examples.hi: पिछले हफ्ते तूफान में हमारे आधे क्लॉथ्स पेग खो गए।

examples.en: She keeps the clothes pegs in a small plastic bag.
examples.hi: वह क्लॉथ्स पेग एक छोटे प्लास्टिक बैग में रखती है।

examples.en: The wooden clothes peg snapped when I pressed it.
examples.hi: दबाने पर लकड़ी का क्लॉथ्स पेग टूट गया।

examples.en: Buy some more clothes pegs; these are all cracked.
examples.hi: कुछ और क्लॉथ्स पेग खरीद लो; ये सब टूटे हुए हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I use clip to hang my clothes on the line.
common_mistake.right: I use a clothes peg to hang my clothes on the line.
common_mistake.why: 'Clip' is a generic English word for any fastening device, but the specific object for holding laundry on a line has its own name, 'clothes peg' (British) or 'clothespin' (American).

cloze.sentence: Grab a ____ from the bag and fix the towel to the line.

en_def: to bend clean, dry clothes neatly so they take up less space and stay tidy
hi_def: साफ, सूखे कपड़ों को करीने से मोड़ना ताकि वे कम जगह लें और व्यवस्थित रहें
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'set the clothes' or 'arrange the clothes' from Hindi habits, but the specific English verb for this action is 'fold', as in 'fold the clothes' or 'fold the laundry'. Note 'cloth' (singular, uncountable meaning fabric) versus 'clothes' (plural, meaning garments) is a very common confusion here.

examples.en: Can you help me fold the clothes from the basket?
examples.hi: क्या तुम टोकरी से कपड़े मोड़ने में मेरी मदद कर सकते हो?

examples.en: I like to fold the clothes as soon as they're dry.
examples.hi: मुझे कपड़े सूखते ही मोड़ना पसंद है।

examples.en: He folded the clothes neatly and put them in the cupboard.
examples.hi: उसने कपड़े करीने से मोड़कर अलमारी में रख दिए।

examples.en: It takes ten minutes to fold the clothes every evening.
examples.hi: हर शाम कपड़े मोड़ने में दस मिनट लगते हैं।

examples.en: Don't just throw the clothes on the bed; fold them properly.
examples.hi: कपड़ों को बिस्तर पर यूं ही मत फेंको; उन्हें ठीक से मोड़ो।

common_mistake.wrong: Please set the cloths in the cupboard.
common_mistake.right: Please fold the clothes and put them in the cupboard.
common_mistake.why: Two errors combine here: 'cloths' (pieces of fabric) is wrongly used instead of 'clothes' (garments), and 'set' is used instead of the correct verb 'fold' for arranging garments neatly.

cloze.sentence: After they dry, please ____ and put them in the drawer.

en_def: to clean clothes using chemical solvents instead of water, usually for delicate fabrics like wool or silk
hi_def: पानी की बजाय रासायनिक विलायकों से कपड़े साफ करना, आमतौर पर ऊन या रेशम जैसे नाज़ुक कपड़ों के लिए
hi_nuance: In India, 'dry clean' is often shortened in speech to just 'dry cleaning ke liye de do' and learners sometimes confuse it with simply 'drying' clothes; it actually means a special chemical washing process, not just drying wet clothes.

examples.en: This silk saree needs to be dry cleaned, not washed at home.
examples.hi: इस रेशमी साड़ी को घर पर नहीं, ड्राई क्लीन करवाना पड़ेगा।

examples.en: I always dry clean my woollen coat before winter.
examples.hi: मैं सर्दियों से पहले हमेशा अपना ऊनी कोट ड्राई क्लीन करवाता हूँ।

examples.en: The label says 'dry clean only' on this jacket.
examples.hi: इस जैकेट पर लेबल में लिखा है 'केवल ड्राई क्लीन'।

examples.en: Dry cleaning is more expensive than regular washing.
examples.hi: ड्राई क्लीनिंग सामान्य धुलाई से ज़्यादा महंगी होती है।

examples.en: She got the wedding lehenga dry cleaned after the function.
examples.hi: उसने फंक्शन के बाद शादी की लहंगे को ड्राई क्लीन करवाया।

common_mistake.wrong: I will dry my suit at the shop.
common_mistake.right: I will get my suit dry cleaned at the shop.
common_mistake.why: Learners confuse 'dry clean' (a chemical cleaning process) with simply 'drying' something; you don't 'dry' a suit at a shop, you get it 'dry cleaned', and note the passive construction 'get something dry cleaned' is the natural way to say this.

cloze.sentence: This wool blazer says '____ only' on the tag.

en_def: a shop where clothes are professionally cleaned using chemical solvents
hi_def: वह दुकान जहाँ रासायनिक विलायकों से पेशेवर तरीके से कपड़े साफ किए जाते हैं
hi_nuance: Note the apostrophe-s, like 'the doctor's' or 'the baker's' — 'dry cleaner's' technically means 'the dry cleaner's shop', a pattern common in British English that Indian learners often miss, simply saying 'dry cleaner' for the shop itself, which is also acceptable in casual speech.

examples.en: I need to drop this jacket at the dry cleaner's.
examples.hi: मुझे यह जैकेट ड्राई क्लीनर के यहाँ छोड़नी है।

examples.en: The dry cleaner's near my house is closed on Sundays.
examples.hi: मेरे घर के पास का ड्राई क्लीनर रविवार को बंद रहता है।

examples.en: Can you pick up my suit from the dry cleaner's on your way home?
examples.hi: क्या तुम घर आते समय मेरा सूट ड्राई क्लीनर से ले आ सकते हो?

examples.en: The dry cleaner's charges extra for same-day service.
examples.hi: ड्राई क्लीनर उसी दिन की सेवा के लिए अतिरिक्त शुल्क लेता है।

examples.en: I forgot my receipt from the dry cleaner's.
examples.hi: मैं ड्राई क्लीनर की रसीद भूल गया।

collocations: drop off at the dry cleaner's
pick up from the dry cleaner's

common_mistake.wrong: I gave my coat to dry cleaner shop.
common_mistake.right: I dropped my coat off at the dry cleaner's.
common_mistake.why: Learners add 'shop' redundantly after 'dry cleaner', but English already implies the shop with the possessive form 'dry cleaner's', similar to 'the butcher's' meaning the butcher's shop.

cloze.sentence: I'll collect the blazer from the ____ this evening.

en_def: a person whose job is making, repairing, or adjusting clothes, especially suits; or to adjust clothes to fit
hi_def: कपड़े बनाने, ठीक करने या फिट करने वाला व्यक्ति; या कपड़ों को नाप के अनुसार ठीक करना
hi_nuance: In India, 'tailor' generally covers all custom clothes-making (shirts, trousers, blouses), while in Britain and America a 'tailor' more specifically suggests suits and formal wear, with a 'seamstress' or 'dressmaker' more common for other garments; this distinction rarely matters in daily Indian usage.

examples.en: I need to take these trousers to the tailor.
examples.hi: मुझे यह पैंट दर्ज़ी के पास ले जानी है।

examples.en: The tailor took my measurements for a new suit.
examples.hi: दर्ज़ी ने नए सूट के लिए मेरा नाप लिया।

examples.en: My local tailor can turn around a shirt in two days.
examples.hi: मेरा स्थानीय दर्ज़ी दो दिन में शर्ट बना देता है।

examples.en: She learned tailoring from her mother.
examples.hi: उसने अपनी माँ से सिलाई सीखी।

examples.en: This suit was tailored specifically for the wedding.
examples.hi: यह सूट खासतौर पर शादी के लिए सिलवाया गया था।

common_mistake.wrong: I gave my shirt to master for stitching.
common_mistake.right: I gave my shirt to the tailor for stitching.
common_mistake.why: 'Master' (from Hindi 'master ji', a common respectful term for a tailor) is a direct translation that doesn't work in English; the standard English word for this profession is 'tailor'.

cloze.sentence: I need to visit the ____ to get this shirt taken in at the waist.

en_def: a single loop of thread made by sewing, or the act of sewing cloth together
hi_def: सिलाई में धागे का एक फंदा, या कपड़े को सुई-धागे से जोड़ने की क्रिया
hi_nuance: In Indian English, 'stitch' is used broadly for any tailoring job — 'I need to stitch a blouse' — which is understood but sometimes British/American speakers would more naturally say 'sew' or 'have something made'; both 'stitch' and 'sew' are correct, but 'stitch' emphasises the actual needlework.

examples.en: The seam came loose; a few stitches have come undone.
examples.hi: सीम ढीली हो गई है; कुछ टांके खुल गए हैं।

examples.en: Can you stitch this button back on for me?
examples.hi: क्या तुम मेरे लिए यह बटन फिर से सिल सकते हो?

examples.en: The tailor stitched a beautiful blouse for the wedding.
examples.hi: दर्ज़ी ने शादी के लिए एक सुंदर ब्लाउज सिला।

examples.en: I need to get this torn pocket stitched.
examples.hi: मुझे यह फटी हुई जेब सिलवानी है।

examples.en: Her hand-stitched embroidery took weeks to finish.
examples.hi: उसकी हाथ से सिली गई कढ़ाई पूरी होने में हफ्तों लगे।

common_mistake.wrong: I need to sew my finger, it's bleeding.
common_mistake.right: I need to get my finger stitched, it's bleeding.
common_mistake.why: This is a false-friend mix-up: 'sew' only applies to cloth with needle and thread; for a medical wound closed with thread, English uses 'stitch' or 'get stitches', not 'sew'.

cloze.sentence: The hem has come loose; can you ____ it back up?

en_def: to make small changes to a piece of clothing so that it fits better
hi_def: किसी कपड़े में छोटे बदलाव करना ताकि वह बेहतर फिट हो
hi_nuance: Indian English speakers often say 'I want to alter my pant' using 'pant' as singular for a single pair of trousers, whereas standard British/American usage keeps 'trousers' plural even for one item, saying 'alter my trousers' or 'alter these trousers'.

examples.en: I need to alter this shirt; the sleeves are too long.
examples.hi: मुझे यह शर्ट ठीक करवानी है; आस्तीनें बहुत लंबी हैं।

examples.en: The tailor altered the waist of the trousers for me.
examples.hi: दर्ज़ी ने मेरे लिए पैंट की कमर ठीक कर दी।

examples.en: Can this dress be altered to fit smaller?
examples.hi: क्या इस ड्रेस को छोटा करने के लिए ठीक किया जा सकता है?

examples.en: It costs extra to alter a suit after buying it off the rack.
examples.hi: रेडीमेड सूट खरीदने के बाद उसे ठीक करवाने में अतिरिक्त पैसे लगते हैं।

examples.en: She had the blazer altered before the interview.
examples.hi: उसने इंटरव्यू से पहले ब्लेज़र ठीक करवाया था।

common_mistake.wrong: I want to alter my pant at the waist.
common_mistake.right: I want to alter my trousers at the waist.
common_mistake.why: Hindi and casual Indian English treat 'pant' as singular for one garment, but standard English always uses the plural 'trousers' (or 'pants' in American English) even for a single pair.

cloze.sentence: These trousers are loose; can the tailor ____ them at the waist?

en_def: the folded and sewn edge of a piece of cloth, especially at the bottom of a garment; or to sew such an edge
hi_def: कपड़े का मुड़ा हुआ और सिला हुआ किनारा, खासकर कपड़े के निचले हिस्से में; या ऐसा किनारा सिलना
hi_nuance: Learners often just say 'the bottom of the pant' instead of the specific tailoring term 'hem'; knowing this word is useful when telling a tailor exactly what needs fixing, e.g. 'the hem has come undone' rather than a vague description.

examples.en: The hem of my trousers has come undone.
examples.hi: मेरी पैंट का हेम खुल गया है।

examples.en: Ask the tailor to take up the hem by two inches.
examples.hi: दर्ज़ी से हेम को दो इंच ऊपर करने को कहो।

examples.en: She hemmed the curtains herself instead of calling a tailor.
examples.hi: उसने खुद ही पर्दों का हेम सिल लिया, दर्ज़ी को नहीं बुलाया।

examples.en: The dress needs a new hem after the alteration.
examples.hi: अल्टरेशन के बाद ड्रेस को नया हेम चाहिए।

examples.en: A crooked hem makes the trousers look uneven.
examples.hi: टेढ़ा हेम पैंट को असमान दिखाता है।

common_mistake.wrong: The bottom of my pant is torn, please fix it.
common_mistake.right: The hem of my trousers has come undone, please fix it.
common_mistake.why: Describing the garment part vaguely as 'bottom of the pant' works but sounds unnatural to a tailor or shop assistant in English; the precise tailoring term is 'hem', which every tailor recognises immediately.

cloze.sentence: The trousers are too long; ask the tailor to take up the ____.

en_def: a small disc used to fasten clothing by passing it through a buttonhole; or to fasten clothing this way
hi_def: कपड़ों को बंद करने के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाला छोटा गोल टुकड़ा जो बटनहोल में से गुज़ारा जाता है; या इस तरह कपड़ा बंद करना
hi_nuance: In casual Indian English, 'button up' is sometimes reversed to 'button down', but 'button-down' is actually a specific style name (a shirt with buttons on the collar), not a general instruction. Use 'button up your shirt' for the everyday action of fastening buttons.

examples.en: One of the buttons on my shirt has come off.
examples.hi: मेरी शर्ट का एक बटन टूट गया है।

examples.en: Please button up your coat, it's cold outside.
examples.hi: कृपया अपना कोट बटन बंद करो, बाहर ठंड है।

examples.en: The top button of his collar was open.
examples.hi: उसके कॉलर का ऊपरी बटन खुला हुआ था।

examples.en: Can you sew this button back on for me?
examples.hi: क्या तुम मेरे लिए यह बटन फिर से सिल सकते हो?

examples.en: She struggled to button the tight cuffs.
examples.hi: उसे तंग कफ के बटन लगाने में मुश्किल हुई।

common_mistake.wrong: Button down your shirt before the meeting.
common_mistake.right: Button up your shirt before the meeting.
common_mistake.why: 'Button-down' is a specific style term for a shirt with buttoned collar points, not an instruction to fasten buttons; the everyday phrasal verb for closing buttons is 'button up'.

cloze.sentence: Wait, one of your shirt ____ has come undone.

en_def: a fastener with two rows of teeth pulled together by a sliding tab; or to close/open something using it
hi_def: दो पंक्तियों के दांतों वाला एक फास्टनर जिसे स्लाइडर से खींचकर बंद या खोला जाता है; या इसका इस्तेमाल करना
hi_nuance: British English says 'zip'; American English says 'zipper' for the noun, though 'zip up' as a verb is common in both. Indian English mostly follows British usage and says 'zip', so learners travelling to the US should recognise 'zipper' as the same thing.

examples.en: The zip on my jacket is stuck.
examples.hi: मेरी जैकेट की ज़िप फंस गई है।

examples.en: Zip up your bag before we leave.
examples.hi: जाने से पहले अपना बैग ज़िप करो।

examples.en: Her zip broke right before the interview.
examples.hi: इंटरव्यू से ठीक पहले उसकी ज़िप टूट गई।

examples.en: Can you help me zip up the back of this dress?
examples.hi: क्या तुम मुझे इस ड्रेस की पीछे की ज़िप लगाने में मदद कर सकते हो?

examples.en: The tailor replaced the broken zip in an hour.
examples.hi: दर्ज़ी ने एक घंटे में टूटी ज़िप बदल दी।

common_mistake.wrong: My jacket's zipper is very smooth in America but not here.
common_mistake.right: My jacket's zip is smooth, unlike a lot of the ones I've used here.
common_mistake.why: This isn't wrong exactly, but learners should know that Americans call it a 'zipper' while British and Indian English typically say 'zip' for the same fastener — mixing the two is fine but worth knowing which is more natural where.

cloze.sentence: Can you help me pull up the ____ at the back of this dress?

en_def: the measurements of a piece of clothing that determine whether it fits a particular body
hi_def: किसी कपड़े का माप जो यह तय करता है कि वह किसी विशेष शरीर पर फिट होगा या नहीं
hi_nuance: Indian shoppers often ask 'what number do you wear' translating from Hindi 'kaunsa number', but standard English asks 'what size are you' or 'what size do you take'. Also note that clothing size numbers differ between Indian, UK, US, and EU systems, so checking a size chart is often necessary while travelling.

examples.en: What size do you take in shirts?
examples.hi: तुम शर्ट में कौनसा साइज़ लेते हो?

examples.en: This size is too small; do you have a larger one?
examples.hi: यह साइज़ बहुत छोटा है; क्या इससे बड़ा है?

examples.en: Indian sizes are different from UK and US sizes.
examples.hi: भारतीय साइज़ यूके और यूएस साइज़ से अलग होते हैं।

examples.en: I usually wear a medium size in T-shirts.
examples.hi: मैं आमतौर पर टी-शर्ट में मीडियम साइज़ पहनता हूँ।

examples.en: Check the size chart before ordering online.
examples.hi: ऑनलाइन ऑर्डर करने से पहले साइज़ चार्ट देख लो।

common_mistake.wrong: What number do you wear in shirts?
common_mistake.right: What size do you take in shirts?
common_mistake.why: Hindi speakers often say 'number' (from asking shoe or clothing 'number') where standard English requires 'size'; 'number' sounds odd or old-fashioned to native English speakers for clothing.

cloze.sentence: I always order one ____ larger because this brand runs small.

en_def: is the right size and shape for someone's body
hi_def: किसी के शरीर के लिए सही आकार और माप का होना
hi_nuance: Learners frequently confuse 'fits' with 'suits' — 'this shirt fits me' is about size, while 'this colour suits me' is about how it looks on you. Mixing these up ('this colour fits me') is one of the most common Indian English mistakes with clothing vocabulary.

examples.en: This jacket fits me perfectly.
examples.hi: यह जैकेट मुझे बिल्कुल सही फिट होती है।

examples.en: These trousers don't fit anymore; I've put on weight.
examples.hi: यह पैंट अब फिट नहीं होती; मेरा वज़न बढ़ गया है।

examples.en: Does this dress fit you, or is it too tight?
examples.hi: क्या यह ड्रेस तुम्हें फिट होती है, या बहुत तंग है?

examples.en: The shoes fit well once I wore them for a day.
examples.hi: एक दिन पहनने के बाद जूते अच्छे से फिट हो गए।

examples.en: It fits at the shoulders but the sleeves are too long.
examples.hi: यह कंधों पर फिट होती है पर आस्तीनें बहुत लंबी हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: This blue colour fits me very well.
common_mistake.right: This blue colour suits me very well.
common_mistake.why: 'Fits' is about the correct size of a garment, while 'suits' is about how a colour or style looks on a person; Hindi doesn't distinguish these two ideas as clearly, so learners mix up 'fit' and 'suit'.

cloze.sentence: Try the next size up; this one doesn't ____ properly at the shoulders.

en_def: not fitting tightly; having extra space around the body
hi_def: ढीला; शरीर के आसपास अतिरिक्त जगह वाला, कसा हुआ नहीं
hi_nuance: A classic spelling and pronunciation confusion for Indian learners: 'loose' (ढीला, rhymes with 'goose') versus 'lose' (खोना, rhymes with 'choose'). Many learners write 'lose' when they mean 'loose' clothing, which is a spelling mistake that changes the meaning entirely.

examples.en: These trousers feel a bit loose around the waist.
examples.hi: यह पैंट कमर के आसपास थोड़ी ढीली लगती है।

examples.en: I prefer loose shirts in this hot weather.
examples.hi: इस गर्म मौसम में मुझे ढीली शर्ट पसंद है।

examples.en: The belt keeps my loose trousers in place.
examples.hi: बेल्ट मेरी ढीली पैंट को जगह पर रखती है।

examples.en: After losing weight, all my old clothes feel loose.
examples.hi: वज़न कम होने के बाद, मेरे सारे पुराने कपड़े ढीले लगते हैं।

examples.en: Ask the tailor to make the sleeves a bit looser.
examples.hi: दर्ज़ी से आस्तीनें थोड़ी ढीली करने को कहो।

common_mistake.wrong: These trousers are lose on me now.
common_mistake.right: These trousers are loose on me now.
common_mistake.why: 'Lose' (rhymes with 'choose', means to misplace or fail to win) and 'loose' (rhymes with 'goose', means not tight) are commonly confused in spelling by Indian learners; only 'loose' is correct for describing baggy clothing.

cloze.sentence: After the diet, my jeans feel really ____ around the waist.

en_def: fitting very closely to the body, with little or no extra space
hi_def: शरीर से बिल्कुल सटा हुआ, बिना किसी अतिरिक्त जगह के
hi_nuance: In Hindi, 'tight' is often borrowed directly and can also colloquially mean 'strict' or even 'drunk' in slang Hinglish; in standard English 'tight' for clothes only means closely fitting, so be careful not to carry over unrelated slang meanings into formal English contexts.

examples.en: This shirt feels too tight around the shoulders.
examples.hi: यह शर्ट कंधों के आसपास बहुत तंग लगती है।

examples.en: My jeans have become tight after the holidays.
examples.hi: छुट्टियों के बाद मेरी जींस तंग हो गई है।

examples.en: Don't buy shoes that are too tight; your feet will hurt.
examples.hi: ऐसे जूते मत खरीदो जो बहुत तंग हों; तुम्हारे पैर दुखेंगे।

examples.en: The collar was so tight I could barely breathe.
examples.hi: कॉलर इतना तंग था कि मैं मुश्किल से सांस ले पा रहा था।

examples.en: She likes her formal trousers slightly tight at the waist.
examples.hi: उसे अपनी फॉर्मल पैंट कमर पर थोड़ी तंग पसंद है।

common_mistake.wrong: My boss is very tight about deadlines.
common_mistake.right: My boss is very strict about deadlines.
common_mistake.why: 'Tight' in Indian English slang can mean 'strict' or 'stingy', borrowed loosely from Hindi/Hinglish usage, but in standard formal English 'tight' mainly describes physical fit (of clothes) or being short on time/money — for a strict person, use 'strict', not 'tight'.

cloze.sentence: These shoes are too ____; I need a half size bigger.

en_def: to put on a piece of clothing to see if it fits or how it looks before buying it
hi_def: खरीदने से पहले यह देखने के लिए कपड़ा पहनना कि वह फिट होता है या कैसा दिखता है
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'check the shirt' or 'wear and see' instead of the correct phrasal verb 'try on'; note the object can go in the middle or end: 'try on the shirt' or 'try the shirt on', but with a pronoun it must be 'try it on', never 'try on it'.

examples.en: Can I try on this shirt before I buy it?
examples.hi: क्या मैं खरीदने से पहले यह शर्ट पहन कर देख सकता हूँ?

examples.en: She tried on five pairs of trousers before choosing one.
examples.hi: उसने एक चुनने से पहले पांच पैंट पहन कर देखीं।

examples.en: Try it on first; the size might not suit you.
examples.hi: पहले पहन कर देखो; साइज़ तुम्हें सूट नहीं कर सकता।

examples.en: He tried on the jacket and decided it was too tight.
examples.hi: उसने जैकेट पहन कर देखी और तय किया कि यह बहुत तंग है।

examples.en: Is there a mirror where I can try on these shoes?
examples.hi: क्या यहाँ कोई शीशा है जहाँ मैं यह जूते पहन कर देख सकता हूँ?

common_mistake.wrong: Can I wear and see this shirt?
common_mistake.right: Can I try on this shirt?
common_mistake.why: 'Wear and see' is a literal translation from Hindi 'pehen kar dekhna'; the correct fixed English phrasal verb for testing clothes before buying is 'try on'.

cloze.sentence: Before buying, always ____ the shoes to check the size.

en_def: a small private room in a shop where customers can try on clothes
hi_def: किसी दुकान में एक छोटा निजी कमरा जहाँ ग्राहक कपड़े पहन कर देख सकते हैं
hi_nuance: British English commonly says 'fitting room' or 'changing room'; American English usually says 'fitting room' or 'dressing room'. In Indian shops, staff often just point and say 'trial room', which is a very common Indian English term understood locally but not standard outside India.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the fitting room?
examples.hi: माफ़ कीजिए, फिटिंग रूम कहाँ है?

examples.en: There was a long queue outside the fitting room.
examples.hi: फिटिंग रूम के बाहर लंबी कतार थी।

examples.en: You can try on up to three items in the fitting room.
examples.hi: आप फिटिंग रूम में तीन चीज़ों तक पहन कर देख सकते हैं।

examples.en: The fitting room mirror made the dress look different.
examples.hi: फिटिंग रूम के शीशे में ड्रेस अलग दिख रही थी।

examples.en: She spent twenty minutes in the fitting room deciding.
examples.hi: उसने फैसला करने में फिटिंग रूम में बीस मिनट बिताए।

common_mistake.wrong: Where is the trial room?
common_mistake.right: Where is the fitting room?
common_mistake.why: 'Trial room' is a common and widely understood Indian English term, but the standard British/American term used internationally is 'fitting room' (or 'changing room'), which is safer to use while travelling abroad.

cloze.sentence: Excuse me, could you tell me where the ____ is?

en_def: the part of a garment that covers the arm
hi_def: कपड़े का वह हिस्सा जो बांह को ढकता है
hi_nuance: Learners are usually fine with 'sleeve' itself, but often forget the phrase 'roll up your sleeves' (meaning to fold sleeves up the arm, also idiomatically meaning to prepare for hard work) — a useful idiom for workplace English.

examples.en: Roll up your sleeves before you start washing the dishes.
examples.hi: बर्तन धोने से पहले अपनी आस्तीनें ऊपर मोड़ो।

examples.en: The sleeve of my shirt got caught on the door handle.
examples.hi: मेरी शर्ट की आस्तीन दरवाज़े की कुंडी में फंस गई।

examples.en: This jacket has long sleeves, which is good for winter.
examples.hi: इस जैकेट की आस्तीनें लंबी हैं, जो सर्दियों के लिए अच्छा है।

examples.en: She prefers short-sleeved shirts in summer.
examples.hi: उसे गर्मियों में छोटी आस्तीन वाली शर्ट पसंद है।

examples.en: The tailor needs to shorten the sleeves by an inch.
examples.hi: दर्ज़ी को आस्तीनें एक इंच छोटी करनी होंगी।

common_mistake.wrong: This shirt has long hand.
common_mistake.right: This shirt has long sleeves.
common_mistake.why: 'Hand' is a literal translation from Hindi 'haath' used loosely for the arm-covering part of a shirt, but English has a specific word for this piece of clothing, 'sleeve', separate from the body part 'arm' or 'hand'.

cloze.sentence: Could you shorten the ____ of this jacket by two centimetres?

en_def: the part of a shirt or coat that fits around the neck
hi_def: शर्ट या कोट का वह हिस्सा जो गर्दन के चारों ओर फिट होता है
hi_nuance: This word is usually fine for learners, but note the idiom 'blue-collar' (manual labour jobs) versus 'white-collar' (office jobs), which is common in workplace and news English and useful for a security engineer discussing job types.

examples.en: Your collar is folded wrong; let me fix it.
examples.hi: तुम्हारा कॉलर गलत मुड़ा हुआ है; मुझे ठीक करने दो।

examples.en: He always wears his collar buttoned up at work.
examples.hi: वह हमेशा काम पर अपना कॉलर बटन बंद करके पहनता है।

examples.en: The starched collar felt stiff against my neck.
examples.hi: स्टार्च किया हुआ कॉलर मेरी गर्दन पर सख्त लग रहा था।

examples.en: This shirt has a slightly larger collar size.
examples.hi: इस शर्ट का कॉलर साइज़ थोड़ा बड़ा है।

examples.en: White-collar jobs usually require formal shirts with a collar.
examples.hi: व्हाइट-कॉलर नौकरियों में आमतौर पर कॉलर वाली फॉर्मल शर्ट चाहिए होती है।

common_mistake.wrong: My neck size for shirt is 16.
common_mistake.right: My collar size is 16.
common_mistake.why: Learners describe the measurement as 'neck size', which is technically what's being measured, but the standard retail and tailoring term for this shirt measurement in English is 'collar size'.

cloze.sentence: This shirt's ____ is too tight; I need a size bigger.

en_def: the end part of a sleeve, near the wrist, sometimes fastened with a button or cufflink
hi_def: आस्तीन का अंतिम हिस्सा, कलाई के पास, जिसे कभी-कभी बटन या कफलिंक से बंद किया जाता है
hi_nuance: This is a lower-frequency word for casual learners but useful for a security engineer who wears formal shirts to work; the phrase 'off the cuff' is also a common idiom meaning 'spoken without preparation', worth knowing for meetings.

examples.en: The cuff of his shirt was stained with ink.
examples.hi: उसकी शर्ट के कफ पर स्याही का दाग था।

examples.en: She fastened her cufflinks before the formal dinner.
examples.hi: उसने औपचारिक डिनर से पहले अपने कफलिंक लगाए।

examples.en: This shirt has a button cuff, not a French cuff.
examples.hi: इस शर्ट में बटन कफ है, फ्रेंच कफ नहीं।

examples.en: Roll the cuff up neatly if you're not wearing a jacket.
examples.hi: अगर जैकेट नहीं पहन रहे हो तो कफ को साफ-सुथरे तरीके से मोड़ो।

examples.en: He gave an answer completely off the cuff in the meeting.
examples.hi: उसने मीटिंग में बिना तैयारी के तुरंत जवाब दिया।

common_mistake.wrong: I need a shirt with french cuff for the wedding, do you have double cuff also.
common_mistake.right: I need a shirt with a French cuff for the wedding — do you also have one with a double cuff?
common_mistake.why: This isn't a major grammar error but a vocabulary gap: 'French cuff' and 'double cuff' actually refer to the same style (a cuff folded back and fastened with cufflinks), so asking for both as if they're different shows a common confusion among first-time formal shirt buyers.

cloze.sentence: He wore cufflinks with his shirt's French ____ for the formal dinner.

en_def: a layer of fabric attached to the inside of a garment to make it more comfortable or durable
hi_def: कपड़े के अंदर की तरफ लगा हुआ कपड़े का एक हिस्सा, जो पहनने में आराम या टिकाऊपन बढ़ाता है
hi_nuance: Many Indian learners know this word only from tailoring shops ('lining lagwani hai'), but forget it applies to jackets, coats, and bags too. A useful phrase to recognise is 'silver lining', an idiom meaning a hopeful aspect of a difficult situation, unrelated to clothing.

examples.en: The lining of my jacket has torn at the shoulder.
examples.hi: मेरी जैकेट की लाइनिंग कंधे पर फट गई है।

examples.en: Ask the tailor to add a silk lining to the blazer.
examples.hi: दर्ज़ी से ब्लेज़र में रेशमी लाइनिंग लगाने को कहो।

examples.en: This coat has a warm woollen lining for winter.
examples.hi: इस कोट में सर्दियों के लिए गर्म ऊनी लाइनिंग है।

examples.en: The lining feels rough against my skin.
examples.hi: लाइनिंग मेरी त्वचा पर खुरदुरी लगती है।

examples.en: Every cloud has a silver lining, my grandmother used to say.
examples.hi: हर बादल की एक रुपहली किनारी होती है, मेरी दादी कहा करती थीं।

common_mistake.wrong: The inside cloth of my jacket is torn.
common_mistake.right: The lining of my jacket is torn.
common_mistake.why: Describing it as 'inside cloth' is understandable but not the correct tailoring term; the specific English word for this inner fabric layer is 'lining', which any tailor will recognise instantly.

cloze.sentence: The tailor added a smooth silk ____ inside the blazer.

en_def: cloth or material made by weaving or knitting fibres together
hi_def: बुनकर या बुनाई करके बनाया गया कपड़ा या सामग्री
hi_nuance: Indian English often uses 'cloth' as a general word for both 'fabric' (the material) and 'clothes' (garments), which can confuse listeners. In standard English, 'fabric' is the material itself (like cotton or silk), 'cloth' is a piece of material (often for cleaning), and 'clothes' are the garments you wear.

examples.en: This fabric feels very soft and breathable.
examples.hi: यह कपड़ा बहुत मुलायम और हवादार लगता है।

examples.en: Cotton is a popular fabric for hot climates.
examples.hi: गर्म जलवायु के लिए सूती कपड़ा एक लोकप्रिय सामग्री है।

examples.en: The shop has a wide range of fabrics for suits.
examples.hi: दुकान में सूट के लिए कई तरह के कपड़े उपलब्ध हैं।

examples.en: Check the fabric care label before washing.
examples.hi: धोने से पहले कपड़े का केयर लेबल देख लो।

examples.en: This synthetic fabric doesn't crease easily.
examples.hi: यह सिंथेटिक कपड़ा आसानी से नहीं सिकुड़ता।

common_mistake.wrong: I bought new cloth for a shirt.
common_mistake.right: I bought new fabric for a shirt.
common_mistake.why: In this context 'cloth' loosely translates Hindi 'kapda', but standard English uses 'fabric' when talking about material bought by the metre for making a garment; 'cloth' more often refers to a small piece of material, like a duster or tablecloth.

cloze.sentence: This shirt is made from a lightweight cotton ____.

en_def: a soft, natural fibre from the cotton plant, used to make lightweight, breathable fabric
hi_def: कपास के पौधे से मिलने वाला मुलायम, प्राकृतिक रेशा, जिससे हल्का और हवादार कपड़ा बनाया जाता है
hi_nuance: This is a well-known word for Indian learners given India's cotton industry, but note the pronunciation trap: 'cotton' has a silent-ish 't' pattern in fast British speech (/ˈkɒʔn/ with a glottal stop), which can confuse learners expecting a clear 't' sound.

examples.en: Cotton shirts are more comfortable in humid weather.
examples.hi: उमस भरे मौसम में सूती शर्ट ज़्यादा आरामदायक होती हैं।

examples.en: This kurta is made of pure cotton.
examples.hi: यह कुर्ता शुद्ध सूती कपड़े से बना है।

examples.en: Cotton absorbs sweat better than polyester.
examples.hi: सूती कपड़ा पॉलिएस्टर से बेहतर पसीना सोखता है।

examples.en: I prefer cotton bedsheets in the summer.
examples.hi: मुझे गर्मियों में सूती चादरें पसंद हैं।

examples.en: This fabric is a cotton-polyester blend.
examples.hi: यह कपड़ा सूती और पॉलिएस्टर का मिश्रण है।

common_mistake.wrong: This shirt is full cotton.
common_mistake.right: This shirt is pure cotton / 100% cotton.
common_mistake.why: 'Full cotton' is a direct translation of the Hindi phrase 'poora cotton'; standard English uses 'pure cotton' or '100% cotton' to express that a fabric contains no other material mixed in.

cloze.sentence: In this heat, I always prefer a pure ____ shirt over synthetic ones.

en_def: a warm, soft natural fibre from sheep, used to make winter clothing
hi_def: भेड़ से मिलने वाला गर्म, मुलायम प्राकृतिक रेशा, जिससे सर्दियों के कपड़े बनाए जाते हैं
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes confuse the adjective form: the fabric noun is 'wool', but the adjective is 'woollen' (British spelling, with double 'l') or 'woolen' (American spelling) — e.g. 'a wool sweater' or 'a woollen sweater' are both correct, but 'a wool sweater' uses the noun as a modifier, which is very common too.

examples.en: This sweater is made of pure wool.
examples.hi: यह स्वेटर शुद्ध ऊन से बना है।

examples.en: Wool keeps you warm even when it's slightly damp.
examples.hi: थोड़ा गीला होने पर भी ऊन आपको गर्म रखती है।

examples.en: I need to buy a woollen shawl for the Delhi winter.
examples.hi: मुझे दिल्ली की सर्दी के लिए एक ऊनी शॉल खरीदनी है।

examples.en: Merino wool is softer than regular wool.
examples.hi: मेरिनो ऊन सामान्य ऊन से ज़्यादा मुलायम होती है।

examples.en: Wash woollen clothes gently by hand, not in the machine.
examples.hi: ऊनी कपड़ों को मशीन में नहीं, हाथ से हल्के से धोएं।

common_mistake.wrong: Don't put this wool sweater in washing machine, it will spoil.
common_mistake.right: Don't put this woollen sweater in the washing machine, it will get ruined.
common_mistake.why: Two small issues combine: using 'wool' where the adjective 'woollen' fits better before a noun in careful writing, and 'spoil' where native speakers would more naturally say 'get ruined' or 'get damaged' for clothing.

cloze.sentence: This ____ jumper keeps me warm even in Shimla's winter.

en_def: (British English) a knitted garment worn on the upper body, usually with long sleeves and no buttons; called a 'sweater' or 'pullover' in American English
hi_def: (ब्रिटिश अंग्रेज़ी) ऊपरी शरीर पर पहना जाने वाला बुना हुआ कपड़ा, आमतौर पर लंबी आस्तीन वाला और बिना बटन का
hi_nuance: This word has a genuinely confusing British-American split: in British English (and hence Indian English, which mostly follows British conventions), a 'jumper' is a knitted pullover/sweater. But in American English, 'jumper' means a sleeveless pinafore dress worn over a blouse, usually by girls or women — completely different garment. Always clarify context when speaking to Americans, or just say 'sweater' to be safe.

examples.en: I bought a warm woollen jumper for winter in London.
examples.hi: मैंने लंदन की सर्दी के लिए एक गर्म ऊनी जंपर खरीदा।

examples.en: She was wearing a blue jumper over her shirt.
examples.hi: वह अपनी शर्ट के ऊपर एक नीला जंपर पहने हुई थी।

examples.en: This jumper has a hole near the elbow.
examples.hi: इस जंपर में कोहनी के पास एक छेद है।

examples.en: Americans would call this jumper a 'sweater' instead.
examples.hi: अमेरिकी इस जंपर को 'स्वेटर' कहेंगे।

examples.en: He layered a jumper under his jacket for the cold flight.
examples.hi: उसने ठंडी उड़ान के लिए जैकेट के नीचे एक जंपर पहना।

common_mistake.wrong: My American colleague said her daughter wore a jumper to school, so I imagined a woolly sweater.
common_mistake.right: My American colleague said her daughter wore a jumper to school, meaning a sleeveless dress, not a woolly sweater.
common_mistake.why: This is exactly the British-American trap: in British/Indian English 'jumper' means a knitted sweater, but in American English it means a sleeveless pinafore dress — assuming the British meaning when an American speaker uses the word leads to real confusion.

cloze.sentence: It's freezing today, so I'm wearing a thick woollen ____ under my coat.

en_def: a casual sweatshirt or jacket with a hood attached, often with a front pocket
hi_def: एक आरामदायक स्वेटशर्ट या जैकेट जिसमें हुड लगा होता है, अक्सर आगे एक जेब के साथ
hi_nuance: This is a fairly recent, informal loanword now common among younger Indian English speakers; older speakers might not recognise it and say 'jacket with a cap' instead. It's informal register, fine for casual conversation but not for formal writing.

examples.en: He wore a grey hoodie to the gym.
examples.hi: वह जिम में एक ग्रे हुडी पहनकर गया।

examples.en: This hoodie has a big pocket in the front.
examples.hi: इस हुडी में आगे एक बड़ी जेब है।

examples.en: Pull up your hoodie, it's raining outside.
examples.hi: अपनी हुडी का हुड चढ़ा लो, बाहर बारिश हो रही है।

examples.en: She bought a black hoodie from the college merchandise stall.
examples.hi: उसने कॉलेज के मर्चेंडाइज स्टॉल से एक काली हुडी खरीदी।

examples.en: Hoodies are popular casual wear among students.
examples.hi: हुडी छात्रों में लोकप्रिय आरामदायक पहनावा है।

common_mistake.wrong: I am wearing jacket with cap on head part.
common_mistake.right: I am wearing a hoodie.
common_mistake.why: Describing the garment feature by feature ('jacket with a cap on the head part') is understandable but unnatural; English has a single common word for this specific style, 'hoodie'.

cloze.sentence: It's chilly this evening, so grab your ____ before we go out.

en_def: a knitted sweater or jacket that opens at the front, usually fastened with buttons or a zip
hi_def: एक बुना हुआ स्वेटर या जैकेट जो आगे से खुलता है, आमतौर पर बटन या ज़िप से बंद होता है
hi_nuance: Indian learners sometimes lump all knitted upper-body garments together as 'sweater', missing the specific distinction that a 'cardigan' opens fully down the front (like a shirt), while a 'jumper'/'sweater' is pulled over the head with no front opening.

examples.en: She wore a beige cardigan over her dress to the office.
examples.hi: उसने ऑफिस में अपनी ड्रेस के ऊपर एक बेज कार्डिगन पहना।

examples.en: This cardigan has wooden buttons down the front.
examples.hi: इस कार्डिगन में आगे लकड़ी के बटन लगे हैं।

examples.en: Grandmother knitted a cardigan for the baby.
examples.hi: दादी ने बच्चे के लिए एक कार्डिगन बुना।

examples.en: A cardigan is easier to put on than a pullover.
examples.hi: पुलओवर के मुकाबले कार्डिगन पहनना आसान होता है।

examples.en: He kept a cardigan on his chair for the air-conditioned office.
examples.hi: उसने एयर-कंडीशन्ड ऑफिस के लिए अपनी कुर्सी पर एक कार्डिगन रखा।

common_mistake.wrong: I bought a new sweater that opens in front with buttons.
common_mistake.right: I bought a new cardigan.
common_mistake.why: Describing the garment's features works but is unnecessary; English already has a specific single word, 'cardigan', for a front-opening knitted sweater, distinct from a pullover-style 'jumper' or 'sweater'.

cloze.sentence: She buttoned up her ____ because the office air conditioning was too cold.

en_def: clothing worn underneath outer clothes, close to the skin, such as vests and underwear
hi_def: बाहरी कपड़ों के नीचे, त्वचा के करीब पहने जाने वाले कपड़े, जैसे बनियान और अंडरगारमेंट्स
hi_nuance: 'Innerwear' is a very common Indian English retail term (used on shop signs and product packaging) but is less common in British or American everyday speech, where 'underwear' is the standard word; 'innerwear' is understood in India but may sound unusual or overly formal to native speakers abroad.

examples.en: This shop has a good collection of cotton innerwear.
examples.hi: इस दुकान में सूती इनरवियर का अच्छा कलेक्शन है।

examples.en: I need to buy some new innerwear before the trip.
examples.hi: मुझे यात्रा से पहले कुछ नया इनरवियर खरीदना है।

examples.en: The advert was for a popular men's innerwear brand.
examples.hi: विज्ञापन एक लोकप्रिय पुरुषों के इनरवियर ब्रांड के लिए था।

examples.en: Always choose breathable innerwear in summer.
examples.hi: गर्मियों में हमेशा हवादार इनरवियर चुनें।

examples.en: She packed extra innerwear for the long train journey.
examples.hi: उसने लंबी ट्रेन यात्रा के लिए अतिरिक्त इनरवियर पैक किया।

common_mistake.wrong: I need to buy innerwear, said to a British colleague, who looked confused.
common_mistake.right: I need to buy some underwear, in case a British colleague isn't familiar with the term 'innerwear'.
common_mistake.why: 'Innerwear' is a distinctly Indian English retail term; native British or American speakers use 'underwear' almost exclusively, so while travelling or talking to foreign colleagues, 'underwear' is the safer, more universally understood word.

cloze.sentence: I need to pack some extra ____ for the week-long trip.

en_def: soft coverings for the feet, worn inside shoes
hi_def: पैरों के लिए मुलायम आवरण, जूतों के अंदर पहने जाते हैं
hi_nuance: This word is simple, but learners often say 'sock' in singular even when talking about a pair, since Hindi doesn't mark plurals the same way; remember 'socks' is almost always used in plural because you wear two.

examples.en: I can't find a matching pair of socks this morning.
examples.hi: आज सुबह मुझे मोज़ों की मिलती-जुलती जोड़ी नहीं मिल रही।

examples.en: These woollen socks keep my feet warm in winter.
examples.hi: यह ऊनी मोज़े सर्दियों में मेरे पैर गर्म रखते हैं।

examples.en: He always wears black socks with formal shoes.
examples.hi: वह हमेशा फॉर्मल जूतों के साथ काले मोज़े पहनता है।

examples.en: One of my socks has a hole in the toe.
examples.hi: मेरे एक मोज़े में पंजे की जगह छेद है।

examples.en: Please put your dirty socks in the wash basket.
examples.hi: कृपया अपने गंदे मोज़े वॉश बास्केट में डालो।

common_mistake.wrong: I lost one sock, now I have only sock left.
common_mistake.right: I lost one sock, now I only have one sock left.
common_mistake.why: The countable singular form is 'a sock' or 'one sock'; dropping the article entirely, as in 'only sock left', is a common error from Hindi's lack of articles — English requires 'a' or 'one' before a singular countable noun.

cloze.sentence: I can never find two matching ____ in the morning.

en_def: a thin cord used to fasten a shoe by threading it through holes and tying it
hi_def: एक पतली रस्सी जिसे जूते के छेदों में पिरोकर बांधा जाता है ताकि जूता कस सके
hi_nuance: British English says 'shoelace'; American English often shortens it to just 'lace' or says 'shoestring' in some contexts (as in the idiom 'on a shoestring budget', meaning with very little money) — a useful idiom to recognise in business or travel contexts.

examples.en: My shoelace came undone while I was walking.
examples.hi: चलते समय मेरा जूते का फीता खुल गया।

examples.en: Can you tie my shoelace? My hands are full.
examples.hi: क्या तुम मेरा जूते का फीता बांध सकते हो? मेरे हाथ भरे हुए हैं।

examples.en: This shoelace is frayed at the end.
examples.hi: यह जूते का फीता आखिर में घिसा हुआ है।

examples.en: I need to replace the broken shoelace on my left shoe.
examples.hi: मुझे अपने बाएं जूते का टूटा हुआ फीता बदलना है।

examples.en: They started the whole business on a shoestring budget.
examples.hi: उन्होंने पूरा व्यवसाय बहुत कम पैसों में शुरू किया।

common_mistake.wrong: My shoe's string is open.
common_mistake.right: My shoelace has come undone.
common_mistake.why: 'String' is a generic word for any thin cord, but the specific English word for the cord used on shoes is 'shoelace' (or just 'lace'); also, in English we say a shoelace 'comes undone', not 'opens'.

cloze.sentence: Wait, your ____ has come undone — you'll trip over it.

en_def: the bottom surface of a shoe or foot that touches the ground
hi_def: जूते या पैर की निचली सतह जो ज़मीन को छूती है
hi_nuance: This word is a homophone of 'soul' (आत्मा), which can confuse learners in listening exercises; context almost always makes the meaning clear, but it's worth knowing the spelling difference explicitly since they sound identical.

examples.en: The sole of my shoe has worn thin.
examples.hi: मेरे जूते का सोल पतला घिस गया है।

examples.en: Rubber soles give better grip on wet floors.
examples.hi: रबर के सोल गीले फर्श पर बेहतर पकड़ देते हैं।

examples.en: The cobbler replaced the cracked sole for a small fee.
examples.hi: मोची ने थोड़े से पैसे में टूटा हुआ सोल बदल दिया।

examples.en: These shoes have a leather sole, not rubber.
examples.hi: इन जूतों में चमड़े का सोल है, रबर का नहीं।

examples.en: My sole came apart from the upper after years of use.
examples.hi: सालों इस्तेमाल के बाद मेरा सोल ऊपरी हिस्से से अलग हो गया।

common_mistake.wrong: The sole of my shoe is gone from my sole.
common_mistake.right: The sole has come off my shoe.
common_mistake.why: This exact sentence shows the classic homophone trap between 'sole' (shoe bottom) and 'soul' (spirit); a careful learner should double-check spelling when writing, since the two words sound exactly alike but mean completely different things.

cloze.sentence: The ____ of these old shoes has almost completely worn away.

en_def: a person whose job is to repair shoes
hi_def: जूते ठीक करने वाला व्यक्ति
hi_nuance: In Indian English, the word 'cobbler' is used, but many people also simply say 'the shoe repair guy' or use the Hindi-derived word 'mochi' even in English conversation; 'cobbler' is the correct standard English term and is safe to use anywhere.

examples.en: I took my broken sandal to the cobbler near the station.
examples.hi: मैं अपनी टूटी हुई चप्पल स्टेशन के पास मोची के पास ले गया।

examples.en: The cobbler fixed the sole in just ten minutes.
examples.hi: मोची ने दस मिनट में ही सोल ठीक कर दिया।

examples.en: There used to be a cobbler sitting under that tree every day.
examples.hi: उस पेड़ के नीचे रोज़ एक मोची बैठा करता था।

examples.en: The cobbler polished my shoes until they looked new.
examples.hi: मोची ने मेरे जूते इतने चमकाए कि वे नए लगने लगे।

examples.en: I asked the cobbler to also stitch the torn strap.
examples.hi: मैंने मोची से फटी हुई पट्टी भी सिलने को कहा।

common_mistake.wrong: I gave my shoe to the shoe-man to repair.
common_mistake.right: I took my shoe to the cobbler to get it repaired.
common_mistake.why: 'Shoe-man' is not a real English word; it's a literal, made-up translation pattern. The correct standard English term for a shoe repair professional is 'cobbler'.

cloze.sentence: Take these worn-out sandals to the ____ near the market.

en_def: damaged or thin from long use, no longer in good condition; can also mean extremely tired
hi_def: लंबे इस्तेमाल से क्षतिग्रस्त या पतला, अब अच्छी हालत में नहीं; व्यक्ति के लिए बहुत थका हुआ भी
hi_nuance: This phrase has two separate meanings that learners often mix up: for objects, 'worn out' means damaged from use (like worn-out shoes); for people, 'worn out' means exhausted/very tired. Both are correct but context changes the meaning entirely — don't say 'my shoes are tired'.

examples.en: These shoes are completely worn out; I need a new pair.
examples.hi: यह जूते पूरी तरह घिस चुके हैं; मुझे नई जोड़ी चाहिए।

examples.en: My old jeans are worn out at the knees.
examples.hi: मेरी पुरानी जींस घुटनों पर घिस गई है।

examples.en: After the long flight, I felt completely worn out.
examples.hi: लंबी उड़ान के बाद, मुझे पूरी तरह थका हुआ महसूस हुआ।

examples.en: The carpet in the hallway looks worn out and needs replacing.
examples.hi: गलियारे का कालीन घिसा हुआ दिखता है और बदलने की ज़रूरत है।

examples.en: He was worn out after working two back-to-back shifts.
examples.hi: दो लगातार शिफ्ट काम करने के बाद वह पूरी तरह थक गया था।

common_mistake.wrong: My shoes are very tired, I need new ones.
common_mistake.right: My shoes are worn out, I need new ones.
common_mistake.why: 'Tired' describes a person's exhaustion, not the condition of an object; for damaged or overused objects like shoes or clothes, English uses 'worn out', not 'tired'.

cloze.sentence: These office shoes are completely ____ after two years of daily use.

en_def: the stage of a washing machine's programme that spins clothes very fast to remove excess water
hi_def: वॉशिंग मशीन के प्रोग्राम का वह चरण जिसमें अतिरिक्त पानी निकालने के लिए कपड़े बहुत तेज़ी से घुमाए जाते हैं
hi_nuance: This is a fairly technical laundry term that many learners don't know precisely, often just saying 'the machine is running' for the whole process; knowing 'spin cycle' specifically helps when reading washing machine manuals or troubleshooting with a repair technician.

examples.en: The washing machine is very loud during the spin cycle.
examples.hi: स्पिन साइकिल के दौरान वॉशिंग मशीन बहुत तेज़ आवाज़ करती है।

examples.en: Choose a slower spin cycle for delicate fabrics.
examples.hi: नाज़ुक कपड़ों के लिए धीमी स्पिन साइकिल चुनें।

examples.en: The clothes were still quite wet after the spin cycle.
examples.hi: स्पिन साइकिल के बाद भी कपड़े काफी गीले थे।

examples.en: This machine has a high-speed spin cycle option.
examples.hi: इस मशीन में तेज़ गति की स्पिन साइकिल का विकल्प है।

examples.en: Something is unbalanced; the machine shakes badly during the spin cycle.
examples.hi: कुछ असंतुलित है; स्पिन साइकिल के दौरान मशीन बहुत हिलती है।

common_mistake.wrong: The machine is doing round-round very fast.
common_mistake.right: The machine is on its spin cycle.
common_mistake.why: 'Round-round' is an informal Hinglish way of describing spinning motion; the correct technical English term for this specific stage of the washing process is 'spin cycle'.

cloze.sentence: Don't open the lid while the machine is on its ____; it's dangerous.

en_def: small bits of fluff or fibre that come off fabric, often collected during washing or drying
hi_def: कपड़े से निकलने वाले छोटे रोएं या रेशे के टुकड़े, जो अक्सर धोने या सुखाने के दौरान जमा होते हैं
hi_nuance: This word is rarely known precisely by Indian learners, who often just say 'fluff' or describe it vaguely as 'thread bits'; 'lint' is the standard word, especially useful when discussing washing machine or dryer filters that need regular cleaning.

examples.en: Clean the lint filter after every wash to keep the machine efficient.
examples.hi: मशीन को कुशल रखने के लिए हर धुलाई के बाद लिंट फिल्टर साफ करो।

examples.en: Dark clothes attract more visible lint than light ones.
examples.hi: गहरे रंग के कपड़े हल्के रंग के कपड़ों से ज़्यादा दिखने वाला लिंट खींचते हैं।

examples.en: There was a lot of lint stuck to my black sweater.
examples.hi: मेरे काले स्वेटर पर बहुत सारा लिंट चिपका हुआ था।

examples.en: Use a lint roller to remove fluff from your suit before the meeting.
examples.hi: मीटिंग से पहले सूट से रोएं हटाने के लिए लिंट रोलर इस्तेमाल करो।

examples.en: The dryer's lint trap was completely blocked.
examples.hi: ड्रायर का लिंट ट्रैप पूरी तरह बंद था।

common_mistake.wrong: There is a lot of thread pieces on my black suit.
common_mistake.right: There is a lot of lint on my black suit.
common_mistake.why: Describing it as 'thread pieces' is understandable but vague; the precise, standard English word for these small bits of fluff that stick to fabric is 'lint'.

cloze.sentence: Use a roller to remove the ____ from your dark trousers before the meeting.

en_def: to unfasten a button, opening the part of the garment it was closing
hi_def: बटन को खोलना, जिससे कपड़े का वह हिस्सा खुल जाए जो उसने बंद कर रखा था
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'open the button' translating directly from Hindi 'button khol do'; while understandable, the more natural and idiomatic English phrase is 'undo the button', especially in British English. 'Open the button' is not wrong exactly but sounds slightly foreign to native ears.

examples.en: Can you undo this button for me? My hands are wet.
examples.hi: क्या तुम मेरे लिए यह बटन खोल सकते हो? मेरे हाथ गीले हैं।

examples.en: He undid the top button of his shirt after the meeting.
examples.hi: मीटिंग के बाद उसने अपनी शर्ट का ऊपरी बटन खोल दिया।

examples.en: I couldn't undo the button on my cuff; it was too tight.
examples.hi: मैं अपने कफ का बटन नहीं खोल पाया; वह बहुत तंग था।

examples.en: She undid the buttons one by one before changing.
examples.hi: उसने कपड़े बदलने से पहले बटन एक-एक करके खोले।

examples.en: Undo the top button if the collar feels too tight.
examples.hi: अगर कॉलर बहुत तंग लगे तो ऊपरी बटन खोल दो।

common_mistake.wrong: Open the button of your shirt, it's too tight.
common_mistake.right: Undo the button on your shirt, it's too tight.
common_mistake.why: 'Open the button' is a direct translation from Hindi that native English speakers understand but find slightly unnatural; the idiomatic English phrase for unfastening a button is 'undo the button' or the single verb 'unbutton'.

cloze.sentence: It's getting warm in here; I might ____ my top button.

en_def: to push the loose ends of a shirt inside the waistband of trousers so it looks neat
hi_def: शर्ट के ढीले सिरों को पैंट की कमरबंद के अंदर खोंसना ताकि वह करीने से दिखे
hi_nuance: Indian office dress codes often require shirts to be tucked in, and learners sometimes say 'put in the shirt' or 'set the shirt inside' instead of the correct phrasal verb 'tuck in'; note 'tuck in' also has an unrelated meaning of eating food eagerly ('tuck in to your dinner'), so context matters.

examples.en: Tuck in your shirt before the client meeting.
examples.hi: क्लाइंट मीटिंग से पहले अपनी शर्ट अंदर खोंसो।

examples.en: He never tucks in his shirt on weekends.
examples.hi: वह वीकेंड पर कभी अपनी शर्ट अंदर नहीं खोंसता।

examples.en: The office dress code requires shirts to be tucked in.
examples.hi: ऑफिस के ड्रेस कोड में शर्ट अंदर खोंसनी ज़रूरी है।

examples.en: She tucked in her blouse neatly before the interview.
examples.hi: उसने इंटरव्यू से पहले अपनी ब्लाउज़ करीने से अंदर खोंसी।

examples.en: My shirt keeps coming untucked when I sit down.
examples.hi: जब मैं बैठता हूँ तो मेरी शर्ट बार-बार बाहर निकल आती है।

common_mistake.wrong: Put your shirt inside the pant for the interview.
common_mistake.right: Tuck your shirt in for the interview.
common_mistake.why: 'Put inside' is a literal word-for-word translation of the Hindi instruction; the natural, idiomatic English phrasal verb for this specific action is 'tuck in' (a shirt), not 'put inside'.

cloze.sentence: Remember to ____ your shirt before you walk into the interview room.

en_def: having a strong, hot taste because of chillies or spices
hi_def: मसालेदार या तीखा (जिसमें मिर्च-मसाले ज्यादा हों)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often say 'hot' to mean spicy, which confuses Americans, who use 'hot' mostly for temperature. In Indian English 'spicy' is used correctly, but be careful: 'hot food' can mean either freshly cooked/warm food or chilli-hot food depending on context.

examples.en: This curry is too spicy for my kids.
examples.hi: यह करी मेरे बच्चों के लिए बहुत मसालेदार है।

examples.en: I love spicy street food.
examples.hi: मुझे मसालेदार स्ट्रीट फूड बहुत पसंद है।

examples.en: Can you make it less spicy, please?
examples.hi: कृपया इसे कम मसालेदार बना दीजिए।

examples.en: He can't handle spicy chutney at all.
examples.hi: वह तीखी चटनी बिल्कुल बर्दाश्त नहीं कर पाता।

examples.en: The spicy smell of the biryani filled the kitchen.
examples.hi: बिरयानी की मसालेदार खुशबू पूरी रसोई में फैल गई।

common_mistake.wrong: This food is very hot, please give me some water.
common_mistake.right: This food is very spicy, please give me some water.
common_mistake.why: In Indian English 'hot' can mean temperature-hot, so when talking about chilli heat it is clearer to say 'spicy' to avoid ambiguity with an American or British listener.

cloze.sentence: Please make the curry less ____, my son can't eat chillies.

en_def: having very little flavour or taste; not spicy or interesting
hi_def: फीका, बेस्वाद (जिसमें मसाले या स्वाद कम हो)
hi_nuance: Many Hindi speakers say 'this has no taste' instead of the more natural single word 'bland' — a direct translation of 'isme koi taste nahi hai'. 'Bland' is the precise English word for under-seasoned or flavourless food.

examples.en: The hospital food was completely bland.
examples.hi: अस्पताल का खाना बिल्कुल फीका था।

examples.en: This dal tastes bland; add some salt.
examples.hi: यह दाल बेस्वाद लग रही है; थोड़ा नमक डालो।

examples.en: I find airline food quite bland.
examples.hi: मुझे हवाई जहाज का खाना काफी फीका लगता है।

examples.en: Without chillies, the dish felt bland to him.
examples.hi: मिर्च के बिना, उसे यह व्यंजन फीका लगा।

examples.en: She prefers bland food after her surgery.
examples.hi: सर्जरी के बाद उसे फीका खाना ही पसंद है।

common_mistake.wrong: This food has no taste at all.
common_mistake.right: This food is bland.
common_mistake.why: Instead of the literal translation 'has no taste', native speakers usually use the single adjective 'bland' to describe under-seasoned food.

cloze.sentence: Without any spices, the soup tasted rather ____.

en_def: having a sharp, acidic taste like lemon or unripe fruit or spoiled milk
hi_def: खट्टा (नींबू जैसा तीखा-अम्लीय स्वाद)
hi_nuance: Note the pronunciation difference between 'sour' /ˈsaʊər/ and 'sore' /sɔːr/ (meaning painful) — Hindi speakers sometimes mix these up because both can sound similar when spoken quickly. Also, 'sour' milk means spoiled milk, not just tangy-tasting milk.

examples.en: The raw mango has a sour taste.
examples.hi: कच्चे आम का स्वाद खट्टा होता है।

examples.en: This yogurt has gone sour; don't eat it.
examples.hi: यह दही खट्टा हो गया है; इसे मत खाओ।

examples.en: She loves sour candies more than sweet ones.
examples.hi: उसे मीठी टॉफी से ज्यादा खट्टी टॉफी पसंद है।

examples.en: Add a little lime to balance the sour flavour.
examples.hi: खट्टे स्वाद को संतुलित करने के लिए थोड़ा नींबू डालो।

examples.en: The milk smelled sour, so I threw it away.
examples.hi: दूध से खट्टी बदबू आ रही थी, इसलिए मैंने उसे फेंक दिया।

common_mistake.wrong: This curd is sore, don't eat it.
common_mistake.right: This curd is sour, don't eat it.
common_mistake.why: 'Sore' /sɔːr/ means painful (a sore throat); the word for a sharp, acidic taste or spoiled dairy is 'sour' /ˈsaʊər/ — the two are easily confused in speech.

cloze.sentence: Unripe tamarind has a very ____ taste.

en_def: to heat food again, usually food that was already cooked earlier
hi_def: दोबारा गरम करना (पहले से पके हुए खाने को)
hi_nuance: Indian households commonly say 'heat it up' or 'warm it up', both of which are fine, but 'reheat' is the precise word used on food packaging and in recipes for warming already-cooked food, especially in a microwave.

examples.en: Just reheat the rice in the microwave for two minutes.
examples.hi: बस चावल को माइक्रोवेव में दो मिनट के लिए दोबारा गरम कर लो।

examples.en: Don't reheat the same curry more than once.
examples.hi: एक ही करी को एक से ज्यादा बार दोबारा गरम मत करो।

examples.en: I reheated last night's dal for breakfast.
examples.hi: मैंने नाश्ते के लिए कल रात की दाल दोबारा गरम की।

examples.en: Can you reheat this paratha on the tawa?
examples.hi: क्या तुम इस पराठे को तवे पर दोबारा गरम कर सकते हो?

examples.en: Reheating pizza in an oven keeps it crispy.
examples.hi: ओवन में पिज्जा दोबारा गरम करने से वह कुरकुरा रहता है।

common_mistake.wrong: Please re-heat again the sabzi.
common_mistake.right: Please reheat the sabzi.
common_mistake.why: 'Reheat' already means 'heat again', so adding 'again' after it is redundant — a common pattern when translating Hindi phrases like 'दोबारा गरम करो फिर से'.

cloze.sentence: Let me ____ the leftover chicken curry for dinner.

en_def: food that remains uneaten after a meal and is often saved to eat later
hi_def: बचा हुआ खाना (जो पहले से पका हो और बाद में खाया जाए)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often say 'extra food' or 'remaining food' as a direct translation of 'बचा हुआ खाना', but the natural English word is 'leftovers', always used in plural form even for a small amount.

examples.en: We had leftovers from yesterday's dinner party.
examples.hi: हमारे पास कल की डिनर पार्टी का बचा हुआ खाना था।

examples.en: Don't throw away the leftovers, pack them for lunch.
examples.hi: बचे हुए खाने को मत फेंको, दोपहर के खाने के लिए पैक कर लो।

examples.en: She turned the leftovers into a tasty fried rice.
examples.hi: उसने बचे हुए खाने से स्वादिष्ट फ्राइड राइस बना दिया।

examples.en: The fridge is full of leftovers from the weekend.
examples.hi: फ्रिज सप्ताहांत के बचे हुए खाने से भरा हुआ है।

examples.en: I usually eat leftovers for breakfast the next day.
examples.hi: मैं आमतौर पर अगले दिन नाश्ते में बचा हुआ खाना खाता हूं।

common_mistake.wrong: Please pack the extra food for tomorrow.
common_mistake.right: Please pack the leftovers for tomorrow.
common_mistake.why: While 'extra food' is understandable, native English speakers use the specific noun 'leftovers' for food saved from an earlier meal.

cloze.sentence: There are enough ____ in the fridge for tomorrow's lunch.

en_def: no longer fresh, especially bread or snacks that have become hard or lost their taste
hi_def: बासी (जो ताजा न हो, खासकर ब्रेड या नमकीन जो पुराना पड़ गया हो)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often use 'rotten' or 'spoiled' for bread that has simply gone hard or dry, but English distinguishes 'stale' (dry, no longer fresh, still usually safe) from 'rotten' (decayed and unsafe to eat) — mixing these up can make food sound more dangerous than it is.

examples.en: This bread has gone stale; let's make toast with it.
examples.hi: यह ब्रेड बासी हो गई है; इससे टोस्ट बना लेते हैं।

examples.en: The biscuits tasted stale because the packet was open.
examples.hi: बिस्किट बासी लग रहे थे क्योंकि पैकेट खुला था।

examples.en: Stale rice makes excellent fried rice the next day.
examples.hi: बासी चावल से अगले दिन बढ़िया फ्राइड राइस बनता है।

examples.en: Don't serve stale chips to the guests.
examples.hi: मेहमानों को बासी चिप्स मत परोसो।

examples.en: The stale smell from the bakery box put me off.
examples.hi: बेकरी के डिब्बे से आ रही बासी गंध ने मेरा मन खराब कर दिया।

common_mistake.wrong: This bread is rotten, throw it away.
common_mistake.right: This bread is stale, we can toast it.
common_mistake.why: 'Rotten' implies decay and being unsafe to eat, while 'stale' just means dry and no longer fresh — stale bread can often still be used, for example toasted.

cloze.sentence: The samosas felt ____ because they were made yesterday.

en_def: decayed and spoiled, usually unsafe or unpleasant to eat
hi_def: सड़ा हुआ, खराब (जो खाने लायक न रह गया हो)
hi_nuance: In Hindi, 'खराब' covers everything from mildly off to fully decayed, so Hindi speakers sometimes call slightly overripe or stale food 'rotten', which sounds extreme in English. Reserve 'rotten' for food that has visibly decayed or gone bad, and use 'stale' or 'overripe' for milder cases.

examples.en: Throw away those rotten tomatoes at the bottom of the bag.
examples.hi: बैग के नीचे रखे उन सड़े टमाटरों को फेंक दो।

examples.en: The eggs smelled rotten when I cracked them.
examples.hi: अंडे तोड़ने पर सड़ी हुई बदबू आ रही थी।

examples.en: A rotten banana attracted fruit flies in the kitchen.
examples.hi: एक सड़े केले ने रसोई में फल-मक्खियां आकर्षित कर लीं।

examples.en: We found rotten vegetables at the back of the fridge.
examples.hi: हमें फ्रिज के पीछे सड़ी हुई सब्जियां मिलीं।

examples.en: Never eat food once it has gone rotten.
examples.hi: एक बार खाना सड़ जाए तो उसे कभी मत खाओ।

common_mistake.wrong: This mango is a little rotten, it's just too ripe.
common_mistake.right: This mango is a little overripe, it's still fine to eat.
common_mistake.why: 'Rotten' means decayed and inedible; an overripe but still edible fruit should be called 'overripe', not 'rotten', which is much stronger.

cloze.sentence: The onions in the sack had turned ____ and had to be thrown out.

en_def: not cooked, or in its natural, unprocessed state
hi_def: कच्चा (जो पका न हो)
hi_nuance: In Hindi, 'kaccha' is used loosely for raw food, unripe fruit, and even undercooked food, which causes Hindi speakers to say 'raw' when they actually mean 'undercooked' (partly cooked but not enough) or 'unripe' (fruit not ready to eat). English keeps these three ideas separate.

examples.en: Sushi is made with raw fish.
examples.hi: सुशी कच्ची मछली से बनाई जाती है।

examples.en: Don't eat raw chicken, it's dangerous.
examples.hi: कच्चा चिकन मत खाओ, यह खतरनाक है।

examples.en: She likes raw carrots in her salad.
examples.hi: उसे अपने सलाद में कच्ची गाजर पसंद है।

examples.en: The kitchen counter still had raw onions on it.
examples.hi: रसोई के काउंटर पर अभी भी कच्चे प्याज रखे थे।

examples.en: Vegans eat a lot of raw vegetables.
examples.hi: वीगन लोग बहुत सारी कच्ची सब्जियां खाते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: This chicken is still raw in the middle, we need to cook it a little more.
common_mistake.right: This chicken is still undercooked in the middle, we need to cook it a little more.
common_mistake.why: 'Raw' means completely uncooked, but food that has been partly cooked and just needs a bit more time is 'undercooked', not 'raw' — an important distinction when following a recipe.

cloze.sentence: Be careful, the fish inside this sushi roll is completely ____.

en_def: cooked for too long, so the food has become too soft, dry, or has lost its taste
hi_def: जरूरत से ज्यादा पका हुआ (जो खाना बहुत देर तक पकाया गया हो)
hi_nuance: Indian English learners sometimes write this as two words, 'over cooked' or 'over-cooked', but the standard spelling in modern usage is one word, 'overcooked', when used as an adjective before or after a noun.

examples.en: The pasta was overcooked and had turned mushy.
examples.hi: पास्ता जरूरत से ज्यादा पक गया था और नरम-मुलायम हो गया था।

examples.en: Overcooked vegetables lose most of their nutrients.
examples.hi: जरूरत से ज्यादा पकी सब्जियां अपने ज्यादातर पोषक तत्व खो देती हैं।

examples.en: My mother-in-law thinks the rice is overcooked.
examples.hi: मेरी सास को लगता है कि चावल ज्यादा पक गए हैं।

examples.en: Overcooked eggs turn rubbery and grey around the yolk.
examples.hi: ज्यादा पके अंडे रबड़ जैसे हो जाते हैं और जर्दी के आसपास धूसर रंग आ जाता है।

examples.en: The steak came back overcooked, so he sent it back.
examples.hi: स्टेक ज्यादा पका हुआ आया, इसलिए उसने उसे वापस भेज दिया।

common_mistake.wrong: The vegetables became over cooked because I forgot the timer.
common_mistake.right: The vegetables became overcooked because I forgot the timer.
