common_mistake.why: 'Overcooked' is written as a single word in standard English; splitting it into 'over cooked' is a common spelling mistake influenced by treating 'over' as a separate word.

cloze.sentence: The noodles turned soggy because they were left ____ on the stove.

en_def: not cooked enough, so the inside is still partly raw
hi_def: अधपका, कम पका हुआ (जो पूरी तरह से पका न हो)
hi_nuance: As with 'raw', Hindi speakers sometimes describe undercooked food simply as 'kaccha', which in English is more accurately 'undercooked' when food has started cooking but needs more time — 'raw' should be reserved for food not cooked at all.

examples.en: The potatoes were undercooked and still hard.
examples.hi: आलू अधपके थे और अभी भी सख्त थे।

examples.en: Eating undercooked eggs can cause food poisoning.
examples.hi: अधपके अंडे खाने से फूड पॉइजनिंग हो सकती है।

examples.en: He complained that the roti was undercooked and doughy.
examples.hi: उसने शिकायत की कि रोटी अधपकी और गीली-आटे जैसी थी।

examples.en: Check the chicken carefully to avoid serving it undercooked.
examples.hi: चिकन को ध्यान से जांचो ताकि वह अधपका परोसा न जाए।

examples.en: The rice was slightly undercooked, with a bit of crunch left.
examples.hi: चावल थोड़े अधपके थे, उनमें थोड़ी कुरकुराहट बाकी थी।

common_mistake.wrong: The dal is still kaccha, cook it more.
common_mistake.right: The dal is still undercooked, cook it more.
common_mistake.why: The Hindi word 'kaccha' is often used loosely for anything not fully done, but in English the specific word for partly-cooked food is 'undercooked'.

cloze.sentence: Send the steak back to the kitchen — it's ____ inside.

en_def: a set of instructions telling you how to prepare and cook a particular dish
hi_def: विधि, नुस्खा (किसी व्यंजन को बनाने के निर्देश)
hi_nuance: This word is often confused with 'receipt' /rɪˈsiːt/, the paper proof of payment, because the two words look similar in writing. A 'recipe' tells you how to cook something; a 'receipt' proves you paid for something.

examples.en: My grandmother's recipe for rajma is the best.
examples.hi: मेरी दादी की राजमा बनाने की विधि सबसे अच्छी है।

examples.en: Can you send me the recipe for that cake?
examples.hi: क्या तुम मुझे उस केक की रेसिपी भेज सकते हो?

examples.en: I follow this recipe exactly every single time.
examples.hi: मैं हर बार बिल्कुल इसी विधि का पालन करता हूं।

examples.en: She is trying a new recipe for dinner tonight.
examples.hi: वह आज रात के खाने के लिए एक नई रेसिपी आजमा रही है।

examples.en: This recipe needs half a cup of yogurt.
examples.hi: इस रेसिपी में आधा कप दही चाहिए।

common_mistake.wrong: Please give me the receipt for the chicken curry.
common_mistake.right: Please give me the recipe for the chicken curry.
common_mistake.why: 'Receipt' is proof of a purchase, while 'recipe' is the cooking instructions — the two words look similar and are commonly confused by Indian English learners.

cloze.sentence: This ____ for butter chicken has been in my family for years.

en_def: one of the items of food used to prepare a particular dish
hi_def: सामग्री (किसी व्यंजन को बनाने में इस्तेमाल होने वाली चीज)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers sometimes pronounce this word as 'in-gredi-ent' with a hard 'g' stress in the wrong place; the correct stress is on the second syllable, 'in-GRE-di-ent'. Also note the plural 'ingredients' is almost always used when listing what a dish needs.

examples.en: Garam masala is the main ingredient in this dish.
examples.hi: गरम मसाला इस व्यंजन की मुख्य सामग्री है।

examples.en: Check if we have all the ingredients before cooking.
examples.hi: खाना बनाने से पहले देख लो कि हमारे पास सारी सामग्री है या नहीं।

examples.en: Fresh ingredients make a huge difference to the taste.
examples.hi: ताजी सामग्री स्वाद में बहुत फर्क डालती है।

examples.en: This recipe only needs five simple ingredients.
examples.hi: इस रेसिपी में सिर्फ पांच आसान सामग्री चाहिए।

examples.en: He always reads the ingredient list on packaged food.
examples.hi: वह पैकेज्ड खाने पर हमेशा सामग्री की सूची पढ़ता है।

common_mistake.wrong: What all things do I need for this recipe?
common_mistake.right: What ingredients do I need for this recipe?
common_mistake.why: 'Things' is too general in this context; the specific English word for the food items used in cooking is 'ingredients'.

cloze.sentence: Flour, sugar, and eggs are the basic ____ for this cake.

en_def: to soak meat, fish, or vegetables in a mixture of spices, oil, or sauce before cooking, to add flavour
hi_def: मैरिनेट करना (मांस या सब्जी को पकाने से पहले मसाले-दही आदि में भिगोना)
hi_nuance: Home cooks in India often just say 'let it sit in masala' instead of using the specific English verb 'marinate'. Note the noun form is 'marinade' (the mixture itself), while 'marinate' is the verb — the two are easily confused.

examples.en: Marinate the chicken in yogurt and spices overnight.
examples.hi: चिकन को दही और मसालों में रातभर के लिए मैरिनेट करो।

examples.en: I always marinate the paneer for at least an hour.
examples.hi: मैं हमेशा पनीर को कम से कम एक घंटे के लिए मैरिनेट करता हूं।

examples.en: Marinated tofu tastes much better on the grill.
examples.hi: मैरिनेट किया हुआ टोफू ग्रिल पर कहीं बेहतर स्वाद देता है।

examples.en: Let the fish marinate in lemon juice and garlic.
examples.hi: मछली को नींबू के रस और लहसुन में मैरिनेट होने दो।

examples.en: She marinates the kebabs the night before the party.
examples.hi: वह पार्टी से एक रात पहले कबाब मैरिनेट कर लेती है।

common_mistake.wrong: Keep the chicken in marinate for two hours.
common_mistake.right: Keep the chicken to marinate for two hours, or leave it in the marinade for two hours.
common_mistake.why: 'Marinate' is the verb (an action), while 'marinade' is the noun (the mixture) — Hindi speakers often mix up the two forms.

cloze.sentence: For the best flavour, ____ the mutton in spices for at least four hours.

en_def: to cook a liquid or food gently in it, just below boiling point, with small bubbles
hi_def: धीमी आंच पर पकाना (उबाल से थोड़ा कम तापमान पर हल्के-हल्के बुलबुले बनते हुए पकाना)
hi_nuance: Hindi commonly uses 'उबालना' (to boil) for both a rolling boil and a gentle simmer, so Hindi speakers often say 'boil on low flame' where English would simply say 'simmer'. Recipes distinguish these two heat levels precisely.

examples.en: Let the gravy simmer on low heat for twenty minutes.
examples.hi: ग्रेवी को धीमी आंच पर बीस मिनट तक पकने दो।

examples.en: Simmer the dal until it becomes soft and thick.
examples.hi: दाल को तब तक धीमी आंच पर पकाओ जब तक वह नरम और गाढ़ी न हो जाए।

examples.en: She turned down the heat to let the sauce simmer.
examples.hi: उसने आंच धीमी कर दी ताकि सॉस धीरे-धीरे पके।

examples.en: Once it boils, reduce the heat and let it simmer.
examples.hi: एक बार उबाल आने पर आंच कम कर दो और उसे धीमे पकने दो।

examples.en: The soup needs to simmer for at least an hour.
examples.hi: सूप को कम से कम एक घंटे तक धीमी आंच पर पकना चाहिए।

common_mistake.wrong: Boil the curry on low flame for ten minutes.
common_mistake.right: Simmer the curry on low heat for ten minutes.
common_mistake.why: When cooking gently below a full boil, English uses the specific verb 'simmer' rather than 'boil on low flame', which sounds like a direct translation from Hindi.

cloze.sentence: Reduce the flame and let the sambar ____ for fifteen minutes.

en_def: to heat a liquid until it bubbles strongly, or to cook food in boiling water
hi_def: उबालना (पानी या तरल को गरम करके बुलबुले बनाना, या उबलते पानी में खाना पकाना)
hi_nuance: This common word is straightforward, but note that 'boiled' can also describe the noun form of food, as in 'boiled egg' or 'boiled potato' — Hindi speakers sometimes say 'boiled' after the noun instead, like 'egg boiled', which sounds unnatural.

examples.en: Boil the water before adding the tea leaves.
examples.hi: चाय की पत्ती डालने से पहले पानी उबालो।

examples.en: I boiled two eggs for breakfast this morning.
examples.hi: मैंने आज सुबह नाश्ते के लिए दो अंडे उबाले।

examples.en: The rice needs to boil for fifteen minutes.
examples.hi: चावल को पंद्रह मिनट तक उबलने की जरूरत है।

examples.en: She boiled the potatoes before mashing them.
examples.hi: उसने आलू मैश करने से पहले उन्हें उबाला।

examples.en: Watch the milk carefully so it doesn't boil over.
examples.hi: दूध पर ध्यान रखो ताकि वह उबलकर बाहर न गिरे।

common_mistake.wrong: Egg boiled is ready, you can eat now.
common_mistake.right: The boiled egg is ready, you can eat it now.
common_mistake.why: 'Boiled' should come before the noun as an adjective, 'boiled egg', not after it — placing the adjective after the noun is a common word-order mistake.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ some water for the tea.

en_def: to cook food in hot oil or fat, usually in a pan
hi_def: तलना या भूनना (गरम तेल में खाना पकाना)
hi_nuance: In everyday Hindi, 'फ्राई करना' or 'भूनना' is used loosely for almost any cooking in oil, so Indian English speakers often say 'fry' for actions that in English would be 'sauté' (lightly cook in a little oil) or 'roast'. Precision matters more in recipes than in daily conversation.

examples.en: Fry the onions until they turn golden brown.
examples.hi: प्याज को तब तक भूनो जब तक वह सुनहरे भूरे रंग की न हो जाए।

examples.en: She fried some pakoras for the evening snack.
examples.hi: उसने शाम के नाश्ते के लिए कुछ पकौड़े तले।

examples.en: Don't fry the fish for too long, it will dry out.
examples.hi: मछली को ज्यादा देर तक मत तलो, वह सूख जाएगी।

examples.en: We fried the potatoes in a little mustard oil.
examples.hi: हमने आलू को थोड़े सरसों के तेल में तला।

examples.en: Fry the spices briefly before adding the vegetables.
examples.hi: सब्जियां डालने से पहले मसालों को थोड़ी देर भूनो।

common_mistake.wrong: I will fry the vegetables in water.
common_mistake.right: I will boil/steam the vegetables in water.
common_mistake.why: 'Fry' specifically means cooking in hot oil, not water — using it with 'water' is a contradiction; use 'boil' or 'steam' for cooking in water.

cloze.sentence: She likes to ____ the paneer cubes before adding them to the gravy.

en_def: to cook food by completely submerging it in a large amount of hot oil
hi_def: डीप फ्राई करना (खाने को पूरी तरह तेल में डुबोकर तलना)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often just say 'fry' for both shallow frying and deep frying, since 'तलना' covers both. English distinguishes 'deep fry' (fully submerged in oil, like samosas or pakoras) from lighter frying or sautéing with just a little oil.

examples.en: We deep fry the samosas until they are crispy.
examples.hi: हम समोसे को कुरकुरा होने तक डीप फ्राई करते हैं।

examples.en: Deep frying uses a lot more oil than pan-frying.
examples.hi: डीप फ्राई करने में पैन-फ्राई करने से कहीं ज्यादा तेल लगता है।

examples.en: The chicken wings are deep fried in the restaurant kitchen.
examples.hi: रेस्तरां की रसोई में चिकन विंग्स को डीप फ्राई किया जाता है।

examples.en: He deep fries the puris until they puff up.
examples.hi: वह पूरियों को फूलने तक डीप फ्राई करता है।

examples.en: Make sure the oil is hot enough before you deep fry anything.
examples.hi: कुछ भी डीप फ्राई करने से पहले सुनिश्चित करो कि तेल पर्याप्त गरम है।

common_mistake.wrong: We deep fry the bhindi in a little oil.
common_mistake.right: We fry/sauté the bhindi in a little oil.
common_mistake.why: 'Deep fry' specifically means fully submerging food in oil; if only a little oil is used, the correct verb is simply 'fry' or 'sauté', not 'deep fry'.

cloze.sentence: For crispy pakoras, you need to ____ them in plenty of hot oil.

en_def: to cook small pieces of food quickly in a little hot oil while stirring constantly
hi_def: हिलाते हुए तेज आंच पर तलना (थोड़े तेल में खाने को लगातार हिलाते हुए जल्दी पकाना)
hi_nuance: This word comes from Chinese cooking style and is common on Indo-Chinese restaurant menus in India, such as 'stir-fried noodles'. Indian English speakers sometimes just say 'fry it fast' — 'stir-fry' is the precise single verb, often written with a hyphen.

examples.en: Stir-fry the vegetables on high heat for five minutes.
examples.hi: सब्जियों को तेज आंच पर हिलाते हुए पांच मिनट तक तलो।

examples.en: This Indo-Chinese place serves great stir-fried noodles.
examples.hi: यह इंडो-चाइनीज़ जगह बढ़िया स्टिर-फ्राई नूडल्स परोसती है।

examples.en: She stir-fries the paneer with capsicum and onion.
examples.hi: वह पनीर को शिमला मिर्च और प्याज के साथ स्टिर-फ्राई करती है।

examples.en: Keep stirring while you stir-fry, or it will burn.
examples.hi: स्टिर-फ्राई करते समय हिलाते रहो, वरना यह जल जाएगा।

examples.en: A wok is the best pan for stir-frying quickly.
examples.hi: जल्दी स्टिर-फ्राई करने के लिए वोक सबसे अच्छा बर्तन है।

common_mistake.wrong: Please fry mix the vegetables quickly.
common_mistake.right: Please stir-fry the vegetables quickly.
common_mistake.why: 'Fry mix' is not a standard English verb; the correct single word for quickly cooking small pieces of food while stirring is 'stir-fry'.

cloze.sentence: The Indo-Chinese chef will ____ the noodles with vegetables in a hot wok.

en_def: to rub food like cheese, carrots, or ginger against a rough tool to break it into small pieces
hi_def: कद्दूकस करना (पनीर, गाजर या अदरक आदि को छोटे टुकड़ों में तोड़ने के लिए घिसना)
hi_nuance: This word is a homophone of 'great' (excellent), which sometimes confuses learners in listening exercises. In the kitchen, we 'grate' ginger, garlic, cheese, or coconut using a grater; this is different from 'chop' or 'mince', which use a knife.

examples.en: Grate some fresh ginger into the tea.
examples.hi: चाय में थोड़ा ताजा अदरक कद्दूकस करके डालो।

examples.en: She grated the cheese for the pizza topping.
examples.hi: उसने पिज्जा टॉपिंग के लिए पनीर कद्दूकस किया।

examples.en: Grate the coconut finely for the chutney.
examples.hi: चटनी के लिए नारियल को बारीक कद्दूकस करो।

examples.en: He always grates garlic instead of chopping it.
examples.hi: वह लहसुन को काटने के बजाय हमेशा कद्दूकस करता है।

examples.en: I burnt my finger while grating the carrot.
examples.hi: गाजर कद्दूकस करते समय मेरी उंगली जल गई।

common_mistake.wrong: Please great some cheese for the pasta.
common_mistake.right: Please grate some cheese for the pasta.
common_mistake.why: 'Grate' (to shred food with a grater) and 'great' (excellent) are homophones with different spellings; only 'grate' is a cooking verb.

cloze.sentence: Use the small holes on the grater to ____ the ginger.

en_def: to cut food into pieces with a knife
hi_def: काटना, कतरना (चाकू से खाने को टुकड़ों में काटना)
hi_nuance: In casual Indian English, 'cut' is often used for every kind of cutting action — chopping, slicing, mincing, and dicing — because Hindi commonly uses 'काटना' for all of them. English cooking vocabulary is more specific: 'chop' means rough, medium-sized pieces, different from 'slice', 'dice', or 'mince'.

examples.en: Chop the onions finely before frying them.
examples.hi: प्याज तलने से पहले उन्हें बारीक काट लो।

examples.en: She chopped the coriander leaves for garnish.
examples.hi: उसने गार्निश के लिए धनिया पत्ती काटी।

examples.en: Can you chop the tomatoes into small pieces?
examples.hi: क्या तुम टमाटर को छोटे टुकड़ों में काट सकते हो?

examples.en: He chopped the vegetables while I heated the pan.
examples.hi: उसने सब्जियां काटीं जबकि मैंने पैन गरम किया।

examples.en: The recipe says to chop the garlic roughly.
examples.hi: रेसिपी में कहा गया है कि लहसुन को मोटा-मोटा काटो।

common_mistake.wrong: Cut the onions in small small pieces.
common_mistake.right: Chop the onions into small pieces.
common_mistake.why: The repeated word 'small small' is a Hindi-influenced pattern used for emphasis; standard English uses 'into small pieces' and prefers the specific verb 'chop' for this action rather than the general 'cut'.

cloze.sentence: Use a sharp knife to ____ the onions before frying.

en_def: to cut or grind meat, garlic, or ginger into very small pieces or a paste
hi_def: कीमा बनाना या बारीक काटना (मांस, लहसुन या अदरक को बहुत महीन काटना या पीसना)
hi_nuance: As a noun, 'mince' or 'minced meat' is exactly what Indian English calls 'keema', so ordering 'mutton keema' at a restaurant is the same as 'minced mutton' in standard English. As a verb, 'mince' garlic or ginger means chopping it much finer than a normal chop.

examples.en: Mince the garlic finely before adding it to the oil.
examples.hi: तेल में डालने से पहले लहसुन को बारीक काटो।

examples.en: This kebab recipe uses minced mutton.
examples.hi: इस कबाब रेसिपी में कीमा किया हुआ मटन इस्तेमाल होता है।

examples.en: She minced the ginger and garlic together in a food processor.
examples.hi: उसने अदरक और लहसुन को फूड प्रोसेसर में साथ में पीसा।

examples.en: You can buy minced chicken at the butcher's shop.
examples.hi: कसाई की दुकान पर तुम कीमा किया हुआ चिकन खरीद सकते हो।

examples.en: Mince the onion very finely for this sauce.
examples.hi: इस सॉस के लिए प्याज को बहुत बारीक काटो।

common_mistake.wrong: I want one plate keema, please make it less spicy.
common_mistake.right: I want a plate of minced mutton, please make it less spicy.
common_mistake.why: Keema translates directly to 'minced meat' in English; also note 'one plate keema' should be 'a plate of minced mutton', since English needs 'of' between the quantity and the food.

cloze.sentence: For kheema curry, first ____ the garlic and ginger into a fine paste.

en_def: to remove the outer skin of a fruit or vegetable
hi_def: छीलना (फल या सब्जी का छिलका उतारना)
hi_nuance: The same word 'peel' is both a verb (to peel a potato) and a noun (banana peel, the skin itself) — Hindi speakers sometimes use 'skin' for both, which is fine for the noun but sounds odd as a verb; 'skin the potato' is unusual, while 'peel the potato' is standard.

examples.en: Peel the potatoes before boiling them.
examples.hi: आलू उबालने से पहले उन्हें छील लो।

examples.en: She peeled the mango carefully with a knife.
examples.hi: उसने चाकू से आम को सावधानी से छीला।

examples.en: Don't throw away the potato peel, it can be composted.
examples.hi: आलू के छिलके मत फेंको, उन्हें खाद बनाया जा सकता है।

examples.en: He peeled the garlic cloves before crushing them.
examples.hi: उसने लहसुन की कलियों को कुचलने से पहले छीला।

examples.en: The banana peel was left on the kitchen counter.
examples.hi: केले का छिलका रसोई के काउंटर पर पड़ा रह गया।

common_mistake.wrong: Skin the potatoes before cutting them.
common_mistake.right: Peel the potatoes before cutting them.
common_mistake.why: The verb used for removing the outer layer of fruits and vegetables in cooking is 'peel', not 'skin' — 'skin' as a verb is mostly used for animals, not vegetables.

cloze.sentence: Remember to ____ the ginger before you grate it.

en_def: to decorate a dish with a small amount of food just before serving, to make it look or taste better
hi_def: गार्निश करना, सजाना (परोसने से पहले व्यंजन को थोड़ी सामग्री से सजाना)
hi_nuance: This word is often used only as a noun in Indian kitchens ('add some garnish'), but in English it is very commonly a verb too — 'garnish the dal with coriander' is more natural than 'put garnish of coriander on the dal'.

examples.en: Garnish the biryani with fried onions and mint leaves.
examples.hi: बिरयानी को तले हुए प्याज और पुदीने की पत्तियों से गार्निश करो।

examples.en: She garnished the soup with a swirl of cream.
examples.hi: उसने सूप को क्रीम की एक लकीर से गार्निश किया।

examples.en: Always garnish the dal with fresh coriander leaves.
examples.hi: दाल को हमेशा ताजी धनिया पत्ती से गार्निश करो।

examples.en: The chef garnished the plate with a lemon wedge.
examples.hi: शेफ ने प्लेट को नींबू के एक टुकड़े से गार्निश किया।

examples.en: Garnish with chopped nuts before serving the kheer.
examples.hi: खीर परोसने से पहले उसे कटे हुए मेवों से गार्निश करो।

common_mistake.wrong: Put garnish of coriander on top the curry.
common_mistake.right: Garnish the curry with coriander on top.
common_mistake.why: In English, 'garnish' works naturally as a verb — 'garnish the curry with coriander' — rather than as a noun phrase like 'put garnish of coriander'.

cloze.sentence: Don't forget to ____ the pasta with fresh basil leaves.

en_def: to add salt, spices, or herbs to food to improve its flavour
hi_def: स्वादानुसार नमक-मसाला डालना (खाने का स्वाद बढ़ाने के लिए)
hi_nuance: This is the same word as 'season' meaning a time of year (summer season), which can confuse learners who only know the weather meaning. 'Season to taste' is a very common recipe instruction meaning add salt and spices until it tastes right to you.

examples.en: Season the soup with salt and black pepper.
examples.hi: सूप में स्वादानुसार नमक और काली मिर्च डालो।

examples.en: Remember to season the meat well before grilling.
examples.hi: ग्रिल करने से पहले मांस में अच्छे से मसाला डालना याद रखो।

examples.en: The recipe says to season to taste at the end.
examples.hi: रेसिपी में कहा गया है कि आखिर में स्वादानुसार नमक-मसाला डालो।

examples.en: She seasoned the salad with lemon juice and salt.
examples.hi: उसने सलाद में नींबू का रस और नमक डाला।

examples.en: Don't over-season the curry with too much chilli.
examples.hi: करी में ज्यादा मिर्च डालकर उसे ओवर-सीजन मत करो।

common_mistake.wrong: Please season time this curry with more salt.
common_mistake.right: Please season this curry with more salt.
common_mistake.why: The cooking verb 'season' means adding salt or spices, and it does not need an extra word like 'time' — that confusion may come from mixing it with the unrelated meaning of 'season' as a period of the year.

cloze.sentence: ____ the dal with a pinch of salt and cumin.

en_def: to try a small amount of food to check its flavour, or to have a particular flavour
hi_def: चखना (स्वाद जांचने के लिए थोड़ा खाना खाना), या स्वाद होना
hi_nuance: As a stative verb describing a quality, English says 'This tastes good' not 'This is tasting good' — Hindi speakers often overuse the continuous (-ing) form here because Hindi naturally uses an ongoing-action structure. Use the simple present for describing how something tastes.

examples.en: This biryani tastes amazing today.
examples.hi: आज यह बिरयानी बहुत बढ़िया स्वाद दे रही है।

examples.en: Can you taste the curry and tell me if it needs salt?
examples.hi: क्या तुम करी चखकर बता सकते हो कि इसमें नमक चाहिए या नहीं?

examples.en: The soup tastes a bit too sour for me.
examples.hi: यह सूप मेरे लिए थोड़ा ज्यादा खट्टा लग रहा है।

examples.en: I tasted the sauce before serving it to the guests.
examples.hi: मैंने मेहमानों को परोसने से पहले सॉस चखी।

examples.en: This mango tastes sweeter than the last one.
examples.hi: यह आम पिछले वाले से ज्यादा मीठा है।

common_mistake.wrong: This chicken is tasting very good today.
common_mistake.right: This chicken tastes very good today.
common_mistake.why: 'Taste' meaning 'to have a flavour' is a stative verb and is not normally used in the continuous form; the correct simple present is 'tastes', not 'is tasting'.

cloze.sentence: Please ____ the dal before you add any more salt.

en_def: a list of the food and drinks available in a restaurant
hi_def: मेन्यू (रेस्तरां में उपलब्ध खाने-पीने की चीजों की सूची)
hi_nuance: Note that 'menu' in English refers only to the printed or digital list of dishes; it does not mean the food itself. Also, when Hindi speakers order, they sometimes say 'give me one tea' or 'one plate noodles' — a direct translation of Hindi quantity phrases — where natural English prefers 'a cup of tea' or 'a plate of noodles'.

examples.en: Can we see the menu, please?
examples.hi: क्या हमें मेन्यू दिखा सकते हैं, कृपया?

examples.en: The menu has both veg and non-veg options.
examples.hi: मेन्यू में वेज और नॉन-वेज दोनों विकल्प हैं।

examples.en: This restaurant changed its menu last month.
examples.hi: इस रेस्तरां ने पिछले महीने अपना मेन्यू बदला।

examples.en: There's a special festive menu this weekend.
examples.hi: इस सप्ताहांत एक खास त्योहारी मेन्यू है।

examples.en: She ordered straight from the menu without asking the waiter.
examples.hi: उसने वेटर से पूछे बिना सीधे मेन्यू से ऑर्डर किया।

common_mistake.wrong: Show me today menu.
common_mistake.right: Show me today's menu.
common_mistake.why: English needs the possessive apostrophe-s, 'today's menu', to show that the menu belongs to today — simply saying 'today menu' skips this grammatical marker that Hindi expresses differently.

cloze.sentence: Could I see the ____ before I decide what to order?

en_def: a person, usually male, who serves food and drinks to customers in a restaurant
hi_def: वेटर (रेस्तरां में खाना-पीना परोसने वाला व्यक्ति)
hi_nuance: A common Indian-English pattern when ordering is to drop the article, saying 'One tea' or 'One plate biryani' to the waiter, directly translating Hindi's 'ek chai' or 'ek plate biryani'. More natural English is 'One tea, please' (acceptable informally) or fuller phrases like 'a cup of tea' and 'a plate of biryani' in formal writing. The female equivalent is 'waitress', though many restaurants now use the gender-neutral 'server'.

examples.en: The waiter recommended the butter chicken.
examples.hi: वेटर ने बटर चिकन की सिफारिश की।

examples.en: Excuse me, could you call the waiter?
examples.hi: माफ कीजिए, क्या आप वेटर को बुला सकते हैं?

examples.en: I asked the waiter for one plate of noodles.
examples.hi: मैंने वेटर से एक प्लेट नूडल्स मांगे।

examples.en: The waiter brought the bill along with two mints.
examples.hi: वेटर बिल के साथ दो मिंट्स भी लाया।

examples.en: She tipped the waiter generously after dinner.
examples.hi: उसने रात के खाने के बाद वेटर को अच्छी टिप दी।

common_mistake.wrong: Waiter, one tea and one samosa!
common_mistake.right: Waiter, could I get a cup of tea and a samosa, please?
common_mistake.why: Ordering with just a number and the food name, like 'one tea', is a direct translation from Hindi ('ek chai') and sounds abrupt in English — adding 'a cup of' or 'please' makes it sound more natural and polite.

cloze.sentence: She called the ____ over to ask for the bill.

en_def: a request for a restaurant table that seats two people
hi_def: दो लोगों के लिए टेबल (रेस्तरां में)
hi_nuance: This exact fixed phrase is used at a restaurant entrance or on the phone when booking; Hindi speakers sometimes translate it awkwardly as 'table of two' instead of the correct preposition 'table for two'.

examples.en: We'd like a table for two, please.
examples.hi: हमें दो लोगों के लिए एक टेबल चाहिए, कृपया।

examples.en: Do you have a table for two available right now?
examples.hi: क्या अभी दो लोगों के लिए कोई टेबल खाली है?

examples.en: I booked a table for two near the window.
examples.hi: मैंने खिड़की के पास दो लोगों के लिए एक टेबल बुक की।

examples.en: A table for two will be ready in ten minutes.
examples.hi: दो लोगों के लिए टेबल दस मिनट में तैयार हो जाएगी।

examples.en: Could we get a table for two on the terrace?
examples.hi: क्या हमें छत पर दो लोगों के लिए टेबल मिल सकती है?

common_mistake.wrong: We need a table of two near the window.
common_mistake.right: We need a table for two near the window.
common_mistake.why: The correct preposition in this fixed restaurant phrase is 'for', as in 'table for two', not 'table of two'.

cloze.sentence: Hi, could we get a ____ by the window, please?

en_def: an arrangement made in advance to have a table, room, or seat kept for you
hi_def: आरक्षण, बुकिंग (पहले से टेबल, कमरा या सीट सुरक्षित करवाना)
hi_nuance: In Indian English, 'booking' is used just as often as 'reservation', especially in British-influenced usage, and both are understood everywhere. 'Reservation' is slightly more formal and is the standard word in American English restaurant contexts.

examples.en: I made a reservation for eight o'clock tonight.
examples.hi: मैंने आज रात आठ बजे के लिए आरक्षण करवाया है।

examples.en: Do we need a reservation for this restaurant?
examples.hi: क्या इस रेस्तरां के लिए बुकिंग जरूरी है?

examples.en: The reservation is under my husband's name.
examples.hi: बुकिंग मेरे पति के नाम पर है।

examples.en: Please confirm the reservation before we arrive.
examples.hi: हमारे पहुंचने से पहले कृपया बुकिंग की पुष्टि कर दें।

examples.en: We cancelled the reservation because of the rain.
examples.hi: बारिश के कारण हमने बुकिंग रद्द कर दी।

common_mistake.wrong: I have done booking of table for tonight.
common_mistake.right: I have made a reservation for tonight.
common_mistake.why: The natural collocation in English is 'make a reservation' (or 'make a booking'), not 'do booking of table' — the verb 'make' pairs with 'reservation', not 'do'.

cloze.sentence: We need to call ahead and make a ____ for Saturday evening.

en_def: a small dish served before the main course of a meal
hi_def: स्टार्टर (मुख्य भोजन से पहले परोसा जाने वाला हल्का व्यंजन)
hi_nuance: This is the standard British and Indian English term; American English usually calls the same dish an 'appetizer'. Both words appear on Indian restaurant menus, but 'starter' is far more common in India.

examples.en: Let's order some starters while we wait for the mains.
examples.hi: मुख्य व्यंजन का इंतजार करते हुए कुछ स्टार्टर ऑर्डर करते हैं।

examples.en: The paneer tikka is a popular vegetarian starter.
examples.hi: पनीर टिक्का एक लोकप्रिय शाकाहारी स्टार्टर है।

examples.en: We shared two starters between the four of us.
examples.hi: हम चारों ने दो स्टार्टर आपस में बांटे।

examples.en: Which starter would you recommend from this menu?
examples.hi: इस मेन्यू में से आप कौन सा स्टार्टर सुझाएंगे?

examples.en: The starter arrived within ten minutes of ordering.
examples.hi: ऑर्डर करने के दस मिनट के भीतर स्टार्टर आ गया।

common_mistake.wrong: We want appetizer first, main course after.
common_mistake.right: We'd like the starters first, and the main course after.
common_mistake.why: 'Appetizer' is the American word; in India and British English 'starter' is the more commonly used term on restaurant menus, and the plural/phrasing here should also sound more natural.

cloze.sentence: Shall we order a ____ before the main course arrives?

en_def: the largest and most important dish of a meal, usually eaten after the starter
hi_def: मुख्य व्यंजन (भोजन का सबसे मुख्य हिस्सा, स्टार्टर के बाद खाया जाने वाला)
hi_nuance: Be careful with the French-origin word 'entrée' — in American English it means the main course, but in French and in some British contexts it actually means a starter, which can confuse travellers. In India, 'main course' is the safest, clearest term to use anywhere.

examples.en: For the main course, I'll have the butter chicken.
examples.hi: मुख्य व्यंजन के लिए, मैं बटर चिकन लूंगा।

examples.en: The main course took a while to arrive.
examples.hi: मुख्य व्यंजन आने में थोड़ा समय लगा।

examples.en: We ordered dal makhani and naan as the main course.
examples.hi: हमने मुख्य व्यंजन के तौर पर दाल मखनी और नान ऑर्डर की।

examples.en: What's your recommendation for the main course tonight?
examples.hi: आज रात के मुख्य व्यंजन के लिए आपकी क्या सिफारिश है?

examples.en: The main course portions here are quite generous.
examples.hi: यहां मुख्य व्यंजन की मात्रा काफी ज्यादा होती है।

common_mistake.wrong: I will take entrée as paneer butter masala.
common_mistake.right: I will have the paneer butter masala as my main course.
common_mistake.why: 'Entrée' is confusing internationally because it means 'main course' in American English but 'starter' in French and some British usage — 'main course' avoids this confusion entirely.

cloze.sentence: For the ____, she chose biryani with raita.

en_def: a sweet dish eaten at the end of a meal
hi_def: मिठाई, डेजर्ट (भोजन के अंत में खाया जाने वाला मीठा व्यंजन)
hi_nuance: Watch the spelling and stress: 'dessert' /dɪˈzɜːrt/ (sweet course) has a double 's' and stress on the second syllable, unlike 'desert' /ˈdezərt/ (a dry sandy area), which looks almost identical but is pronounced differently. Indian English often also uses 'sweet' or 'sweet dish' informally instead of 'dessert'.

examples.en: What's for dessert tonight?
examples.hi: आज रात मिठाई में क्या है?

examples.en: Gulab jamun is my favourite Indian dessert.
examples.hi: गुलाब जामुन मेरी पसंदीदा भारतीय मिठाई है।

examples.en: We skipped dessert because we were too full.
examples.hi: हमने मिठाई नहीं खाई क्योंकि हमारा पेट पहले से भरा था।

examples.en: The restaurant's dessert menu has ice cream and kheer.
examples.hi: रेस्तरां के मिठाई मेन्यू में आइसक्रीम और खीर है।

examples.en: She always saves room for dessert.
examples.hi: वह हमेशा मिठाई के लिए थोड़ी जगह बचाकर रखती है।

common_mistake.wrong: We went to desert after dinner.
common_mistake.right: We had dessert after dinner.
common_mistake.why: 'Desert' /ˈdezərt/ (a dry, sandy region) and 'dessert' /dɪˈzɜːrt/ (the sweet course) are frequently confused in spelling because they look so similar, but they are unrelated words.

cloze.sentence: After the meal, we ordered gulab jamun for ____.

en_def: the piece of paper showing how much money you owe for a meal at a restaurant
hi_def: बिल (रेस्तरां में खाने का भुगतान पत्र)
hi_nuance: 'Bill' is the standard British and Indian English word for the restaurant check; American English calls the same thing a 'check' (spelled 'check' in the US, 'cheque' only for bank cheques). If you travel to the US, ask for 'the check', not 'the bill', to avoid confusion.

examples.en: Could we get the bill, please?
examples.hi: क्या हमें बिल मिल सकता है, कृपया?

examples.en: The bill came to twelve hundred rupees.
examples.hi: बिल बारह सौ रुपये का बना।

examples.en: He paid the bill using his credit card.
examples.hi: उसने अपने क्रेडिट कार्ड से बिल का भुगतान किया।

examples.en: Always check the bill for any extra charges.
examples.hi: किसी भी अतिरिक्त शुल्क के लिए बिल जरूर जांच लो।

examples.en: She insisted on paying the bill this time.
examples.hi: इस बार उसने बिल भरने पर जोर दिया।

common_mistake.wrong: In America also, ask waiter for the bill.
common_mistake.right: In America, ask the waiter for the check.
common_mistake.why: 'Bill' is used in India and Britain for a restaurant payment slip, but Americans call the same thing a 'check' — using 'bill' in the US is understood but sounds noticeably foreign.

cloze.sentence: Excuse me, could we have the ____ please?

en_def: to divide the cost of a restaurant bill between two or more people
hi_def: बिल आपस में बांटना (रेस्तरां का खर्च कई लोगों में बांटना)
hi_nuance: This is sometimes called 'going Dutch' in casual British and American English, though that idiom is used less in India. 'Split the bill' or 'split the check' (American) are the clearer, more universally understood phrases to use while travelling.

examples.en: Let's split the bill equally among the four of us.
examples.hi: चलो हम चारों में बिल बराबर बांट लेते हैं।

examples.en: Can we split the bill, or do you want to pay it all?
examples.hi: क्या हम बिल बांट सकते हैं, या तुम पूरा भुगतान करना चाहते हो?

examples.en: They decided to split the bill instead of arguing.
examples.hi: उन्होंने बहस करने के बजाय बिल बांटने का फैसला किया।

examples.en: We usually split the bill when we eat out with friends.
examples.hi: हम आमतौर पर दोस्तों के साथ बाहर खाते समय बिल बांट लेते हैं।

examples.en: The waiter offered to split the bill into separate checks.
examples.hi: वेटर ने बिल को अलग-अलग हिस्सों में बांटने की पेशकश की।

common_mistake.wrong: We will divide bill in equal equal parts.
common_mistake.right: We will split the bill equally.
common_mistake.why: The natural English phrase is 'split the bill equally'; repeating 'equal equal' for emphasis is a Hindi-influenced pattern that sounds unnatural in English.

cloze.sentence: Since everyone ordered different dishes, let's just ____.

en_def: a small amount of extra money given to a waiter or service worker to thank them for good service
hi_def: टिप, बख्शीश (अच्छी सेवा के लिए वेटर को दिया जाने वाला अतिरिक्त पैसा)
hi_nuance: Many Indian restaurant bills already include a 'service charge', which is different from a voluntary tip, so Indian diners sometimes feel confused about whether tipping is still expected — it generally is, as a separate gesture, especially for good service.

examples.en: We left a generous tip for the waiter.
examples.hi: हमने वेटर के लिए एक अच्छी टिप छोड़ी।

examples.en: Is the tip included in the bill already?
examples.hi: क्या टिप पहले से ही बिल में शामिल है?

examples.en: He always tips ten percent at restaurants.
examples.hi: वह रेस्तरां में हमेशा दस प्रतिशत टिप देता है।

examples.en: She forgot to leave a tip after the meal.
examples.hi: वह खाने के बाद टिप देना भूल गई।

examples.en: A small tip in cash is common in India.
examples.hi: भारत में नकद में थोड़ी टिप देना आम बात है।

common_mistake.wrong: The bill already has service charge, so tip is not needed at all, ever.
common_mistake.right: The bill already has a service charge, but a small extra tip for good service is still appreciated.
common_mistake.why: A 'service charge' on the bill is a fixed restaurant fee, not the same as a voluntary 'tip' for the waiter personally — many diners still tip on top of it for good service.

cloze.sentence: Don't forget to leave a small ____ for the waiter.

en_def: food packed up at a restaurant to take away and eat somewhere else, instead of eating there
hi_def: पार्सल (रेस्तरां से पैक करवाकर ले जाया जाने वाला खाना)
hi_nuance: 'Parcel' for takeaway food is a very Indian English usage — in American English this is called 'to go' or 'takeout', and in British English it's called 'takeaway'. Saying 'I want a parcel' at a restaurant abroad may confuse staff; use 'to go' in the US or 'takeaway' in the UK instead.

examples.en: Can I get this biryani as a parcel?
examples.hi: क्या मुझे यह बिरयानी पार्सल में मिल सकती है?

examples.en: We ordered a parcel instead of eating at the restaurant.
examples.hi: हमने रेस्तरां में खाने के बजाय पार्सल ऑर्डर किया।

examples.en: The parcel was packed neatly in a plastic bag.
examples.hi: पार्सल एक प्लास्टिक बैग में साफ-सुथरे तरीके से पैक किया गया था।

examples.en: She picked up her parcel from the counter.
examples.hi: उसने काउंटर से अपना पार्सल उठाया।

examples.en: Please make it a parcel, we're in a hurry.
examples.hi: कृपया इसे पार्सल कर दीजिए, हमें जल्दी है।

common_mistake.wrong: I want to parcel this food, please pack it to go, both together.
common_mistake.right: I'd like this as a parcel to take away, please.
common_mistake.why: 'Parcel' is India's word for takeaway food, 'takeaway' is the British word, and 'to go' or 'takeout' is the American word — mixing all three terms together in one sentence is unnecessary and confusing.

cloze.sentence: We're running late, so let's just get the food as a ____.

en_def: a meal where different dishes are laid out and people serve themselves as much as they like
hi_def: बुफे (जहां कई व्यंजन रखे होते हैं और लोग खुद परोसकर खाते हैं)
hi_nuance: This word is often mispronounced by reading it phonetically as it's spelled, but the final 't' is silent, so it's pronounced 'boo-FAY', not 'buff-it' or 'buff-et'. It comes from French, like 'ballet' and 'valet', which also have silent final letters.

examples.en: The hotel offers an all-you-can-eat buffet on Sundays.
examples.hi: होटल रविवार को ऑल-यू-कैन-ईट बुफे परोसता है।

examples.en: We went to a wedding buffet with over twenty dishes.
examples.hi: हम एक शादी के बुफे में गए जहां बीस से ज्यादा व्यंजन थे।

examples.en: The buffet includes both starters and desserts.
examples.hi: बुफे में स्टार्टर और मिठाई दोनों शामिल हैं।

examples.en: Don't overfill your plate at the buffet counter.
examples.hi: बुफे काउंटर पर अपनी प्लेट ज्यादा मत भरो।

examples.en: The lunch buffet is cheaper than ordering à la carte.
examples.hi: लंच बुफे अलग से ऑर्डर करने से सस्ता है।

common_mistake.wrong: We ate at a buff-et restaurant yesterday.
common_mistake.right: We ate at a buffet restaurant yesterday.
common_mistake.why: 'Buffet' has a silent final 't', pronounced 'boo-FAY', not with the 't' sound — many learners pronounce it exactly as it is spelled.

cloze.sentence: The hotel's Sunday brunch ____ has both Indian and continental dishes.

en_def: knives, forks, and spoons used for eating food
hi_def: कटलरी (खाने के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाले चाकू, कांटे और चम्मच)
hi_nuance: British and Indian English use 'cutlery' for these eating tools; American English usually says 'silverware' or 'flatware' instead, even when the utensils are not made of actual silver. 'Cutlery' is always used as an uncountable noun — never say 'a cutlery' or 'cutleries'.

examples.en: Please set out the cutlery before the guests arrive.
examples.hi: मेहमानों के आने से पहले कृपया कटलरी सजा दो।

examples.en: The waiter forgot to bring extra cutlery.
examples.hi: वेटर अतिरिक्त कटलरी लाना भूल गया।

examples.en: This restaurant uses steel cutlery instead of plastic.
examples.hi: यह रेस्तरां प्लास्टिक के बजाय स्टील की कटलरी इस्तेमाल करता है।

examples.en: Wash the cutlery separately from the greasy pans.
examples.hi: कटलरी को चिकने बर्तनों से अलग धोओ।

examples.en: The gift set included cutlery and a matching tablecloth.
examples.hi: उपहार सेट में कटलरी और उससे मिलती-जुलती मेज़पोश शामिल थी।

common_mistake.wrong: Please give me one cutlery.
common_mistake.right: Please give me some cutlery, or please give me a fork and spoon.
common_mistake.why: 'Cutlery' is an uncountable noun in English, so it cannot be used with 'one' or in the plural — you can say 'some cutlery' or name the specific item, like 'a fork'.

cloze.sentence: Please lay out the ____ before the guests sit down to eat.

en_def: a piece of cloth or paper used at meals to wipe your mouth or hands, or protect your clothes
hi_def: नैपकिन (खाने के दौरान मुंह या हाथ पोंछने के लिए कपड़ा या कागज का टुकड़ा)
hi_nuance: 'Napkin' is standard in both American and British English, though British speakers sometimes call the cloth version a 'serviette' (from French) in more casual or older-fashioned usage. In India, 'napkin' most commonly refers to the paper tissue given at restaurants.

examples.en: Can I have an extra napkin, please?
examples.hi: क्या मुझे एक अतिरिक्त नैपकिन मिल सकता है, कृपया?

examples.en: She wiped her hands on the paper napkin.
examples.hi: उसने अपने हाथ कागज के नैपकिन से पोंछे।

examples.en: The waiter placed a cloth napkin beside each plate.
examples.hi: वेटर ने हर प्लेट के बगल में एक कपड़े का नैपकिन रखा।

examples.en: There were no napkins left on the table.
examples.hi: टेबल पर कोई नैपकिन नहीं बचा था।

examples.en: He tucked the napkin into his collar before eating.
examples.hi: उसने खाने से पहले नैपकिन अपने कॉलर में खोंस लिया।

common_mistake.wrong: Please give me one tissue paper for hand.
common_mistake.right: Please give me a napkin.
common_mistake.why: At a restaurant table, the correct word for the paper used to wipe your mouth or hands is 'napkin'; 'tissue paper' usually refers to gift-wrapping paper or a facial tissue, not the table item.

cloze.sentence: He wiped his mouth with a paper ____ after the meal.

en_def: a utensil with a small, shallow bowl and a handle, used for eating liquid or soft food
hi_def: चम्मच (तरल या नरम खाना खाने के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाला बर्तन)
hi_nuance: This is a basic, universally known word with no British-American difference, but note the collocation 'a spoon of sugar' or 'a spoonful of sugar' — English requires 'of' between the quantity word and the noun, unlike the direct Hindi phrasing.

examples.en: Could I have a spoon for this soup?
examples.hi: क्या मुझे इस सूप के लिए एक चम्मच मिल सकती है?

examples.en: She stirred her tea with a small spoon.
examples.hi: उसने अपनी चाय को एक छोटी चम्मच से हिलाया।

examples.en: Add one spoon of sugar to the batter.
examples.hi: घोल में एक चम्मच चीनी डालो।

examples.en: The baby used a plastic spoon to eat.
examples.hi: बच्चे ने खाने के लिए प्लास्टिक की चम्मच इस्तेमाल की।

examples.en: There's only one clean spoon left in the drawer.
examples.hi: दराज में सिर्फ एक साफ चम्मच बची है।

common_mistake.wrong: Add one spoon sugar in the tea.
common_mistake.right: Add one spoon of sugar to the tea.
common_mistake.why: English requires the preposition 'of' between a quantity word and the noun that follows — 'a spoon of sugar', not 'spoon sugar' — a small but important grammar point often dropped in Indian English speech.

cloze.sentence: Could you bring me a clean ____ for the soup?

en_def: a utensil with pointed prongs used for lifting and eating food
hi_def: कांटा (खाना उठाने और खाने के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाला बर्तन)
hi_nuance: Straightforward everyday word; the main note for Hindi speakers is the pronunciation, since the vowel sound /ɔː/ doesn't exist in Hindi and can come out closer to 'fark' or 'phork' — practising the rounded 'or' sound helps.

examples.en: Please pass me a fork and knife.
examples.hi: कृपया मुझे एक कांटा और चाकू दे दो।

examples.en: He ate the pasta with a fork.
examples.hi: उसने पास्ता कांटे से खाया।

examples.en: The restaurant gave us forks even though it's usually eaten with hands.
examples.hi: रेस्तरां ने हमें कांटे दिए, हालांकि यह आमतौर पर हाथों से खाया जाता है।

examples.en: She dropped her fork on the floor by mistake.
examples.hi: उसका कांटा गलती से फर्श पर गिर गया।

examples.en: Use a fork to twirl the noodles neatly.
examples.hi: नूडल्स को साफ-सुथरे तरीके से लपेटने के लिए कांटे का इस्तेमाल करो।

common_mistake.wrong: Give me one fork and one spoon, both together for eating rice.
common_mistake.right: Please give me a fork and a spoon to eat the rice.
common_mistake.why: The phrase 'both together' is unnecessary in English once you've already listed two items with 'and' — it's a redundant addition often carried over from Hindi speech habits.

cloze.sentence: She twirled the spaghetti neatly around her ____.

en_def: a pair of thin sticks, usually held in one hand, used for eating food, especially in East Asian and Indo-Chinese cuisine
hi_def: चॉपस्टिक्स (एक जोड़ी पतली छड़ियां, जिनसे खाना खाया जाता है, खासकर चाइनीज़ खाने में)
hi_nuance: This word is always used in the plural form, 'chopsticks', just like 'scissors' or 'trousers' — you cannot say 'a chopstick' meaning the pair; instead say 'a pair of chopsticks' if you need to count them.

examples.en: Can you use chopsticks to eat noodles?
examples.hi: क्या तुम नूडल्स चॉपस्टिक्स से खा सकते हो?

examples.en: This Indo-Chinese restaurant gives you a choice of chopsticks or a fork.
examples.hi: यह इंडो-चाइनीज़ रेस्तरां तुम्हें चॉपस्टिक्स या कांटे में से चुनने का विकल्प देता है।

examples.en: I struggled to hold the chopsticks properly at first.
examples.hi: शुरुआत में मुझे चॉपस्टिक्स सही से पकड़ने में दिक्कत हुई।

examples.en: She ordered an extra pair of chopsticks for her friend.
examples.hi: उसने अपने दोस्त के लिए चॉपस्टिक्स की एक अतिरिक्त जोड़ी मंगाई।

examples.en: Wooden chopsticks are common at Chinese restaurants.
examples.hi: चाइनीज़ रेस्तरां में लकड़ी की चॉपस्टिक्स आम हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: Give me a chopstick to eat this noodles.
common_mistake.right: Give me a pair of chopsticks to eat these noodles.
common_mistake.why: 'Chopsticks' is always plural, like 'scissors', so it's 'a pair of chopsticks', never 'a chopstick'; also 'noodles' itself is plural, so it takes 'these', not 'this'.

cloze.sentence: At the Chinese restaurant, she asked for ____ instead of a fork.

en_def: a thin tube used for drinking a liquid, usually made of plastic, paper, or steel
hi_def: स्ट्रॉ, तिनका (पेय पदार्थ पीने के लिए इस्तेमाल होने वाली पतली नली)
hi_nuance: Many restaurants and juice shops in India have switched from plastic straws to paper or steel straws due to environmental rules — worth knowing the phrase 'no plastic straws' if you see it on a menu or sign.

examples.en: Can I have a straw for my juice, please?
examples.hi: क्या मुझे मेरे जूस के लिए एक स्ट्रॉ मिल सकता है, कृपया?

examples.en: This café only uses paper straws now.
examples.hi: यह कैफे अब सिर्फ कागज के स्ट्रॉ इस्तेमाल करता है।

examples.en: The kid drank his milkshake through a straw.
examples.hi: बच्चे ने अपनी मिल्कशेक स्ट्रॉ से पी।

examples.en: Steel straws are reusable and better for the environment.
examples.hi: स्टील के स्ट्रॉ फिर से इस्तेमाल हो सकते हैं और पर्यावरण के लिए बेहतर हैं।

examples.en: The lemonade came with a colourful bendy straw.
examples.hi: लेमोनेड एक रंगीन मुड़ने वाले स्ट्रॉ के साथ आई।

common_mistake.wrong: Give me a straw for drink this water.
common_mistake.right: Give me a straw to drink this water.
common_mistake.why: After 'give me a straw', English uses the infinitive 'to drink', not 'for drink' — 'for' should be followed by a noun or gerund ('for drinking'), while 'to' pairs with the base verb form.

cloze.sentence: The waiter brought a paper ____ along with the fresh lime soda.

en_def: a service where food is brought directly to your house from a restaurant or shop
hi_def: होम डिलीवरी (रेस्तरां या दुकान से खाना सीधे घर पहुंचाने की सेवा)
hi_nuance: In everyday international English, people often just say 'delivery' without adding 'home' — 'Does this restaurant do delivery?' — while Indian English regularly says the fuller phrase 'home delivery', which is understood everywhere but sounds slightly more formal or old-fashioned to native speakers.

examples.en: This restaurant offers home delivery within thirty minutes.
examples.hi: यह रेस्तरां तीस मिनट के भीतर होम डिलीवरी देता है।

examples.en: We ordered home delivery because it was raining heavily.
examples.hi: हमने होम डिलीवरी मंगवाई क्योंकि तेज बारिश हो रही थी।

examples.en: Does this pizza place have home delivery on weekends?
examples.hi: क्या यह पिज्जा जगह सप्ताहांत में होम डिलीवरी देती है?

examples.en: Home delivery charges are added to the final bill.
examples.hi: होम डिलीवरी शुल्क अंतिम बिल में जोड़ा जाता है।

examples.en: The app tracks your home delivery in real time.
examples.hi: ऐप आपकी होम डिलीवरी को वास्तविक समय में ट्रैक करता है।

common_mistake.wrong: Does this hotel have home delivery facility?
common_mistake.right: Does this restaurant offer home delivery?
common_mistake.why: In this context, 'hotel' should be 'restaurant' — a very common Indian-English mix-up where 'hotel' is used for any eating place, even though in standard English a 'hotel' is specifically a place to stay overnight.

cloze.sentence: Since it's raining, let's just order ____ instead of going out.

en_def: a payment method where you pay in cash when your food or parcel is delivered to you, rather than paying online in advance
hi_def: कैश ऑन डिलीवरी (सामान या खाना पहुंचने पर नकद भुगतान करना, पहले से ऑनलाइन भुगतान करने के बजाय)
hi_nuance: This phrase, often shortened to 'COD', is extremely common in Indian food delivery apps and e-commerce, more so than in many Western countries where online prepayment is the default. It's useful vocabulary specific to ordering in India.

examples.en: I selected cash on delivery for this order.
examples.hi: मैंने इस ऑर्डर के लिए कैश ऑन डिलीवरी चुनी।

examples.en: Does this app support cash on delivery?
examples.hi: क्या यह ऐप कैश ऑन डिलीवरी सपोर्ट करता है?

examples.en: He paid by cash on delivery instead of using his card.
examples.hi: उसने कार्ड इस्तेमाल करने के बजाय कैश ऑन डिलीवरी से भुगतान किया।

examples.en: Some restaurants have stopped offering cash on delivery.
examples.hi: कुछ रेस्तरां ने कैश ऑन डिलीवरी देना बंद कर दिया है।

examples.en: Keep exact change ready for cash on delivery.
examples.hi: कैश ऑन डिलीवरी के लिए सही खुले पैसे तैयार रखो।

common_mistake.wrong: I will give cash on delivery time.
common_mistake.right: I will pay by cash on delivery.
common_mistake.why: The correct fixed phrase is simply 'pay by cash on delivery' or 'choose cash on delivery'; adding 'time' after it is unnecessary and not standard usage.

cloze.sentence: Since I don't trust online payments, I usually choose ____ for food orders.

en_def: to eat a meal inside a restaurant, rather than taking it away or having it delivered
hi_def: रेस्तरां में बैठकर खाना (पार्सल लेने या डिलीवरी मंगवाने के बजाय)
hi_nuance: Fast-food counters and food apps in India usually offer three choices: 'dine in', 'takeaway/parcel', or 'delivery' — knowing all three terms helps you respond quickly when asked 'Dine in or parcel?' at a counter.

examples.en: Would you like to dine in or take it away?
examples.hi: क्या आप यहां बैठकर खाना चाहेंगे या पार्सल लेंगे?

examples.en: We decided to dine in instead of ordering delivery.
examples.hi: हमने डिलीवरी मंगवाने के बजाय रेस्तरां में बैठकर खाने का फैसला किया।

examples.en: The dine-in area was fully booked on Saturday night.
examples.hi: शनिवार रात को डाइन-इन क्षेत्र पूरी तरह से बुक था।

examples.en: This café only offers dine-in, no delivery.
examples.hi: यह कैफे केवल डाइन-इन देता है, कोई डिलीवरी नहीं।

examples.en: Dining in lets you enjoy the food while it's hot.
examples.hi: रेस्तरां में बैठकर खाने से आप गरम खाने का आनंद ले सकते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: Are you dine in or take away?
common_mistake.right: Are you dining in or taking away?
common_mistake.why: 'Dine in' needs to be used as a verb phrase with the correct form, 'dining in', when following 'are you' — using the base form directly after 'are you' is a grammar slip common in spoken Indian English.

cloze.sentence: The counter staff asked if we wanted to ____ or get a parcel.

en_def: a small, informal restaurant or place where you can buy and eat food
hi_def: खाने-पीने की छोटी दुकान, ईटरी (छोटा, अनौपचारिक रेस्तरां)
hi_nuance: A classic Indian English mistake is calling any restaurant a 'hotel', as in 'let's eat at that hotel', which confuses foreigners because in standard English a 'hotel' means a place to stay overnight, not to eat. This everyday usage in India ('veg hotel', 'non-veg hotel') comes from older regional English, but the correct international words are 'restaurant', 'eatery', or 'diner' for a place that only serves food.

examples.en: There's a nice little eatery near my office.
examples.hi: मेरे ऑफिस के पास एक अच्छी छोटी ईटरी है।

examples.en: This roadside eatery serves the best dosas in town.
examples.hi: यह सड़क किनारे की ईटरी शहर के सबसे बढ़िया डोसे परोसती है।

examples.en: We found a cheap eatery for a quick lunch.
examples.hi: हमें झटपट दोपहर के खाने के लिए एक सस्ती ईटरी मिली।

examples.en: The local eatery is always crowded on weekends.
examples.hi: स्थानीय ईटरी सप्ताहांत में हमेशा भीड़ भरी रहती है।

examples.en: Many small eateries don't accept card payments.
examples.hi: कई छोटी ईटरी कार्ड से भुगतान स्वीकार नहीं करतीं।

common_mistake.wrong: Let's have dinner at that hotel near our house.
common_mistake.right: Let's have dinner at that restaurant near our house.
common_mistake.why: In standard English, a 'hotel' is a place where you stay overnight; using it to mean 'restaurant' or 'eatery', as is common in Indian English, confuses people from outside India — say 'restaurant' or 'eatery' instead.

cloze.sentence: We stopped at a small roadside ____ for some hot samosas.

en_def: clean and healthy, free from germs or dirt that could cause illness
hi_def: स्वच्छ, हाइजीनिक (साफ-सुथरा और स्वास्थ्यवर्धक, कीटाणुओं से मुक्त)
hi_nuance: Note the stress pattern: 'hy-gi-EN-ic', with the main stress on the third syllable, which many learners get wrong by stressing the first syllable instead. This word is frequently discussed regarding street food safety in India.

examples.en: Make sure the kitchen is kept hygienic at all times.
examples.hi: सुनिश्चित करो कि रसोई हमेशा स्वच्छ रखी जाए।

examples.en: This street food stall looks quite hygienic.
examples.hi: यह स्ट्रीट फूड स्टॉल काफी स्वच्छ दिखता है।

examples.en: Always wash your hands to stay hygienic before eating.
examples.hi: खाने से पहले स्वच्छ रहने के लिए हमेशा अपने हाथ धोओ।

examples.en: The restaurant received a certificate for hygienic practices.
examples.hi: रेस्तरां को स्वच्छ प्रथाओं के लिए एक प्रमाणपत्र मिला।

examples.en: She avoids stalls that don't look hygienic.
examples.hi: वह उन स्टॉलों से बचती है जो स्वच्छ नहीं दिखते।

common_mistake.wrong: This shop is very hygenic, we can eat here safely.
common_mistake.right: This shop is very hygienic, we can eat here safely.
common_mistake.why: The correct spelling is 'hygienic', with 'ie' before the 'n', not 'hygenic' — a common spelling slip since the pronunciation doesn't clearly signal the letter order.

cloze.sentence: We only eat at stalls that look clean and ____.

en_def: food sold and often cooked by vendors on the street, usually cheap and eaten quickly
hi_def: स्ट्रीट फूड (सड़क किनारे विक्रेताओं द्वारा बेचा जाने वाला सस्ता और झटपट खाया जाने वाला खाना)
hi_nuance: This term is used worldwide, and Indian street food like chaat, vada pav, and pani puri is internationally famous. Travellers are often warned to check hygiene levels before trying street food, but it remains one of the most authentic ways to experience local flavours.

examples.en: Mumbai is famous for its delicious street food.
examples.hi: मुंबई अपने स्वादिष्ट स्ट्रीट फूड के लिए प्रसिद्ध है।

examples.en: We tried different street food stalls during our trip.
examples.hi: हमने अपनी यात्रा के दौरान अलग-अलग स्ट्रीट फूड स्टॉल आजमाए।

examples.en: Pani puri is one of the most popular street foods in India.
examples.hi: पानी पूरी भारत के सबसे लोकप्रिय स्ट्रीट फूड में से एक है।

examples.en: Some tourists are cautious about eating street food.
examples.hi: कुछ पर्यटक स्ट्रीट फूड खाने को लेकर सतर्क रहते हैं।

examples.en: The street food here is cheaper than restaurant meals.
examples.hi: यहां का स्ट्रीट फूड रेस्तरां के खाने से सस्ता है।

common_mistake.wrong: This city have very famous street foods.
common_mistake.right: This city has very famous street food.
common_mistake.why: 'Street food' is usually treated as an uncountable noun in general statements, so 'street food' (singular) is preferred over 'street foods'; also the verb should agree as 'has', not 'have', with the singular subject 'city'.

cloze.sentence: Vada pav is one of Mumbai's most loved ____ items.

en_def: containing meat, fish, or eggs; not vegetarian (an informal Indian English term)
hi_def: नॉन-वेज (मांस, मछली या अंडे युक्त; शाकाहारी नहीं)
hi_nuance: 'Non-veg' is a very common and widely understood term across India, but it is not standard International English — it would sound unusual in the US, UK, or Australia. In standard English, say 'a meat dish', 'non-vegetarian food', or simply name the item (like 'chicken curry') instead of 'non-veg' when writing or speaking to an international audience.

examples.en: Do you have any non-veg options on the menu?
examples.hi: क्या मेन्यू में कोई नॉन-वेज विकल्प है?

examples.en: He doesn't eat non-veg food at all.
examples.hi: वह बिल्कुल भी नॉन-वेज खाना नहीं खाता।

examples.en: This restaurant has separate veg and non-veg sections.
examples.hi: इस रेस्तरां में वेज और नॉन-वेज के लिए अलग-अलग सेक्शन हैं।

examples.en: We ordered one veg and one non-veg starter.
examples.hi: हमने एक वेज और एक नॉन-वेज स्टार्टर ऑर्डर किया।

examples.en: She switched to non-veg food only recently.
examples.hi: उसने हाल ही में नॉन-वेज खाना शुरू किया।

common_mistake.wrong: I ordered a non-veg in the airplane and the American beside me looked confused.
common_mistake.right: I ordered a non-vegetarian meal on the airplane, and the American beside me looked confused because 'non-veg' isn't a standard English term.
common_mistake.why: 'Non-veg' is common and clearly understood across India, but it isn't standard International English; travellers should use 'non-vegetarian' or name the specific dish when speaking with people from outside India.

cloze.sentence: The menu clearly marks each dish as either vegetarian or ____.

en_def: a lower price than usual, agreed after discussion between buyer and seller; also, to negotiate the price of something.
hi_def: वह कम कीमत जो खरीदार और विक्रेता के बीच बातचीत के बाद तय होती है; किसी चीज़ की कीमत पर मोल-भाव करना।
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often use 'bargain' as a verb the way मोल-भाव करना works, saying 'I will bargain him' instead of 'I will bargain with him' — bargain needs 'with' before a person. Also note bargain (noun, a good deal) versus haggle (the act of negotiating) are often confused.

examples.en: I got this shirt at a bargain price.
examples.hi: मुझे यह शर्ट सस्ते दाम में मिली।

examples.en: Let's bargain with the shopkeeper before buying.
examples.hi: खरीदने से पहले दुकानदार से मोल-भाव करते हैं।

examples.en: That laptop was a real bargain.
examples.hi: वह लैपटॉप सच में बहुत सस्ता सौदा था।

examples.en: You can bargain a little at this market.
examples.hi: इस बाज़ार में थोड़ा मोल-भाव कर सकते हैं।

examples.en: He struck a bargain with the vendor for the mangoes.
examples.hi: उसने आम वाले से मोल-भाव करके सौदा तय किया।

common_mistake.wrong: I bargained him for a lower price.
common_mistake.right: I bargained with him for a lower price.
common_mistake.why: In Hindi, मोल-भाव करना doesn't require an equivalent of 'with'; learners drop the preposition 'with' needed before the person you negotiate with in English.

cloze.sentence: The vendor offered me a good ____ on the vegetables.

en_def: to argue or discuss with someone in order to reach an agreement about the price of something.
hi_def: किसी चीज़ की कीमत को लेकर विक्रेता से बहस या बातचीत करना, ताकि दाम कम कराया जा सके।
hi_nuance: Haggle and bargain are near-synonyms as verbs, but haggle carries a slightly negative or tiring connotation (long back-and-forth), while bargain sounds neutral. Many Indian shoppers say 'do bargaining' (Hinglish) instead of haggle or bargain — avoid mixing 'do' with these words.

examples.en: She haggled over the price of the bangles for ten minutes.
examples.hi: उसने चूड़ियों की कीमत को लेकर दस मिनट तक मोल-भाव किया।

examples.en: Don't haggle too much, it's already a fair price.
examples.hi: ज़्यादा मोल-भाव मत करो, यह पहले से ही सही दाम है।

examples.en: Tourists often haggle at street markets.
examples.hi: पर्यटक अक्सर सड़क के बाज़ारों में मोल-भाव करते हैं।

examples.en: I hate haggling, so I prefer fixed-price shops.
examples.hi: मुझे मोल-भाव करना पसंद नहीं, इसलिए मैं फिक्स्ड-प्राइस दुकानों को तरजीह देता हूँ।

examples.en: He haggled the price down by two hundred rupees.
examples.hi: उसने कीमत दो सौ रुपये कम करा ली।

common_mistake.wrong: I did haggling with the seller.
common_mistake.right: I haggled with the seller. / I did some haggling with the seller.
common_mistake.why: 'Haggling' used as a noun needs 'do some haggling,' not 'do haggling' alone, and as a verb it's simply 'haggled' — a direct translation of मोल-भाव किया as 'did haggling' sounds unnatural.

cloze.sentence: Tourists like to ____ over prices at the local market.

en_def: available to buy at a reduced price, usually for a limited time.
hi_def: किसी सीमित समय के लिए घटी हुई कीमत पर उपलब्ध सामान।
hi_nuance: In American English 'on sale' means discounted; in British English it can simply mean 'available for purchase' (which Americans call 'for sale'). Indian English mostly follows the American sense (discounted), so be careful when reading British text where 'on sale' might just mean 'in stores now.'

examples.en: These shoes are on sale this week.
examples.hi: ये जूते इस हफ़्ते सेल पर हैं।

examples.en: I bought this jacket when it was on sale.
examples.hi: मैंने यह जैकेट तब खरीदी जब यह सेल पर थी।

examples.en: Everything in the store is on sale for the festival.
examples.hi: त्योहार के लिए दुकान में सब कुछ सेल पर है।

examples.en: Is this phone still on sale, or has the offer ended?
examples.hi: क्या यह फ़ोन अभी भी सेल पर है, या ऑफर खत्म हो गया?

examples.en: Winter clothes go on sale in March.
examples.hi: सर्दियों के कपड़े मार्च में सेल पर आते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: This shop's sale is on from today, all items are on sale price.
common_mistake.right: This shop's sale starts today; all items are on sale.
common_mistake.why: Learners often add the redundant word 'price' after 'on sale,' since Hindi phrasing सेल में already implies price; 'on sale' alone already means discounted.

cloze.sentence: All winter jackets are ____ this week, so hurry!

en_def: a temporary deal in which something is sold at a lower price or with an extra benefit, to attract customers.
hi_def: ग्राहकों को आकर्षित करने के लिए कुछ समय के लिए दी जाने वाली विशेष छूट या अतिरिक्त लाभ वाली पेशकश।
hi_nuance: Indian shops often shout 'special offer, special offer!' to mean any discount at all; in standard English 'special offer' specifically implies something extra (like a free gift or bundle), while a plain price cut is usually just called a discount or sale.

examples.en: There's a special offer on cooking oil this month.
examples.hi: इस महीने खाने के तेल पर एक विशेष ऑफर है।

examples.en: The shop is running a special offer: buy two, get one free.
examples.hi: दुकान एक विशेष ऑफर चला रही है: दो खरीदो, एक मुफ्त पाओ।

examples.en: I signed up early to get the special offer price.
examples.hi: मैंने विशेष ऑफर की कीमत पाने के लिए जल्दी रजिस्टर किया।

examples.en: Check the app for today's special offers.
examples.hi: आज के विशेष ऑफर के लिए ऐप देखो।

examples.en: The special offer ends on Sunday.
examples.hi: यह विशेष ऑफर रविवार को खत्म हो जाएगा।

common_mistake.wrong: Shop is giving special offer, come fast.
common_mistake.right: The shop is running a special offer, come fast.
common_mistake.why: Indian English often drops articles ('a,' 'the') and auxiliary verbs, directly mirroring Hindi, which doesn't use articles; English requires 'a special offer' and a proper subject-verb structure.

cloze.sentence: The store has a ____ on smartphones this weekend — twenty percent off.

en_def: not currently available to buy because the shop has none left.
hi_def: दुकान में सामान का न होना, यानी वह वस्तु फिलहाल उपलब्ध नहीं है।
hi_nuance: Indian shopkeepers often say 'stock nahi hai' — in English this becomes 'out of stock,' not 'no stock' or 'stock is not there,' which are direct, ungrammatical translations from Hindi.

examples.en: Sorry, that size is out of stock right now.
examples.hi: माफ़ कीजिए, वह साइज़ अभी उपलब्ध नहीं है।

examples.en: The medicine I need is out of stock at every pharmacy nearby.
examples.hi: मुझे जो दवा चाहिए वह आसपास की हर दुकान में उपलब्ध नहीं है।

examples.en: This item has been out of stock for two weeks.
examples.hi: यह सामान दो हफ़्तों से स्टॉक में नहीं है।

examples.en: Can you tell me when it will be back in stock? It's out of stock online too.
examples.hi: क्या आप बता सकते हैं यह कब वापस स्टॉक में आएगा? यह ऑनलाइन भी उपलब्ध नहीं है।

examples.en: We ran out of stock during the festival rush.
examples.hi: त्योहार की भीड़ के दौरान हमारा स्टॉक खत्म हो गया।

common_mistake.wrong: Sir, stock is not there, come tomorrow.
common_mistake.right: Sir, it's out of stock; please come tomorrow.
common_mistake.why: This is a literal translation of स्टॉक नहीं है — English needs the fixed phrase 'out of stock' rather than 'stock is not there.'

cloze.sentence: I wanted to buy that saree, but it was ____ everywhere.

en_def: currently available to buy in a shop or warehouse.
hi_def: दुकान या गोदाम में किसी वस्तु का उपलब्ध होना।
hi_nuance: Pairs directly with 'out of stock.' Indian English speakers sometimes say 'stock is available' instead of the more natural 'it's in stock' — both are understood, but 'in stock' is the standard retail phrase used on receipts, apps, and signs.

examples.en: Good news, your size is in stock now.
examples.hi: अच्छी खबर है, आपका साइज़ अब उपलब्ध है।

examples.en: We keep this brand in stock all year round.
examples.hi: हम यह ब्रांड पूरे साल स्टॉक में रखते हैं।

examples.en: Is the red one in stock, or only the blue?
examples.hi: क्या लाल वाला उपलब्ध है, या सिर्फ नीला?

examples.en: The website shows it's in stock, but the shop says otherwise.
examples.hi: वेबसाइट दिखाती है कि यह उपलब्ध है, पर दुकान कुछ और कहती है।

examples.en: As soon as it's in stock, I'll call you.
examples.hi: जैसे ही यह स्टॉक में आएगा, मैं आपको फोन करूँगा।

collocations: in stock and ready to ship

common_mistake.wrong: This item is having stock.
common_mistake.right: This item is in stock.
common_mistake.why: Indian English overuses continuous '-ing' forms with 'have' (carried over from Hindi's habitual verb structures); English retail simply says 'in stock,' not 'having stock.'

cloze.sentence: Don't worry, we have plenty ____, you can buy it right now.

en_def: a line of people waiting for their turn, for example to pay at a counter.
hi_def: अपनी बारी का इंतज़ार करते हुए लोगों की कतार या लाइन।
hi_nuance: British English says 'queue' (and 'queue up'); American English usually says 'line' ('stand in line'). Indian English uses both, but 'queue' is common in formal/official contexts (banks, government offices) while spoken Hindi-English often says 'line laga do' for 'join the queue.'

examples.en: There's a long queue at the billing counter.
examples.hi: बिलिंग काउंटर पर लंबी कतार है।

examples.en: Please stand in the queue, don't jump ahead.
examples.hi: कृपया कतार में खड़े रहें, आगे मत बढ़िए।

examples.en: We queued for twenty minutes to pay the electricity bill.
examples.hi: हम बिजली का बिल भरने के लिए बीस मिनट कतार में खड़े रहे।

examples.en: The queue moved quickly today.
examples.hi: आज कतार जल्दी आगे बढ़ी।

examples.en: Is this the queue for the cash counter?
examples.hi: क्या यह कैश काउंटर की कतार है?

common_mistake.wrong: Please make a queue here.
common_mistake.right: Please form a queue here.
common_mistake.why: 'Make a queue' is a direct translation of कतार बनाओ; the natural English collocation is 'form a queue,' not 'make.'

cloze.sentence: There was a huge ____ outside the mobile shop for the new phone launch.

en_def: money in the form of notes and coins, rather than by card or digital transfer.
hi_def: नोट और सिक्कों के रूप में पैसा, कार्ड या डिजिटल भुगतान के बजाय।
hi_nuance: In India, 'cash' is often contrasted with UPI/card as 'cash ya online?' — English speakers might ask 'cash or card?' but Indians usually add UPI as a third option. Note 'cash' is uncountable — avoid saying 'cashes' or 'a cash.'

examples.en: Do you have exact cash, or should I use my card?
examples.hi: क्या आपके पास सही कैश है, या मैं कार्ड इस्तेमाल करूँ?

examples.en: I only carry a little cash these days.
examples.hi: मैं आजकल थोड़ा ही कैश साथ रखता हूँ।

examples.en: Cash or UPI, whichever is easier for you.
examples.hi: कैश हो या यूपीआई, जो भी आपको आसान लगे।

examples.en: The shop doesn't accept cards, only cash.
examples.hi: वह दुकान कार्ड स्वीकार नहीं करती, सिर्फ कैश लेती है।

examples.en: I withdrew some cash from the ATM before shopping.
examples.hi: मैंने खरीदारी से पहले एटीएम से कुछ कैश निकाला।

common_mistake.wrong: I don't have cashes with me.
common_mistake.right: I don't have cash with me.
common_mistake.why: 'Cash' is an uncountable noun in English, so it never takes a plural '-s,' unlike Hindi पैसे, which is grammatically plural.

cloze.sentence: I forgot my wallet, do you accept ____, or only card?

en_def: to pass a payment card through or tap it on a card machine to make a payment.
hi_def: भुगतान के लिए कार्ड को मशीन में डालना, घुमाना या टैप करना।
hi_nuance: Originally 'swipe' meant dragging the magnetic stripe through a reader; most Indian card machines now use 'insert' (chip) or 'tap' (contactless), but 'swipe the card' has stuck as the general everyday phrase for 'pay by card,' similar to how people still say 'dial a number' for phones without dials.

examples.en: Please swipe the card here, sir.
examples.hi: सर, कृपया यहाँ कार्ड स्वाइप कीजिए।

examples.en: I swiped my card twice but the payment failed both times.
examples.hi: मैंने कार्ड दो बार स्वाइप किया पर दोनों बार भुगतान नहीं हुआ।

examples.en: You can tap or swipe the card, whichever works.
examples.hi: आप कार्ड टैप या स्वाइप कर सकते हैं, जो भी चले।

examples.en: The cashier asked me to swipe the card again for the correct amount.
examples.hi: कैशियर ने सही राशि के लिए कार्ड फिर से स्वाइप करने को कहा।

examples.en: Swipe the card slowly, the machine is old.
examples.hi: कार्ड धीरे से स्वाइप कीजिए, मशीन पुरानी है।

common_mistake.wrong: Please do swipe of the card.
common_mistake.right: Please swipe the card.
common_mistake.why: Indian English sometimes turns simple verbs into noun phrases with 'do' ('do the swipe'), influenced by Hindi constructions like स्वाइप कर दो; English keeps 'swipe' as a direct verb.

cloze.sentence: The cashier asked me to ____ at the machine near the counter.

en_def: Unified Payments Interface — India's popular instant, mobile-based payment system that lets people transfer money directly between bank accounts using an app and a QR code or ID.
hi_def: यूनिफाइड पेमेंट्स इंटरफेस — भारत की एक लोकप्रिय तुरंत भुगतान प्रणाली, जिससे मोबाइल ऐप और क्यूआर कोड के ज़रिए सीधे बैंक खातों के बीच पैसे भेजे जा सकते हैं।
hi_nuance: UPI is uniquely Indian and has no direct Western equivalent (it's faster and more universal than Western apps like Venmo or PayPal, working across all banks). When explaining to non-Indians, describe it as a bank-to-bank instant transfer app used everywhere, even by street vendors.

examples.en: Just scan the QR code and pay by UPI.
examples.hi: बस क्यूआर कोड स्कैन कीजिए और यूपीआई से भुगतान कीजिए।

examples.en: Even the roadside vendor accepts UPI now.
examples.hi: अब सड़क किनारे का दुकानदार भी यूपीआई स्वीकार करता है।

examples.en: My UPI payment failed, can I try again?
examples.hi: मेरा यूपीआई भुगतान असफल हो गया, क्या मैं फिर से कोशिश कर सकता हूँ?

examples.en: Do you have UPI, or should I pay cash?
examples.hi: क्या आपके पास यूपीआई है, या मैं कैश दूँ?

examples.en: I set a daily limit on my UPI app for safety.
examples.hi: मैंने सुरक्षा के लिए अपने यूपीआई ऐप पर रोज़ की एक सीमा तय की है।

common_mistake.wrong: Send me money by UPI app of yours.
common_mistake.right: Send me the money through your UPI app.
common_mistake.why: Word order errors like 'app of yours' instead of 'your app' happen because Hindi possessives (तुम्हारे ऐप से) can follow the noun; English possessives must come before the noun.

cloze.sentence: I don't carry cash anymore, I pay for everything using ____.

en_def: the precise amount of money needed for a purchase, with no extra to be returned.
hi_def: खरीदारी के लिए ज़रूरी सही रकम, जिसमें वापस करने के लिए कुछ अतिरिक्त न बचे।
hi_nuance: Shopkeepers in India frequently ask 'chutta hai kya?' (do you have loose/small money?) — in English this is best phrased as 'Do you have exact change?' not 'Do you have loose money?' (that phrase describes coins/small notes generally, see 'loose change').

examples.en: Do you have exact change? I don't have a hundred-rupee note to break.
examples.hi: क्या आपके पास सही चेंज है? मेरे पास तोड़ने के लिए सौ का नोट नहीं है।

examples.en: Please keep exact change ready before boarding the bus.
examples.hi: बस में चढ़ने से पहले कृपया सही चेंज तैयार रखें।

examples.en: I always carry exact change for the auto-rickshaw fare.
examples.hi: मैं ऑटो-रिक्शा के किराए के लिए हमेशा सही चेंज साथ रखता हूँ।

examples.en: Sorry, I don't have exact change, can you break this note?
examples.hi: माफ़ कीजिए, मेरे पास सही चेंज नहीं है, क्या आप यह नोट तोड़ सकते हैं?

examples.en: The vending machine only accepts exact change.
examples.hi: वेंडिंग मशीन सिर्फ सही चेंज ही स्वीकार करती है।

common_mistake.wrong: Give me back exact change of hundred rupees.
common_mistake.right: Give me the exact change for a hundred rupees.
common_mistake.why: Indian English often uses 'of' where 'for' is correct in English money expressions, mirroring the Hindi structure सौ रुपये का चेंज।

cloze.sentence: Sorry, I only have a five-hundred rupee note, do you have ____?

en_def: small coins and low-value notes that a person carries, usually for minor purchases.
hi_def: छोटे सिक्के और कम मूल्य के नोट जो व्यक्ति छोटी-मोटी खरीदारी के लिए साथ रखता है।
hi_nuance: 'Loose change' refers generally to small coins/notes one is carrying (like coins jingling in a pocket), different from 'exact change,' which is the specific correct amount for one purchase. Hindi 'chutta' covers both meanings, which can confuse learners about which English phrase to use when.

examples.en: I always have some loose change in my pocket for the tea stall.
examples.hi: मेरे पास चाय की दुकान के लिए हमेशा कुछ खुल्ले पैसे होते हैं।

examples.en: Check if you have any loose change for the parking fee.
examples.hi: देखो कि पार्किंग शुल्क के लिए तुम्हारे पास कुछ खुल्ले पैसे हैं क्या।

examples.en: My loose change is all coins today.
examples.hi: आज मेरे खुल्ले पैसे सारे सिक्के हैं।

examples.en: He emptied his loose change onto the counter.
examples.hi: उसने अपने खुल्ले पैसे काउंटर पर उंडेल दिए।

examples.en: I keep loose change in a small purse.
examples.hi: मैं खुल्ले पैसे एक छोटे पर्स में रखता हूँ।

common_mistake.wrong: Give me loose money for hundred rupees.
common_mistake.right: Can you give me change for a hundred rupees? / Do you have some loose change?
common_mistake.why: 'Loose money' is a direct, non-idiomatic translation of खुल्ले पैसे; the standard English collocation is 'loose change' or simply 'change.'

cloze.sentence: I never have enough ____ for the rickshaw driver, always big notes.

en_def: to give back a purchased item in return for a different one, a refund, or store credit.
hi_def: खरीदी हुई वस्तु को वापस करके उसकी जगह दूसरी वस्तु, पैसे वापस, या स्टोर क्रेडिट लेना।
hi_nuance: In shops, 'exchange' (item for item) is different from 'return' (item for refund) — Indian English speakers often use 'return' and 'exchange' interchangeably even when they mean different things; a store's return policy and exchange policy can have different rules, so the distinction matters when reading terms.

examples.en: Can I exchange this shirt for a bigger size?
examples.hi: क्या मैं यह शर्ट बड़े साइज़ के लिए बदल सकता हूँ?

examples.en: The shop allows exchange within seven days with the bill.
examples.hi: दुकान बिल के साथ सात दिनों के अंदर बदलने की अनुमति देती है।

examples.en: I want to exchange this gift, it's the wrong color.
examples.hi: मैं यह तोहफा बदलना चाहता हूँ, यह गलत रंग का है।

examples.en: Sorry, we don't exchange sale items.
examples.hi: माफ़ कीजिए, हम सेल के सामान नहीं बदलते।

examples.en: He exchanged his old phone for a new model with some extra cash.
examples.hi: उसने कुछ अतिरिक्त पैसे देकर अपना पुराना फ़ोन नए मॉडल से बदल लिया।

common_mistake.wrong: I want to exchange back this shirt.
common_mistake.right: I want to exchange this shirt. / I want to return this shirt.
common_mistake.why: Learners often add 'back' unnecessarily (influenced by वापस बदलना, where वापस means 'back'), but English 'exchange' already implies giving something back, so 'back' is redundant.

cloze.sentence: This shirt doesn't fit, can I ____ it for a larger size?

en_def: a small handwritten or printed bill given by a shop as proof of a cash purchase (an old-fashioned Indian English term; the modern general term is simply 'receipt').
hi_def: दुकान द्वारा नकद खरीदारी के प्रमाण के रूप में दी जाने वाली एक छोटी हाथ से लिखी या छपी रसीद।
hi_nuance: 'Cash memo' is a very Indian, somewhat old-fashioned term still used by small shops and traditional accountants; in everyday modern English (and in most other English-speaking countries) people simply say 'receipt' or 'bill.' Younger urban Indians increasingly say 'receipt' too.

examples.en: Please give me a cash memo for this purchase.
examples.hi: कृपया इस खरीदारी की कैश मेमो दीजिए।

examples.en: Keep the cash memo safe in case you need a warranty claim.
examples.hi: वारंटी क्लेम के लिए कैश मेमो संभालकर रखें।

examples.en: The shopkeeper wrote out a cash memo by hand.
examples.hi: दुकानदार ने हाथ से कैश मेमो लिख दी।

examples.en: Without the cash memo, they won't accept a return.
examples.hi: कैश मेमो के बिना, वे वापसी स्वीकार नहीं करेंगे।

examples.en: I lost my cash memo, so I can't claim the warranty now.
examples.hi: मेरी कैश मेमो खो गई, इसलिए अब मैं वारंटी क्लेम नहीं कर सकता।

common_mistake.wrong: Give me memo of this bill.
common_mistake.right: Give me the cash memo for this purchase. / Give me the receipt.
common_mistake.why: The full fixed term is 'cash memo,' not just 'memo' (which in general English means a short office note); using 'memo' alone confuses non-Indian readers.

cloze.sentence: Please don't forget to give me the ____ for the phone case.
