examples.en: Her bag never arrived at baggage claim, so she filed a complaint.
examples.hi: उसका बैग बैगेज क्लेम पर कभी नहीं आया, इसलिए उसने शिकायत दर्ज की।

examples.en: We grabbed a trolley near baggage claim to carry all our luggage.
examples.hi: हमने सारा सामान ले जाने के लिए बैगेज क्लेम के पास एक ट्रॉली ली।

common_mistake.wrong: Go and take your baggage from luggage claim.
common_mistake.right: Go and collect your baggage from baggage claim.
common_mistake.why: Learners often mix 'baggage' and 'luggage' within the same phrase; the fixed term at airports is specifically 'baggage claim', not 'luggage claim'.

cloze.sentence: After landing, we walked straight to ____ to collect our suitcases.

en_def: a railway staff member who checks passenger tickets and berth reservations on a train
hi_def: टिकट चेकर, टीटी (ट्रेन में टिकट जाँचने वाला कर्मचारी)
hi_nuance: In India this role is often called 'TT' (Travelling Ticket Examiner) informally; learners should know 'ticket checker' or 'TTE' are the standard terms, since 'TT' alone may not be understood outside India. Some learners also say 'ticket collector', an older but still recognisable British term.

examples.en: The ticket checker asked to see everyone's ID and ticket.
examples.hi: टिकट चेकर ने सभी का पहचान पत्र और टिकट देखने को कहा।

examples.en: We showed our tickets to the ticket checker soon after boarding.
examples.hi: चढ़ने के तुरंत बाद हमने टिकट चेकर को अपने टिकट दिखाए।

examples.en: The ticket checker allotted us a confirmed berth from the waiting list.
examples.hi: टिकट चेकर ने वेटिंग लिस्ट में से हमें एक कन्फ़र्म बर्थ दे दी।

examples.en: A passenger without a ticket was fined by the ticket checker.
examples.hi: बिना टिकट वाले एक यात्री पर टिकट चेकर ने जुर्माना लगाया।

examples.en: The ticket checker walked through the compartment checking every seat.
examples.hi: टिकट चेकर डिब्बे में हर सीट जाँचते हुए चला।

collocations: show your ticket to the checker

common_mistake.wrong: TT will come and check ticket.
common_mistake.right: The ticket checker will come and check your ticket.
common_mistake.why: Indian English commonly drops articles and uses the abbreviation 'TT' directly, which non-Indian readers may not understand; standard English needs the article and full noun.

cloze.sentence: Keep your ticket ready — the ____ usually comes around after the first station.

en_def: to turn left while walking or driving
hi_def: बाईं ओर मुड़ना (चलते या गाड़ी चलाते समय बाईं तरफ़ मुड़ना)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'take left' without the article 'a', which sounds incomplete in standard English directions. In India people drive on the left side of the road, so left turns often come up more casually in daily conversation than in countries that drive on the right.

examples.en: Take a left after the temple, and the office is on your right.
examples.hi: मंदिर के बाद बाईं ओर मुड़ें, दफ़्तर आपके दाईं ओर होगा।

examples.en: Take a left at the second traffic signal to reach the mall.
examples.hi: मॉल पहुँचने के लिए दूसरे सिग्नल पर बाईं ओर मुड़ें।

examples.en: The driver was told to take a left near the flyover.
examples.hi: ड्राइवर से फ्लाईओवर के पास बाईं ओर मुड़ने को कहा गया।

examples.en: If you take a left here, you'll end up on a one-way street.
examples.hi: अगर आप यहाँ बाईं ओर मुड़ेंगे, तो एक-तरफ़ा सड़क पर पहुँच जाएँगे।

examples.en: Take a left just before the petrol pump, then go straight.
examples.hi: पेट्रोल पंप से ठीक पहले बाईं ओर मुड़ें, फिर सीधे जाएँ।

common_mistake.wrong: Take left from here.
common_mistake.right: Take a left from here.
common_mistake.why: Hindi speakers often drop the article 'a' before 'left' and 'right' in directions, which is understood but grammatically incomplete in standard English.

cloze.sentence: ____ at the next signal, and you'll see the office building.

en_def: to turn right while walking or driving
hi_def: दाईं ओर मुड़ना (चलते या गाड़ी चलाते समय दाईं तरफ़ मुड़ना)
hi_nuance: The same article-dropping issue occurs as with 'take a left'; learners also sometimes confuse 'right' (direction) with 'right' (correct), causing ambiguity in fast speech, such as 'is this right?' meaning two different things.

examples.en: Take a right just after the flyover to reach the airport road.
examples.hi: एयरपोर्ट रोड पर पहुँचने के लिए फ्लाईओवर के ठीक बाद दाईं ओर मुड़ें।

examples.en: The auto driver took a right instead of going straight, and we got lost.
examples.hi: ऑटो ड्राइवर सीधे जाने की बजाय दाईं ओर मुड़ गया, और हम रास्ता भटक गए।

examples.en: Take a right at the roundabout and continue for two kilometres.
examples.hi: गोल चक्कर पर दाईं ओर मुड़ें और दो किलोमीटर तक चलते रहें।

examples.en: If you take a right here, you will pass the petrol pump on your left.
examples.hi: अगर आप यहाँ दाईं ओर मुड़ेंगे, तो पेट्रोल पंप आपकी बाईं ओर मिलेगा।

examples.en: She told the cab driver to take a right near the mall entrance.
examples.hi: उसने कैब ड्राइवर से मॉल के प्रवेश द्वार के पास दाईं ओर मुड़ने को कहा।

common_mistake.wrong: Take right after the signal.
common_mistake.right: Take a right after the signal.
common_mistake.why: The article 'a' is often dropped before 'right' in Hindi-influenced speech; standard spoken English keeps it: 'take a right'.

cloze.sentence: ____ at the second lane, and our building is the third one on the left.

en_def: to continue moving forward without turning
hi_def: सीधे जाना (बिना मुड़े आगे बढ़ना)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes repeat 'go straight straight' for emphasis, translating a Hindi repetition pattern, which sounds odd in English; instead English says 'keep going straight' or 'go straight ahead'. Learners also sometimes confuse 'straight' with 'straight away' (meaning immediately).

examples.en: Go straight for two kilometres, then take a left at the signal.
examples.hi: दो किलोमीटर तक सीधे जाएँ, फिर सिग्नल पर बाईं ओर मुड़ें।

examples.en: Just go straight from here; you can't miss the office building.
examples.hi: बस यहाँ से सीधे जाएँ; दफ़्तर की इमारत आपसे छूटेगी नहीं।

examples.en: The driver was told to go straight until the flyover.
examples.hi: ड्राइवर से फ्लाईओवर तक सीधे जाने को कहा गया।

examples.en: Go straight past the petrol pump, and the hotel is on your right.
examples.hi: पेट्रोल पंप को पार करके सीधे जाएँ, होटल आपकी दाईं ओर होगा।

examples.en: Keep going straight along this road until you see the toll booth.
examples.hi: इस सड़क पर तब तक सीधे चलते रहें जब तक आपको टोल बूथ न दिखे।

common_mistake.wrong: Go straight straight from here.
common_mistake.right: Keep going straight from here.
common_mistake.why: Repeating 'straight' to show emphasis is a direct translation from Hindi; standard English instead says 'keep going straight' or 'go straight ahead'.

cloze.sentence: After the roundabout, just ____ for about a kilometre and you'll reach the station.

en_def: a well-known building or place used to describe a location or give directions
hi_def: लैंडमार्क, पहचान चिह्न (दिशा बताने के लिए इस्तेमाल की जाने वाली प्रसिद्ध जगह)
hi_nuance: In India, addresses commonly include landmarks because street numbering can be unreliable, which is worth explaining to foreign colleagues who may only expect a plain street address. Some learners mispronounce it with equal stress on both syllables instead of stressing the first syllable.

examples.en: The temple is a famous landmark near our office in Bengaluru.
examples.hi: मंदिर बेंगलुरु में हमारे दफ़्तर के पास का एक मशहूर लैंडमार्क है।

examples.en: Please share a nearby landmark along with your address for the delivery.
examples.hi: डिलीवरी के लिए कृपया अपने पते के साथ कोई नज़दीकी लैंडमार्क भी बताएँ।

examples.en: The tour guide pointed out several historical landmarks in Old Delhi.
examples.hi: टूर गाइड ने पुरानी दिल्ली में कई ऐतिहासिक लैंडमार्क दिखाए।

examples.en: Use the big water tank as a landmark; our house is right behind it.
examples.hi: बड़े पानी की टंकी को लैंडमार्क मानें; हमारा घर उसके ठीक पीछे है।

examples.en: Without a landmark, the delivery boy could not find our apartment.
examples.hi: बिना किसी लैंडमार्क के, डिलीवरी वाला लड़का हमारा अपार्टमेंट नहीं ढूँढ़ पाया।

common_mistake.wrong: Please give me any landmark near to your house.
common_mistake.right: Please give me a landmark near your house.
common_mistake.why: Hindi speakers often add 'near to' instead of just 'near'; in English 'near' already functions as a preposition and does not need 'to' after it.

cloze.sentence: Since there's no clear street number, please mention a nearby ____ in the address.

en_def: a turn made by a vehicle to go back in the opposite direction
hi_def: यू-टर्न (गाड़ी को घुमाकर विपरीत दिशा में ले जाना)
hi_nuance: Indian traffic rules often have designated 'no U-turn' zones and specific 'U-turn allowed' cuts on highways, so learners should mention these precisely when discussing traffic. The word is also used figuratively in Indian English, such as 'he took a U-turn on his decision', a meaning learners should recognise beyond literal driving.

examples.en: Take a U-turn after the flyover to get back onto the main road.
examples.hi: मुख्य सड़क पर वापस आने के लिए फ्लाईओवर के बाद यू-टर्न लें।

examples.en: U-turns are not allowed here; you'll have to go to the next junction.
examples.hi: यहाँ यू-टर्न की अनुमति नहीं है; आपको अगले चौराहे तक जाना होगा।

examples.en: The taxi driver made a sudden U-turn and nearly caused an accident.
examples.hi: टैक्सी ड्राइवर ने अचानक यू-टर्न लिया और लगभग दुर्घटना हो गई।

examples.en: After missing the exit, we had to take a U-turn a kilometre later.
examples.hi: एग्ज़िट छूटने के बाद, हमें एक किलोमीटर बाद यू-टर्न लेना पड़ा।

examples.en: The minister took a complete U-turn on the new toll policy.
examples.hi: मंत्री ने नई टोल नीति पर पूरी तरह यू-टर्न ले लिया।

common_mistake.wrong: Take a back turn here.
common_mistake.right: Take a U-turn here.
common_mistake.why: Learners sometimes invent the phrase 'back turn' instead of using the correct fixed term 'U-turn' for reversing direction on a road.

cloze.sentence: There's no U-turn allowed here, so we'll have to ____ at the next signal.

en_def: a set of red, yellow and green lights that controls traffic at a junction
hi_def: ट्रैफ़िक सिग्नल (चौराहे पर लाल, पीली और हरी बत्ती वाला यातायात नियंत्रण उपकरण)
hi_nuance: Indian speakers often just say 'signal' alone, such as 'wait at the signal', which is fine locally but should be expanded to 'traffic signal' or 'traffic light' when speaking to non-Indian colleagues. Saying 'the signal is red' is standard, but some learners incorrectly say 'the light is on red', translating awkwardly.

examples.en: Stop at the traffic signal; it just turned red.
examples.hi: ट्रैफ़िक सिग्नल पर रुकें; अभी लाल हुआ है।

examples.en: The traffic signal near our office is often out of order.
examples.hi: हमारे दफ़्तर के पास का ट्रैफ़िक सिग्नल अक्सर ख़राब रहता है।

examples.en: We waited almost five minutes at the traffic signal during rush hour.
examples.hi: रश आवर के दौरान हम ट्रैफ़िक सिग्नल पर लगभग पाँच मिनट रुके रहे।

examples.en: Jumping a traffic signal can get you a heavy fine in Bengaluru.
examples.hi: बेंगलुरु में ट्रैफ़िक सिग्नल तोड़ने पर भारी जुर्माना लग सकता है।

examples.en: Turn right at the next traffic signal to reach the mall.
examples.hi: मॉल पहुँचने के लिए अगले ट्रैफ़िक सिग्नल पर दाईं ओर मुड़ें।

collocations: traffic signal is out of order

common_mistake.wrong: The signal is jump by many bikes here.
common_mistake.right: Many bikes jump the traffic signal here.
common_mistake.why: Learners often construct a passive sentence incorrectly with 'jump by'; the correct active form is 'someone jumps the traffic signal'.

cloze.sentence: Please stop the car — the ____ has just turned red.

en_def: a circular junction where roads meet and traffic moves around a central island
hi_def: गोल चक्कर, राउंडअबाउट (गोलाकार चौराहा जहाँ गाड़ियाँ एक केंद्रीय द्वीप के चारों ओर घूमती हैं)
hi_nuance: Indian English commonly calls this a 'circle' (for example 'Gateway Circle') rather than 'roundabout'; both are understood locally, but 'roundabout' is the standard international term, especially in British English. American English generally says 'traffic circle'.

examples.en: Go around the roundabout and take the second exit.
examples.hi: गोल चक्कर के चारों ओर जाएँ और दूसरा एग्ज़िट लें।

examples.en: There's a big roundabout near the city centre with a fountain in the middle.
examples.hi: शहर के केंद्र के पास एक बड़ा गोल चक्कर है जिसके बीच में एक फव्वारा है।

examples.en: Traffic moves quite slowly around this roundabout during office hours.
examples.hi: दफ़्तर के समय इस गोल चक्कर के चारों ओर ट्रैफ़िक काफ़ी धीरे चलता है।

examples.en: Take the third exit at the roundabout to reach the highway.
examples.hi: हाईवे पर पहुँचने के लिए गोल चक्कर पर तीसरा एग्ज़िट लें।

examples.en: The new roundabout has reduced accidents at that busy junction.
examples.hi: नए गोल चक्कर ने उस व्यस्त चौराहे पर दुर्घटनाएँ कम कर दी हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: Turn at the circle number two.
common_mistake.right: Take the second exit at the roundabout.
common_mistake.why: Indian English often calls a roundabout a 'circle' and numbers it oddly; standard English describes movement using 'exit' numbers at a 'roundabout'.

cloze.sentence: At the ____ , take the second exit to reach the airport road.

en_def: a raised road built over another road or junction to ease traffic flow
hi_def: फ्लाईओवर (यातायात आसान बनाने के लिए दूसरी सड़क के ऊपर बनी ऊँची सड़क)
hi_nuance: 'Flyover' is British and Indian English; American English uses 'overpass', so learners writing to American colleagues should know both terms refer to the same structure. Learners should also distinguish 'flyover' (over a road) from 'bridge' (over water or a valley), a distinction some blur.

examples.en: Take the flyover to avoid the traffic jam below.
examples.hi: नीचे के ट्रैफ़िक जाम से बचने के लिए फ्लाईओवर लें।

examples.en: The new flyover has cut our commute time by twenty minutes.
examples.hi: नए फ्लाईओवर ने हमारे सफ़र का समय बीस मिनट कम कर दिया है।

examples.en: We got stuck under the flyover because of waterlogging.
examples.hi: जलभराव के कारण हम फ्लाईओवर के नीचे फँस गए।

examples.en: Turn left just before the flyover to reach the mall.
examples.hi: मॉल पहुँचने के लिए फ्लाईओवर से ठीक पहले बाईं ओर मुड़ें।

examples.en: The flyover connects the airport road directly to the highway.
examples.hi: फ्लाईओवर एयरपोर्ट रोड को सीधे हाईवे से जोड़ता है।

common_mistake.wrong: We are stuck below the overbridge.
common_mistake.right: We are stuck under the flyover.
common_mistake.why: 'Overbridge' is a literal Hindi-influenced translation; the standard English term for a raised road over traffic is 'flyover' (British/Indian) or 'overpass' (American).

cloze.sentence: Take the ____ instead of the main road; it's much faster during rush hour.

en_def: a road or path that goes underneath another road, railway or junction
hi_def: अंडरपास (एक सड़क या मार्ग जो दूसरी सड़क या रेल पटरी के नीचे से जाता है)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes confuse 'underpass' (for vehicles or pedestrians) with 'subway', which in American English means an underground train system but in British English means an underground pedestrian passage — a genuine source of confusion for Indian learners who use 'subway' loosely for metro-like systems.

examples.en: Use the underpass to cross the highway safely.
examples.hi: हाईवे को सुरक्षित रूप से पार करने के लिए अंडरपास का इस्तेमाल करें।

examples.en: The new underpass has reduced traffic near the railway crossing.
examples.hi: नए अंडरपास ने रेलवे क्रॉसिंग के पास ट्रैफ़िक कम कर दिया है।

examples.en: We waited in the underpass until the rain stopped.
examples.hi: बारिश रुकने तक हम अंडरपास में इंतज़ार करते रहे।

examples.en: Cyclists are not allowed to use the pedestrian underpass here.
examples.hi: यहाँ साइकिल चालकों को पैदल यात्री अंडरपास इस्तेमाल करने की अनुमति नहीं है।

examples.en: The underpass floods every monsoon because of poor drainage.
examples.hi: ख़राब जल निकासी के कारण अंडरपास में हर मानसून में पानी भर जाता है।

common_mistake.wrong: Take the subway to cross the road, not the metro.
common_mistake.right: Take the underpass to cross the road.
common_mistake.why: Indian learners sometimes call a pedestrian underpass a 'subway', but in American English 'subway' means an underground train, which can confuse international listeners; 'underpass' is unambiguous.

cloze.sentence: Instead of crossing the busy road, use the ____ near the station.

en_def: to leave someone at a particular place, usually by vehicle
hi_def: मुझे ... पर छोड़ना (गाड़ी से किसी को किसी स्थान पर उतारना)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often say 'please drop me' without adding 'at + place', which sounds incomplete in English. This 'drop' is unrelated to 'drop' meaning to fall, though beginners sometimes worry it sounds like abandoning someone; the harsher-sounding 'leave me at' is also sometimes confused with this phrase.

examples.en: Can you drop me at the metro station on your way to office?
examples.hi: क्या तुम दफ़्तर जाते समय मुझे मेट्रो स्टेशन पर छोड़ सकते हो?

examples.en: Please drop me at the next signal; I'll walk from there.
examples.hi: कृपया मुझे अगले सिग्नल पर छोड़ दो; मैं वहाँ से पैदल चला जाऊँगा।

examples.en: My father usually drops me at the railway station before his own commute.
examples.hi: मेरे पिता आमतौर पर अपने दफ़्तर जाने से पहले मुझे रेलवे स्टेशन पर छोड़ते हैं।

examples.en: Could you drop me at the airport by six o'clock tomorrow?
examples.hi: क्या तुम मुझे कल छह बजे तक एयरपोर्ट पर छोड़ सकते हो?

examples.en: The cab driver agreed to drop me at the office gate directly.
examples.hi: कैब ड्राइवर मुझे सीधे दफ़्तर के गेट पर छोड़ने के लिए राज़ी हो गया।

common_mistake.wrong: Please drop me.
common_mistake.right: Please drop me at the station.
common_mistake.why: Hindi speakers often omit the destination, but English 'drop' requires a location ('drop me at/off at + place') to sound complete and natural.

cloze.sentence: Could you please ____ the next junction? I'll take an auto from there.

en_def: to collect someone from a place by vehicle
hi_def: मुझे लेने आना (गाड़ी से किसी को किसी स्थान से लेना)
hi_nuance: This is a separable phrasal verb, and learners often place the object incorrectly, saying 'pick up me' instead of 'pick me up'. It is also easily confused with 'pick up' meaning to lift an object, rather than to collect a person.

examples.en: Can you pick me up from the airport tonight around ten?
examples.hi: क्या तुम आज रात लगभग दस बजे मुझे एयरपोर्ट से लेने आ सकते हो?

examples.en: My colleague will pick me up from home before the meeting.
examples.hi: मीटिंग से पहले मेरा सहकर्मी मुझे घर से लेने आएगा।

examples.en: I asked the cab driver to pick me up exactly at seven.
examples.hi: मैंने कैब ड्राइवर से ठीक सात बजे मुझे लेने आने को कहा।

examples.en: She usually gets her brother to pick her up after office.
examples.hi: वह आमतौर पर दफ़्तर के बाद अपने भाई से खुद को लेने बुलवाती है।

examples.en: Please pick me up near the main gate, not the back entrance.
examples.hi: कृपया मुझे मुख्य गेट के पास लेने आना, पिछले दरवाज़े पर नहीं।

common_mistake.wrong: Please pick up me from the station.
common_mistake.right: Please pick me up from the station.
common_mistake.why: 'Pick up' is a separable phrasal verb, and with a pronoun object like 'me', it must go in the middle: 'pick me up', not after 'up'.

cloze.sentence: My sister will ____ from the bus stand at nine tonight.

en_def: a three-wheeled auto-rickshaw that carries multiple unrelated passengers on a fixed route for a shared fare
hi_def: शेयर्ड ऑटो (तय रूट पर कई अलग-अलग यात्रियों को ले जाने वाला ऑटो-रिक्शा, जिसका किराया बँटा होता है)
hi_nuance: This is a distinctly Indian transport concept; learners should describe it to foreigners as similar to a 'shared taxi' since there's no single universal English word for it. Learners sometimes just say 'auto' assuming it's understood as shared, when autos in some cities are private unless specified as 'shared'.

examples.en: I took a shared auto to the station to save money.
examples.hi: मैंने पैसे बचाने के लिए स्टेशन तक शेयर्ड ऑटो लिया।

examples.en: The shared auto only leaves once it has four passengers.
examples.hi: शेयर्ड ऑटो तभी चलता है जब उसमें चार यात्री हो जाते हैं।

examples.en: We squeezed into a shared auto with two other office-goers.
examples.hi: हम दो और दफ़्तर जाने वालों के साथ एक शेयर्ड ऑटो में घुस गए।

examples.en: A shared auto is much cheaper than booking a private cab.
examples.hi: शेयर्ड ऑटो प्राइवेट कैब बुक करने से कहीं सस्ता है।

examples.en: Shared autos on this route charge a fixed fare of twenty rupees.
examples.hi: इस रूट पर शेयर्ड ऑटो बीस रुपये का तय किराया लेते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: I took auto sharing to office.
common_mistake.right: I took a shared auto to office.
common_mistake.why: Learners often reverse the word order, saying 'auto sharing' instead of the correct adjective-noun order 'shared auto'.

cloze.sentence: Instead of a private cab, we hopped into a ____ to save time and money.

en_def: a designated place where auto-rickshaws wait to pick up passengers
hi_def: ऑटो स्टैंड (वह जगह जहाँ ऑटो-रिक्शा यात्रियों को लेने के लिए खड़े रहते हैं)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'auto stop' instead of 'auto stand'; 'stand' (a fixed waiting place) is correct, while 'stop' usually refers to a bus stop where vehicles pause briefly rather than wait. This distinction between 'stand' and 'stop' is a frequent source of error.

examples.en: There's always an auto stand right outside our office gate.
examples.hi: हमारे दफ़्तर के गेट के ठीक बाहर हमेशा एक ऑटो स्टैंड होता है।

examples.en: We walked to the nearest auto stand to find a ride home.
examples.hi: हम घर जाने की सवारी ढूँढ़ने के लिए सबसे नज़दीकी ऑटो स्टैंड तक गए।

examples.en: The auto stand near the station is busiest in the evening.
examples.hi: स्टेशन के पास वाला ऑटो स्टैंड शाम को सबसे ज़्यादा व्यस्त रहता है।

examples.en: No autos were available at the auto stand during the strike.
examples.hi: हड़ताल के दौरान ऑटो स्टैंड पर कोई ऑटो उपलब्ध नहीं था।

examples.en: I asked the guard where the closest auto stand was.
examples.hi: मैंने गार्ड से पूछा कि सबसे नज़दीकी ऑटो स्टैंड कहाँ है।

common_mistake.wrong: Meet me at the auto stop near the mall.
common_mistake.right: Meet me at the auto stand near the mall.
common_mistake.why: Learners confuse 'stand' (a fixed waiting area for vehicles) with 'stop' (a brief pause point); autos wait at a 'stand', buses pause at a 'stop'.

cloze.sentence: Wait for me at the ____ outside the mall; I'll be there in ten minutes.

en_def: charging a fare according to the reading on a taxi's or auto's fare meter, rather than a fixed negotiated price
hi_def: मीटर से (टैक्सी या ऑटो का किराया मीटर की रीडिंग के अनुसार लिया जाना)
hi_nuance: In many Indian cities, auto drivers often refuse to go 'on the meter' and instead negotiate a fixed price, which frustrates commuters and is a common complaint topic. Saying 'by the meter' instead of 'on the meter' is a common preposition error, translating the Hindi phrase 'मीटर से' too literally.

examples.en: Please go on the meter; I don't want to negotiate a fare.
examples.hi: कृपया मीटर से चलें; मैं किराया मोलभाव नहीं करना चाहता।

examples.en: The driver refused to go on the meter during peak hours.
examples.hi: व्यस्त समय में ड्राइवर ने मीटर से चलने से मना कर दिया।

examples.en: Most app-based cabs always charge on the meter automatically.
examples.hi: ज़्यादातर ऐप-आधारित कैब हमेशा अपने आप मीटर के हिसाब से किराया लेती हैं।

examples.en: I insisted the auto driver go on the meter instead of charging a flat rate.
examples.hi: मैंने ऑटो ड्राइवर से ज़िद की कि वह तय किराए की बजाय मीटर से चले।

examples.en: It's illegal for auto drivers to refuse to go on the meter in this city.
examples.hi: इस शहर में ऑटो ड्राइवरों का मीटर से चलने से मना करना ग़ैरकानूनी है।

common_mistake.wrong: Please go by the meter, not by fixed price.
common_mistake.right: Please go on the meter, not for a fixed price.
common_mistake.why: The fixed preposition in this expression is 'on', not 'by'; Hindi speakers often substitute 'by' from translating 'मीटर से'.

cloze.sentence: I always ask the auto driver to go ____ instead of quoting a random fare.

en_def: the money a passenger pays to travel by bus, train, taxi or auto
hi_def: किराया (बस, ट्रेन, टैक्सी या ऑटो में यात्रा के लिए दिया जाने वाला पैसा)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes confuse 'fare' (travel cost) with 'fair' (just or reasonable), which sound identical; this homophone confusion is common in writing. Note also that 'fare' is not used for house rent or shopping prices, only for transport.

examples.en: The auto fare from my house to the office is about eighty rupees.
examples.hi: मेरे घर से दफ़्तर तक ऑटो का किराया लगभग अस्सी रुपये है।

examples.en: Train fares increase slightly during the festival season.
examples.hi: त्योहारों के मौसम में ट्रेन का किराया थोड़ा बढ़ जाता है।

examples.en: We split the cab fare four ways among the colleagues.
examples.hi: हमने सहकर्मियों के बीच कैब का किराया चार हिस्सों में बाँटा।

examples.en: The fare from the airport to the city can be quite high at night.
examples.hi: रात में एयरपोर्ट से शहर तक का किराया काफ़ी ज़्यादा हो सकता है।

examples.en: Please check the fare before boarding a shared auto.
examples.hi: शेयर्ड ऑटो में चढ़ने से पहले कृपया किराया जाँच लें।

common_mistake.wrong: The fair to the station is fifty rupees.
common_mistake.right: The fare to the station is fifty rupees.
common_mistake.why: 'Fare' (travel cost) and 'fair' (just, or a carnival) sound identical but have completely different spellings and meanings.

cloze.sentence: The auto ____ from the airport to my flat comes to around three hundred rupees.

en_def: a fee paid to use certain roads, highways or bridges
hi_def: टोल (कुछ सड़कों, हाईवे या पुलों के इस्तेमाल के लिए दिया जाने वाला शुल्क)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'toll tax', a common Indian English redundancy, since 'toll' already implies a fee; international English usually just says 'toll'. FASTag-related vocabulary for electronic toll collection is now common in Indian conversation and worth learning alongside this word.

examples.en: We paid the toll twice on our drive from Mumbai to Pune.
examples.hi: मुंबई से पुणे तक की ड्राइव में हमने दो बार टोल चुकाया।

examples.en: The FASTag automatically deducts the toll as you pass through.
examples.hi: जैसे ही आप गुज़रते हैं, FASTag अपने आप टोल काट लेता है।

examples.en: Long queues form at the toll booth during holiday weekends.
examples.hi: छुट्टियों के सप्ताहांत में टोल बूथ पर लंबी लाइनें लग जाती हैं।

examples.en: This highway has three toll points between the two cities.
examples.hi: इस हाईवे पर दोनों शहरों के बीच तीन टोल पॉइंट हैं।

examples.en: The toll increased slightly after the road was widened.
examples.hi: सड़क चौड़ी होने के बाद टोल थोड़ा बढ़ गया।

common_mistake.wrong: We had to pay toll tax three times.
common_mistake.right: We had to pay the toll three times.
common_mistake.why: 'Toll' already means a fee for using a road, so adding 'tax' after it is redundant; standard English simply says 'pay the toll'.

cloze.sentence: Make sure your FASTag has enough balance before you reach the ____ plaza.

en_def: a long line of vehicles that cannot move because of heavy traffic
hi_def: ट्रैफ़िक जाम (भारी यातायात के कारण गाड़ियों का लंबे समय तक न चल पाना)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'traffic' alone to mean a jam, which is understood, but the specific phrase 'traffic jam' is clearer for describing being completely stuck. The word 'jam' is also sometimes confused with the fruit spread of the same name, a common source of jokes among learners.

examples.en: We got stuck in a traffic jam for almost an hour near the flyover.
examples.hi: हम फ्लाईओवर के पास लगभग एक घंटे तक ट्रैफ़िक जाम में फँसे रहे।

examples.en: The traffic jam on the outer ring road made me late for the meeting.
examples.hi: आउटर रिंग रोड के ट्रैफ़िक जाम की वजह से मुझे मीटिंग के लिए देर हो गई।

examples.en: Heavy rain always causes a massive traffic jam in this city.
examples.hi: भारी बारिश इस शहर में हमेशा बहुत बड़ा ट्रैफ़िक जाम लगा देती है।

examples.en: I left home early today to avoid the morning traffic jam.
examples.hi: मैं आज सुबह के ट्रैफ़िक जाम से बचने के लिए घर से जल्दी निकला।

examples.en: The accident caused a long traffic jam on the highway.
examples.hi: दुर्घटना के कारण हाईवे पर लंबा ट्रैफ़िक जाम लग गया।

common_mistake.wrong: There is too much jam on this road.
common_mistake.right: There is a huge traffic jam on this road.
common_mistake.why: Learners sometimes drop 'traffic' and just say 'jam', which without context might be misread as the fruit spread; the full phrase 'traffic jam' avoids ambiguity.

cloze.sentence: We were stuck in a ____ for almost two hours on the way to the airport.

en_def: the time of day when traffic is heaviest, usually when people travel to or from work
hi_def: रश आवर, व्यस्त समय (जब यातायात सबसे ज़्यादा होता है, आमतौर पर ऑफ़िस आने-जाने के समय)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'office time' or 'peak time' instead of 'rush hour'; while these are understandable, 'rush hour' is the standard international term. It is used even when the busy period lasts more than one hour, such as a morning rush hour spanning two or three hours.

examples.en: I try to avoid travelling during rush hour whenever possible.
examples.hi: मैं जितना हो सके रश आवर में सफ़र करने से बचने की कोशिश करता हूँ।

examples.en: The roads near my office are terrible during the evening rush hour.
examples.hi: शाम के रश आवर में मेरे दफ़्तर के पास की सड़कों की हालत बहुत ख़राब होती है।

examples.en: Rush hour in Bengaluru can last from eight until almost eleven in the morning.
examples.hi: बेंगलुरु में रश आवर सुबह आठ बजे से लगभग ग्यारह बजे तक चल सकता है।

examples.en: We left an hour early to beat the rush hour traffic.
examples.hi: हम रश आवर के ट्रैफ़िक से बचने के लिए एक घंटा पहले निकले।

examples.en: Metro trains are extremely crowded during rush hour.
examples.hi: रश आवर के दौरान मेट्रो ट्रेनें बहुत ज़्यादा भरी होती हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: Office time traffic is very bad here.
common_mistake.right: Rush hour traffic is very bad here.
common_mistake.why: Learners often say 'office time' as a literal translation of local usage; the standard English term for this busy commuting period is 'rush hour'.

cloze.sentence: Try not to leave the office during ____ ; the roads are impossible then.

en_def: a quicker or more direct route than the usual one
hi_def: शॉर्टकट (सामान्य रास्ते से जल्दी या सीधा पहुँचने वाला रास्ता)
hi_nuance: The word is usually spelled as one word 'shortcut' in standard English, though learners sometimes write it as two words 'short cut'; one word is more common for describing a route. It is also used figuratively, as in 'a shortcut to success', a sense learners should recognise beyond roads.

examples.en: The auto driver took a shortcut through the narrow lanes.
examples.hi: ऑटो ड्राइवर संकरी गलियों से होकर शॉर्टकट ले गया।

examples.en: There's a shortcut behind the temple that saves ten minutes.
examples.hi: मंदिर के पीछे एक शॉर्टकट है जिससे दस मिनट बच जाते हैं।

examples.en: We missed the shortcut and had to go the long way round.
examples.hi: हमसे शॉर्टकट छूट गया और हमें लंबे रास्ते से जाना पड़ा।

examples.en: Locals know a shortcut that avoids the main traffic jam.
examples.hi: स्थानीय लोग एक ऐसा शॉर्टकट जानते हैं जिससे मुख्य ट्रैफ़िक जाम से बचा जा सकता है।

examples.en: Taking that shortcut can be risky at night because it's poorly lit.
examples.hi: रात में वह शॉर्टकट लेना जोखिम भरा हो सकता है क्योंकि वहाँ रोशनी कम है।

common_mistake.wrong: Let's go by short way.
common_mistake.right: Let's take a shortcut.
common_mistake.why: Learners sometimes invent 'short way' as a direct translation; the correct, natural English noun for a quicker route is 'shortcut'.

cloze.sentence: The driver knew a ____ that saved us almost fifteen minutes in traffic.

en_def: to send someone your current position through a phone app or message so they can find you or track your route
hi_def: अपनी लोकेशन शेयर करना (फ़ोन ऐप से किसी को अपनी वर्तमान स्थिति भेजना)
hi_nuance: This is a very common safety habit in India, especially for solo travellers and women travelling late at night; a security-conscious learner should know the natural phrasing 'I'll share my location with you' rather than the slightly less natural 'I will send my location'. Some learners also drop the possessive 'my', which is fine in app UI text but less natural in full sentences.

examples.en: I always share my location with my wife when I take a cab alone at night.
examples.hi: जब मैं रात में अकेले कैब लेता हूँ, तो हमेशा अपनी पत्नी के साथ अपनी लोकेशन शेयर करता हूँ।

examples.en: Can you share your location so I know exactly where to pick you up?
examples.hi: क्या तुम अपनी लोकेशन शेयर कर सकते हो ताकि मुझे पता चले कि तुम्हें कहाँ से लेना है?

examples.en: She shared her location with her father before boarding the late train.
examples.hi: देर रात की ट्रेन में चढ़ने से पहले उसने अपनी लोकेशन अपने पिता के साथ शेयर की।

examples.en: I shared my location on WhatsApp in case the driver took a wrong turn.
examples.hi: मैंने व्हाट्सऐप पर अपनी लोकेशन शेयर की, ताकि अगर ड्राइवर गलत मुड़ जाए तो पता चल सके।

examples.en: For safety, always share your location when travelling alone late at night.
examples.hi: सुरक्षा के लिए, देर रात अकेले सफ़र करते समय हमेशा अपनी लोकेशन शेयर करें।

common_mistake.wrong: I am sending you my location live.
common_mistake.right: I am sharing my live location with you.
common_mistake.why: Learners often say 'sending... live', which sounds unnatural; the standard, natural collocation used in messaging apps is 'sharing my live location'.

cloze.sentence: For safety, I always ____ with my family whenever I travel alone at night.

en_def: the incorrect direction, especially driving against the flow of traffic on a one-way road
hi_def: गलत रास्ता, उल्टी दिशा (विशेषकर एक-तरफ़ा सड़क पर विपरीत दिशा में गाड़ी चलाना)
hi_nuance: In Indian traffic contexts, 'wrong side driving' is a very common local phrase that isn't standard international English; the correct phrase is 'driving the wrong way' or 'going the wrong way'. Learners should be aware this local phrase might confuse non-Indian listeners.

examples.en: That biker is going the wrong way on this one-way street.
examples.hi: वह बाइक सवार इस एक-तरफ़ा सड़क पर उल्टी दिशा में जा रहा है।

examples.en: We realised we were driving the wrong way and had to turn back.
examples.hi: हमें एहसास हुआ कि हम गलत रास्ते पर गाड़ी चला रहे थे और हमें वापस मुड़ना पड़ा।

examples.en: The policeman stopped him for going the wrong way near the flyover.
examples.hi: पुलिसवाले ने फ्लाईओवर के पास उसे उल्टी दिशा में जाने पर रोका।

examples.en: Please don't drive the wrong way just to save two minutes.
examples.hi: कृपया केवल दो मिनट बचाने के लिए गलत दिशा में गाड़ी मत चलाओ।

examples.en: We took the wrong way and ended up near the railway station instead.
examples.hi: हम गलत रास्ते पर चले गए और इसके बजाय रेलवे स्टेशन के पास पहुँच गए।

common_mistake.wrong: He is driving in wrong side.
common_mistake.right: He is driving the wrong way.
common_mistake.why: Indian English commonly uses 'wrong side driving' as a fixed local phrase, but standard English expresses this as 'driving the wrong way' or 'going the wrong way'.

cloze.sentence: The traffic police stopped him for going the ____ down a one-way street.

en_def: a street on which vehicles may only travel in a single direction
hi_def: एक-तरफ़ा सड़क (जिस सड़क पर गाड़ियाँ केवल एक ही दिशा में जा सकती हैं)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'one side road' instead of 'one-way street'; the hyphenated compound adjective 'one-way' is the correct standard form before 'street' or 'road'. Note that some Indian one-way streets are poorly marked, leading to genuine driver confusion, a good real-life talking point.

examples.en: This is a one-way street, so we can't enter from this side.
examples.hi: यह एक-तरफ़ा सड़क है, इसलिए हम इस तरफ़ से अंदर नहीं जा सकते।

examples.en: I didn't notice the sign and drove into a one-way street the wrong way.
examples.hi: मैंने बोर्ड नहीं देखा और एक-तरफ़ा सड़क पर उल्टी दिशा में गाड़ी घुसा दी।

examples.en: The market area has several narrow one-way streets.
examples.hi: बाज़ार के इलाके में कई संकरी एक-तरफ़ा सड़कें हैं।

examples.en: Turning here is illegal because it's a one-way street.
examples.hi: यहाँ मुड़ना गैरकानूनी है क्योंकि यह एक-तरफ़ा सड़क है।

examples.en: Delivery trucks often block this one-way street during the day.
examples.hi: दिन में डिलीवरी ट्रक अक्सर इस एक-तरफ़ा सड़क को जाम कर देते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: This road is one side only.
common_mistake.right: This is a one-way street.
common_mistake.why: Learners often translate 'एक तरफ़ा' as 'one side only'; the correct standard English compound term is 'one-way street' or 'one-way road'.

cloze.sentence: You can't turn right here — it's a ____ going the other direction.

en_def: a rule or sign indicating that vehicles must not be parked in a particular area
hi_def: नो पार्किंग (उस क्षेत्र में वाहन खड़ा करने की मनाही का संकेत या नियम)
hi_nuance: Learners generally use this phrase correctly since it's a widely seen sign in India, but some incorrectly reorder the words, such as saying 'parking is no'; the fixed sign phrase must stay as 'no parking'. Fines for violating 'no parking' zones are a very common everyday topic for drivers.

examples.en: You can't leave the car here; it's a no parking zone.
examples.hi: तुम यहाँ गाड़ी नहीं छोड़ सकते; यह नो पार्किंग ज़ोन है।

examples.en: The traffic police towed my bike from a no parking area.
examples.hi: ट्रैफ़िक पुलिस मेरी बाइक को नो पार्किंग वाली जगह से खींच ले गई।

examples.en: There's a big no parking sign right outside the building.
examples.hi: इमारत के ठीक बाहर एक बड़ा नो पार्किंग बोर्ड लगा है।

examples.en: We got fined for ignoring the no parking sign near the market.
examples.hi: बाज़ार के पास नो पार्किंग बोर्ड को नज़रअंदाज़ करने पर हमें जुर्माना हुआ।

examples.en: Please don't stop here for even a minute; it's strictly no parking.
examples.hi: कृपया यहाँ एक मिनट के लिए भी मत रुको; यहाँ सख़्ती से नो पार्किंग है।

common_mistake.wrong: Here parking is not.
common_mistake.right: This is a no parking zone.
common_mistake.why: Learners sometimes construct a literal word-for-word translation from Hindi; the fixed English sign phrase is simply 'no parking', used as a set noun phrase, not built from a full sentence.

cloze.sentence: Don't stop the car here — see that ____ sign on the wall?

en_def: a strap in a vehicle that holds a passenger safely in their seat
hi_def: सीट बेल्ट (गाड़ी में यात्री को सुरक्षित रखने वाली पट्टी)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes write 'seat belt' as one word 'seatbelt', which is also acceptable in some dictionaries, but the two-word form is more common in Indian usage. A common mistake is saying 'wear seat belt' without an article or possessive; 'wear your seat belt' is more natural.

examples.en: Please wear your seat belt before the car starts moving.
examples.hi: गाड़ी चलने से पहले कृपया अपनी सीट बेल्ट पहन लें।

examples.en: The traffic police fined him for not wearing a seat belt.
examples.hi: सीट बेल्ट न पहनने पर ट्रैफ़िक पुलिस ने उस पर जुर्माना लगाया।

examples.en: Make sure the children's seat belts are fastened properly.
examples.hi: सुनिश्चित करें कि बच्चों की सीट बेल्ट ठीक से बंधी हो।

examples.en: I always check my seat belt before starting a long drive.
examples.hi: लंबी ड्राइव शुरू करने से पहले मैं हमेशा अपनी सीट बेल्ट जाँचता हूँ।

examples.en: The car beeps loudly if you don't fasten your seat belt.
examples.hi: अगर आप सीट बेल्ट नहीं बाँधते तो गाड़ी ज़ोर से बीप करती है।

common_mistake.wrong: Please wear seat belt.
common_mistake.right: Please wear your seat belt.
common_mistake.why: Learners often drop the possessive 'your' before 'seat belt', which sounds incomplete; standard English usually includes 'your' or 'a' before the noun.

cloze.sentence: The moment you get into the car, please fasten your ____ .

en_def: a hard protective covering worn on the head, especially by riders of two-wheelers
hi_def: हेलमेट (सिर की सुरक्षा के लिए पहना जाने वाला कठोर आवरण, विशेषकर दोपहिया चलाते समय)
hi_nuance: Learners generally use this word correctly since it's widely known, but common errors include forgetting the article, saying 'I forgot helmet' instead of 'I forgot my helmet'. Learners also sometimes confuse 'wear a helmet' with 'put a helmet', where 'wear' is the standard verb for protective gear.

examples.en: Wearing a helmet is compulsory for both the rider and the pillion in many states.
examples.hi: कई राज्यों में चालक और पीछे बैठने वाले दोनों के लिए हेलमेट पहनना ज़रूरी है।

examples.en: I always keep a spare helmet for my friend when he rides with me.
examples.hi: जब मेरा दोस्त मेरे साथ बाइक पर बैठता है, तो मैं हमेशा उसके लिए एक अतिरिक्त हेलमेट रखता हूँ।

examples.en: The traffic police stopped him for riding without a helmet.
examples.hi: बिना हेलमेट के बाइक चलाने पर ट्रैफ़िक पुलिस ने उसे रोका।

examples.en: She bought a new helmet after her old one cracked in an accident.
examples.hi: दुर्घटना में उसका पुराना हेलमेट टूटने के बाद उसने नया हेलमेट खरीदा।

examples.en: Please put on your helmet before we start the bike.
examples.hi: बाइक स्टार्ट करने से पहले कृपया अपना हेलमेट पहन लो।

common_mistake.wrong: He was riding without helmet.
common_mistake.right: He was riding without a helmet.
common_mistake.why: Learners frequently drop the article 'a' before a singular countable noun like 'helmet'; standard English requires it here.

cloze.sentence: It's illegal to ride a two-wheeler without wearing a ____ .

en_def: an official document that permits a person to legally drive a vehicle
hi_def: ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस (गाड़ी चलाने की कानूनी अनुमति देने वाला आधिकारिक दस्तावेज़)
hi_nuance: British English spells it 'driving licence' as a noun, while American English uses 'license' for both noun and verb; Indian English generally follows the American spelling 'license' in everyday writing despite otherwise following British conventions. Learners also sometimes drop 'driving' and just say 'license', which can be ambiguous with other kinds of permits.

examples.en: I renewed my driving license last month at the RTO.
examples.hi: मैंने पिछले महीने RTO में अपना ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस रिन्यू करवाया।

examples.en: Never drive without carrying your driving license and vehicle papers.
examples.hi: अपना ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस और गाड़ी के कागज़ात साथ लिए बिना कभी गाड़ी मत चलाओ।

examples.en: She applied for a learner's driving license before taking lessons.
examples.hi: उसने ड्राइविंग सीखने से पहले लर्नर ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस के लिए आवेदन किया।

examples.en: The policeman asked to see my driving license at the checkpoint.
examples.hi: चेकपॉइंट पर पुलिसवाले ने मेरा ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस देखने को कहा।

examples.en: You need a valid driving license to rent a car in most cities.
examples.hi: ज़्यादातर शहरों में गाड़ी किराए पर लेने के लिए वैध ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस चाहिए।

common_mistake.wrong: Show me your license, not the driving one.
common_mistake.right: Show me your driving license.
common_mistake.why: Learners sometimes drop 'driving' assuming 'license' alone is unambiguous, but in many contexts 'license' could mean other permits; specifying 'driving license' avoids confusion.

cloze.sentence: You must always carry your ____ and the vehicle registration papers while driving.

en_def: the official documents, such as the registration certificate, insurance and pollution certificate, that must be carried while driving a vehicle
hi_def: गाड़ी के कागज़ात (गाड़ी चलाते समय साथ रखे जाने वाले पंजीकरण, बीमा आदि दस्तावेज़)
hi_nuance: This is a distinctly Indian collocation covering the registration certificate, insurance and PUC together; learners should know that internationally this would usually be broken into specific terms like 'registration certificate' rather than the single umbrella phrase 'vehicle papers'. Some learners write 'car papers', which is understood but 'vehicle papers' is the more formal, general term covering all vehicle types.

examples.en: The traffic police asked to check my vehicle papers at the checkpoint.
examples.hi: चेकपॉइंट पर ट्रैफ़िक पुलिस ने मेरे गाड़ी के कागज़ात जाँचने को कहा।

examples.en: Always keep your vehicle papers and driving license together in the car.
examples.hi: अपने गाड़ी के कागज़ात और ड्राइविंग लाइसेंस हमेशा गाड़ी में एक साथ रखें।

examples.en: His vehicle papers were not in order, so he was fined at the toll booth.
examples.hi: उसके गाड़ी के कागज़ात ठीक नहीं थे, इसलिए टोल बूथ पर उस पर जुर्माना लगाया गया।

examples.en: I keep digital copies of all my vehicle papers on my phone.
examples.hi: मैं अपने सभी गाड़ी के कागज़ातों की डिजिटल प्रतियाँ अपने फ़ोन में रखता हूँ।

examples.en: The insurance agent asked us to submit copies of the vehicle papers.
examples.hi: बीमा एजेंट ने हमसे गाड़ी के कागज़ातों की प्रतियाँ जमा करने को कहा।

common_mistake.wrong: Police checked my car's paper.
common_mistake.right: The police checked my vehicle papers.
common_mistake.why: Learners often use the singular 'paper' and possessive 'car's' instead of the correct plural collocation 'vehicle papers', which is the standard fixed phrase.

cloze.sentence: Make sure you carry all your ____ before you start the road trip.

en_def: a small hole in a tyre that causes it to lose air, often from a sharp object on the road
hi_def: पंक्चर (टायर में छोटा छेद जिससे हवा निकल जाती है)
hi_nuance: Learners commonly use 'puncture' as both noun and verb correctly in Indian English, similar to British English; American English tends to prefer 'flat tire' more often than 'puncture' as a noun. Learners should know both are understood but 'flat tire' is more common in the US.

examples.en: We got a puncture on the highway right before the toll booth.
examples.hi: टोल बूथ से ठीक पहले हाईवे पर हमारा टायर पंक्चर हो गया।

examples.en: The mechanic fixed the puncture in about fifteen minutes.
examples.hi: मैकेनिक ने लगभग पंद्रह मिनट में पंक्चर ठीक कर दिया।

examples.en: I always carry a puncture repair kit on long bike trips.
examples.hi: लंबी बाइक यात्राओं में मैं हमेशा पंक्चर मरम्मत किट साथ रखता हूँ।

examples.en: A nail on the road caused the puncture in my rear tyre.
examples.hi: सड़क पर पड़ी एक कील की वजह से मेरे पिछले टायर में पंक्चर हो गया।

examples.en: We had to push the bike to the nearest puncture shop.
examples.hi: हमें बाइक को धकेलकर सबसे नज़दीकी पंक्चर की दुकान तक ले जाना पड़ा।

common_mistake.wrong: My tyre is flat because of punchar.
common_mistake.right: My tyre has a puncture.
common_mistake.why: Learners sometimes misspell 'puncture' phonetically as 'punchar'; the correct spelling and usual construction is 'have/get a puncture'.

cloze.sentence: We had to stop by the roadside because of a ____ in the front tyre.

en_def: a place where vehicles are filled with petrol or diesel fuel
hi_def: पेट्रोल पंप (जहाँ गाड़ियों में पेट्रोल या डीज़ल भरा जाता है)
hi_nuance: British and Indian English says 'petrol pump' or 'petrol station'; American English says 'gas station' and uses 'gas' instead of 'petrol'. A learner talking to American colleagues should recognise 'gas station' refers to the same place, not natural gas.

examples.en: Let's stop at the next petrol pump; the tank is almost empty.
examples.hi: चलो अगले पेट्रोल पंप पर रुकते हैं; टंकी लगभग खाली है।

examples.en: The petrol pump near our office also has an air-filling facility.
examples.hi: हमारे दफ़्तर के पास वाले पेट्रोल पंप पर हवा भरने की सुविधा भी है।

examples.en: We waited in a long queue at the petrol pump during the fuel shortage.
examples.hi: ईंधन की कमी के दौरान हम पेट्रोल पंप पर लंबी लाइन में खड़े रहे।

examples.en: I always fill up at the same petrol pump on my way to work.
examples.hi: मैं दफ़्तर जाते समय हमेशा उसी पेट्रोल पंप पर टंकी भरवाता हूँ।

examples.en: There's no petrol pump for the next twenty kilometres on this highway.
examples.hi: इस हाईवे पर अगले बीस किलोमीटर तक कोई पेट्रोल पंप नहीं है।

collocations: fill up at a petrol pump

common_mistake.wrong: Let's stop at the gas pump for petrol.
common_mistake.right: Let's stop at the petrol pump.
common_mistake.why: Learners sometimes mix British 'petrol' with American 'gas', producing the odd hybrid 'gas pump for petrol'; in Indian English, the consistent term is 'petrol pump'.

cloze.sentence: We need to stop at the next ____ ; the fuel light just came on.

en_def: to put fuel into a vehicle until the fuel tank is full
hi_def: टंकी भरवाना (गाड़ी की फ्यूल टंकी में तेल भरना)
hi_nuance: Learners sometimes say 'fill the petrol' or 'fill petrol' instead of the correct phrasal construction 'fill up the tank'; the object of 'fill up' should be the tank, not the fuel itself. Note that 'full tank, please' is the common short request used at the pump.

examples.en: Let's fill up the tank before we start the long drive to Pune.
examples.hi: पुणे की लंबी ड्राइव शुरू करने से पहले टंकी भरवा लेते हैं।

examples.en: I asked the attendant to fill up the tank completely.
examples.hi: मैंने अटेंडेंट से टंकी पूरी भरने को कहा।

examples.en: We only fill up the tank halfway to save on the weight.
examples.hi: हम वज़न बचाने के लिए टंकी सिर्फ़ आधी भरवाते हैं।

examples.en: Please fill up the tank with premium petrol this time.
examples.hi: इस बार कृपया टंकी में प्रीमियम पेट्रोल भरवाएँ।

examples.en: He forgot to fill up the tank and ran out of fuel on the highway.
examples.hi: वह टंकी भरवाना भूल गया और हाईवे पर उसका ईंधन ख़त्म हो गया।

common_mistake.wrong: Please fill the petrol in full.
common_mistake.right: Please fill up the tank.
common_mistake.why: Learners often say 'fill the petrol' treating fuel as the object; standard English treats the tank as the object: 'fill up the tank' (with petrol or diesel).

cloze.sentence: Before the long trip, we stopped to ____ completely.

en_def: the next place where a bus, train or metro will stop
hi_def: अगला स्टॉप (बस, ट्रेन या मेट्रो का अगला रुकने का स्थान)
hi_nuance: Learners generally get this right, but sometimes confuse 'stop' (for buses and metro) with 'station' (for trains); 'next stop' is standard for bus and metro announcements, while trains usually say 'next station'. It can also be confused with 'halt', a British and Indian railway term for a small station.

examples.en: Please get down at the next stop; this is where our office is.
examples.hi: कृपया अगले स्टॉप पर उतर जाना; यहीं हमारा दफ़्तर है।

examples.en: The conductor announced that the next stop was the central market.
examples.hi: कंडक्टर ने घोषणा की कि अगला स्टॉप सेंट्रल मार्केट है।

examples.en: I pressed the bell for the next stop near my house.
examples.hi: मैंने अपने घर के पास वाले अगले स्टॉप के लिए घंटी बजाई।

examples.en: The metro announcement said the next stop was Indiranagar.
examples.hi: मेट्रो की घोषणा में कहा गया कि अगला स्टॉप इंदिरानगर है।

examples.en: Excuse me, is the next stop close to the mall?
examples.hi: माफ़ कीजिए, क्या अगला स्टॉप मॉल के पास है?

collocations: get down at the next stop

common_mistake.wrong: I will get down on next stop.
common_mistake.right: I will get down at the next stop.
common_mistake.why: Learners often use the wrong preposition 'on' instead of 'at' before 'the next stop'; the correct fixed preposition here is 'at'.

cloze.sentence: Please ring the bell — I need to get off at the ____ .

en_def: to leave a bus, train or vehicle by stepping off it (Indian English usage)
hi_def: उतरना (बस, ट्रेन या गाड़ी से नीचे उतरना)
hi_nuance: This is one of the most classic Indian English calques: 'get down' is used everywhere in India for leaving public transport, but in British and American English 'get off' is the standard phrase, since 'get down' abroad usually means crouching or lowering oneself, or even slang for dancing. This is worth flagging directly since this learner may travel internationally for work.

examples.en: Please get down carefully; the train hasn't fully stopped yet.
examples.hi: कृपया ध्यान से उतरें; ट्रेन अभी पूरी तरह रुकी नहीं है।

examples.en: I usually get down two stops before my office to walk a little.
examples.hi: मैं आमतौर पर थोड़ा पैदल चलने के लिए अपने दफ़्तर से दो स्टॉप पहले उतर जाता हूँ।

examples.en: We got down at the wrong stop and had to walk back.
examples.hi: हम गलत स्टॉप पर उतर गए और हमें वापस पैदल जाना पड़ा।

examples.en: The conductor asked everyone to get down at the last stop.
examples.hi: कंडक्टर ने सबसे आख़िरी स्टॉप पर सबको उतरने को कहा।

examples.en: Get down here; this is the closest stop to the mall.
examples.hi: यहाँ उतर जाओ; यह मॉल के सबसे नज़दीक वाला स्टॉप है।

common_mistake.wrong: Get down from the plane after Delhi.
common_mistake.right: Get off the plane after landing in Delhi.
common_mistake.why: 'Get down' is Indian English for leaving a bus or train, but in international English 'get off' is the standard phrase for leaving any vehicle, including buses, trains and planes; 'get down' abroad can sound like crouching or even be misheard as slang.

cloze.sentence: This is our stop — let's ____ before the bus starts moving again.

en_def: the specific number assigned to a railway platform, used to identify where a train arrives or departs
hi_def: प्लेटफ़ॉर्म नंबर (रेलवे प्लेटफ़ॉर्म को दिया गया विशेष नंबर)
hi_nuance: Platform numbers in India can change suddenly close to departure time, so phrases like 'please confirm the platform number' are common and useful. 'Platform number' is also often shortened to just 'PF' or 'PF no.' in informal written Indian English, such as on tickets, which learners should recognise as an abbreviation.

examples.en: Please check the display board for the correct platform number.
examples.hi: कृपया सही प्लेटफ़ॉर्म नंबर के लिए डिस्प्ले बोर्ड देखें।

examples.en: Our platform number changed twice before the train finally arrived.
examples.hi: ट्रेन के आख़िरकार आने से पहले हमारा प्लेटफ़ॉर्म नंबर दो बार बदला।

examples.en: The announcement gave the platform number just ten minutes before departure.
examples.hi: घोषणा में प्रस्थान से सिर्फ़ दस मिनट पहले प्लेटफ़ॉर्म नंबर बताया गया।

examples.en: Can you tell me the platform number for the Chennai Express?
examples.hi: क्या आप मुझे चेन्नई एक्सप्रेस का प्लेटफ़ॉर्म नंबर बता सकते हैं?

examples.en: I always double-check the platform number to avoid boarding the wrong train.
examples.hi: गलत ट्रेन में चढ़ने से बचने के लिए मैं हमेशा प्लेटफ़ॉर्म नंबर दोबारा जाँचता हूँ।

common_mistake.wrong: Which platform this train comes?
common_mistake.right: Which platform number does this train arrive at?
common_mistake.why: Learners often drop the auxiliary verb 'does' and the preposition, producing an incomplete question; standard English needs the full structure with 'does' and 'at'.

cloze.sentence: The screen shows the ____ has changed from two to five.

en_def: an unreserved train compartment where passengers can travel without a seat reservation, usually crowded
hi_def: जनरल डिब्बा (बिना आरक्षण वाला ट्रेन का डिब्बा, जो आमतौर पर भीड़भाड़ वाला होता है)
hi_nuance: This is a distinctly Indian Railways concept with no direct Western equivalent; learners should be ready to explain it to non-Indian colleagues as 'an unreserved, first-come-first-served compartment'. Spoken Indian English also commonly shortens 'general compartment' to just 'general', dropping the noun.

examples.en: We couldn't get a reservation, so we travelled in the general compartment.
examples.hi: हमें रिज़र्वेशन नहीं मिला, इसलिए हमने जनरल डिब्बे में यात्रा की।

examples.en: The general compartment was so crowded that we had to stand the whole way.
examples.hi: जनरल डिब्बा इतना भरा हुआ था कि हमें पूरे रास्ते खड़े रहना पड़ा।

examples.en: He always prefers the general compartment because tickets are cheaper.
examples.hi: वह हमेशा जनरल डिब्बा पसंद करता है क्योंकि टिकट सस्ते होते हैं।

examples.en: Fights sometimes break out over seats in the general compartment.
examples.hi: जनरल डिब्बे में सीटों को लेकर कभी-कभी झगड़े हो जाते हैं।

examples.en: We boarded the general compartment since the waiting list hadn't cleared.
examples.hi: चूँकि वेटिंग लिस्ट साफ़ नहीं हुई थी, हम जनरल डिब्बे में चढ़ गए।

common_mistake.wrong: We are going in general only.
common_mistake.right: We are travelling in the general compartment.
common_mistake.why: Spoken Indian English often shortens 'general compartment' to just 'general', omitting the noun; a full and clear sentence should include 'compartment'.

cloze.sentence: Since we didn't have a reservation, we had to travel in the ____ .

en_def: the phone number connected to someone's mobile phone, used to call or message them
hi_def: मोबाइल नंबर (मोबाइल फ़ोन से जुड़ा नंबर, जिस पर कॉल या मैसेज किया जाता है)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often say 'What is your mobile?' dropping 'number', which sounds odd in English because 'mobile' alone means the phone itself, not the number. In British English the device is called a 'mobile phone' or 'mobile', while American English says 'cell phone' or 'cell number' — Indian offices often mix both, writing 'Contact: mobile no.' Also 'number' is countable, so say 'give me your mobile number', not 'give me your mobile numbers' unless you truly have more than one.

examples.en: Can you share your mobile number so I can save it?
examples.hi: क्या आप अपना मोबाइल नंबर शेयर कर सकते हैं ताकि मैं उसे सेव कर लूँ?

examples.en: I changed my mobile number after I lost my old SIM.
examples.hi: पुराना सिम खोने के बाद मैंने अपना मोबाइल नंबर बदल दिया।

examples.en: The bank asked me to verify my mobile number before login.
examples.hi: बैंक ने लॉगिन से पहले मेरा मोबाइल नंबर सत्यापित करने को कहा।

examples.en: Please update your mobile number in the office HR system.
examples.hi: कृपया ऑफ़िस के एचआर सिस्टम में अपना मोबाइल नंबर अपडेट करें।

examples.en: He gave the wrong mobile number, so the delivery boy couldn't reach him.
examples.hi: उसने ग़लत मोबाइल नंबर दिया, इसलिए डिलीवरी वाला उस तक नहीं पहुँच पाया।

common_mistake.wrong: What is your good mobile number?
common_mistake.right: What is your mobile number?
common_mistake.why: 'Good name' is a polite Indian-English phrase borrowed from Hindi ('शुभ नाम'), but it doesn't extend to 'good mobile number' — native speakers simply say 'your mobile number' or 'your number'.

cloze.sentence: I lost my phone, so please call me on my new ____.

en_def: a phone call that was not answered, so it stops ringing and is only recorded as a call attempt
hi_def: मिस्ड कॉल (ऐसी कॉल जिसे उठाया नहीं गया और वह केवल एक सूचना के रूप में रह जाती है)
hi_nuance: 'Missed call' is standard English, but in India it has taken on an extra cultural meaning — people deliberately dial and hang up as a free signal, which doesn't exist in the West. Saying 'I did a missed call' is understood in India but sounds odd to a British or American listener, who would say 'I gave you a missed call' or simply 'I called and hung up'.

examples.en: I have three missed calls from an unknown number.
examples.hi: मेरे पास एक अनजान नंबर से तीन मिस्ड कॉल हैं।

examples.en: Sorry, I was in a meeting — I saw your missed call later.
examples.hi: माफ़ करना, मैं मीटिंग में था — मैंने तुम्हारी मिस्ड कॉल बाद में देखी।

examples.en: She checked her phone and found a missed call from her mother.
examples.hi: उसने अपना फ़ोन देखा और माँ की मिस्ड कॉल पाई।

examples.en: I'll give you a missed call when the cab arrives outside.
examples.hi: जब कैब बाहर पहुँचेगी तो मैं तुम्हें मिस्ड कॉल दूँगा।

examples.en: My phone shows a missed call, but there's no voicemail.
examples.hi: मेरे फ़ोन पर मिस्ड कॉल दिख रही है, लेकिन कोई वॉइसमेल नहीं है।

common_mistake.wrong: He did a missed call to me.
common_mistake.right: He gave me a missed call.
common_mistake.why: In Indian English, the verb used with 'missed call' is 'give', not 'do' — 'give a missed call' is the fixed collocation, similar to 'give a ring'.

cloze.sentence: I saw a ____ from you, so I called back immediately.

en_def: to call someone and hang up before they answer, usually as a signal rather than to talk
hi_def: मिस्ड कॉल देना (जानबूझकर कॉल करके काटना, बात करने के लिए नहीं बल्कि इशारा देने के लिए)
hi_nuance: This exact phrase is an Indian-English invention — 'give a missed call' doesn't exist in British or American English, where people would say 'call and hang up' or 'flash me' (in some regions). It's completely natural in Indian offices and families, but using it abroad may confuse people, so it's worth knowing it's an India-specific fixed expression.

examples.en: Give me a missed call when you reach the metro station.
examples.hi: जब तुम मेट्रो स्टेशन पहुँचो तो मुझे मिस्ड कॉल देना।

examples.en: I gave him a missed call so he would call me back and save my balance.
examples.hi: मैंने उसे मिस्ड कॉल दी ताकि वह मुझे वापस कॉल करे और मेरा बैलेंस बच जाए।

examples.en: Just give a missed call once you're outside the gate.
examples.hi: बस गेट के बाहर पहुँचते ही मिस्ड कॉल दे देना।

examples.en: She gives her brother a missed call every morning to wake him up.
examples.hi: वह हर सुबह अपने भाई को जगाने के लिए मिस्ड कॉल देती है।

examples.en: Don't call and talk, just give a missed call, I'll call you back.
examples.hi: कॉल करके बात मत करना, बस मिस्ड कॉल दे देना, मैं वापस कॉल कर लूँगा।

common_mistake.wrong: Please missed call me when you arrive.
common_mistake.right: Please give me a missed call when you arrive.
common_mistake.why: 'Missed call' is a noun, not a verb, so it needs 'give' before it — you cannot say 'missed call me', only 'give me a missed call'.

cloze.sentence: Don't waste your balance talking — just ____ and I'll call you back.

en_def: the signal or connection that lets a mobile phone make calls and use data
hi_def: नेटवर्क (मोबाइल फ़ोन की वह सिग्नल व्यवस्था जिससे कॉल और डेटा चलता है)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers often say 'my phone is not catching network' — a direct translation influenced by 'नेटवर्क नहीं पकड़ रहा'. In natural English you 'get' or 'have' network/signal, you don't 'catch' it. Also, 'network' in tech contexts (like computer networks) is a separate, wider meaning that engineers should keep distinct from 'mobile network/signal'.

examples.en: The network is very weak inside the basement parking.
examples.hi: बेसमेंट पार्किंग के अंदर नेटवर्क बहुत कमज़ोर है।

examples.en: I couldn't call you because there was no network in the tunnel.
examples.hi: मैं तुम्हें कॉल नहीं कर पाया क्योंकि सुरंग में नेटवर्क नहीं था।

examples.en: Which network do you use, Jio or Airtel?
examples.hi: तुम कौन सा नेटवर्क इस्तेमाल करते हो, जियो या एयरटेल?

examples.en: The network improved as soon as I stepped out of the elevator.
examples.hi: लिफ़्ट से बाहर निकलते ही नेटवर्क बेहतर हो गया।

examples.en: Our office building has poor network on the top floor.
examples.hi: हमारी ऑफ़िस बिल्डिंग की सबसे ऊपरी मंज़िल पर नेटवर्क कमज़ोर है।

common_mistake.wrong: My phone is not catching network here.
common_mistake.right: My phone isn't getting any network here.
common_mistake.why: 'Catch network' is a literal translation from Hindi; in natural English you 'get', 'have' or 'lose' network/signal, you don't 'catch' it.

cloze.sentence: There's no ____ in this elevator, so my calls always drop.

en_def: used to say that a mobile or internet network has stopped working completely for a period
hi_def: नेटवर्क डाउन है (मोबाइल या इंटरनेट नेटवर्क पूरी तरह से काम करना बंद कर देना)
hi_nuance: Indian English speakers often say 'network is not working' or 'network is gone', which is understandable but less precise than the standard technical phrase 'the network is down', commonly used by engineers and customer care. 'Down' here means 'not functioning', the same sense as 'the server is down' or 'the website is down' — a useful pattern for IT professionals to reuse.

examples.en: The whole area's network is down after last night's storm.
examples.hi: कल रात के तूफ़ान के बाद इस पूरे इलाक़े का नेटवर्क डाउन है।

examples.en: Customer care said the network is down for maintenance tonight.
examples.hi: कस्टमर केयर ने बताया कि आज रात नेटवर्क मेंटेनेंस के लिए डाउन है।

examples.en: If the network is down, even emergency calls won't connect.
examples.hi: अगर नेटवर्क डाउन है, तो इमरजेंसी कॉल भी नहीं लगेगी।

examples.en: I couldn't do UPI payments because the network was down for an hour.
examples.hi: मैं यूपीआई भुगतान नहीं कर पाया क्योंकि एक घंटे तक नेटवर्क डाउन था।

examples.en: The technician confirmed the tower's network was down, not just my phone.
examples.hi: तकनीशियन ने बताया कि टावर का नेटवर्क डाउन था, सिर्फ़ मेरा फ़ोन नहीं।

common_mistake.wrong: The network is off today.
common_mistake.right: The network is down today.
common_mistake.why: 'Off' is used for switches and devices you control ('the Wi-Fi is off'), while a network failure caused by the provider is described as 'down', not 'off'.

cloze.sentence: I can't make any calls — the ____ since morning.

en_def: having no phone signal at all, so calls, messages and internet don't work
hi_def: नो नेटवर्क, कोई नेटवर्क नहीं (फ़ोन में सिग्नल बिल्कुल न आना)
hi_nuance: This phrase is used correctly by Hindi speakers most of the time, but many add an extra word and say 'there is no any network', doubling the negative under Hindi influence ('कोई भी नेटवर्क नहीं'). Standard English uses only one negative: 'there is no network' or 'there isn't any network', never both together.

examples.en: There is no network in the hill station we visited last week.
examples.hi: पिछले हफ़्ते हम जिस हिल स्टेशन गए थे वहाँ कोई नेटवर्क नहीं था।

examples.en: My screen shows 'No network' whenever I enter the lift.
examples.hi: लिफ़्ट में घुसते ही मेरी स्क्रीन पर 'नो नेटवर्क' दिखने लगता है।

examples.en: We had no network for two days during the trek.
examples.hi: ट्रेक के दौरान हमारे पास दो दिन तक कोई नेटवर्क नहीं था।

examples.en: With no network, I couldn't check my office emails all evening.
examples.hi: नेटवर्क न होने की वजह से मैं पूरी शाम अपने ऑफ़िस के ईमेल चेक नहीं कर पाया।

examples.en: The village has no network, so people climb a hill to make calls.
examples.hi: उस गाँव में कोई नेटवर्क नहीं है, इसलिए लोग कॉल करने के लिए एक पहाड़ी पर चढ़ते हैं।

common_mistake.wrong: There is no any network in this basement.
common_mistake.right: There is no network in this basement.
common_mistake.why: English does not double negatives with 'no' and 'any' together — say either 'no network' or 'not any network', never both in the same clause.

cloze.sentence: I tried calling you all day, but my phone showed ____.

en_def: the act of adding money or validity to a prepaid mobile connection, or the amount added
hi_def: रिचार्ज (प्रीपेड मोबाइल कनेक्शन में पैसे या वैधता डलवाना)
hi_nuance: Indian English uses 'recharge' both as a noun ('I did a recharge') and verb ('recharge my number'), which is correct and widely understood — but it's an India/South-Asia-specific usage; in the US or UK people 'top up' their phone, they don't say 'recharge' for money (they use 'recharge' only for batteries). So 'top up' is the international equivalent worth knowing.

examples.en: I need to recharge my phone before the balance runs out.
examples.hi: बैलेंस ख़त्म होने से पहले मुझे अपना फ़ोन रिचार्ज करना होगा।

examples.en: Can you do a recharge of 199 rupees on this number?
examples.hi: क्या तुम इस नंबर पर 199 रुपये का रिचार्ज कर सकते हो?

examples.en: I recharge my mother's number every month through the app.
examples.hi: मैं हर महीने ऐप के ज़रिए अपनी माँ के नंबर का रिचार्ज करता हूँ।

examples.en: The shop near our office also does mobile recharges.
examples.hi: हमारे ऑफ़िस के पास वाली दुकान मोबाइल रिचार्ज भी करती है।

examples.en: My recharge got deducted, but the balance didn't update.
examples.hi: मेरा रिचार्ज कट गया, लेकिन बैलेंस अपडेट नहीं हुआ।

common_mistake.wrong: Please do the needful and recharge my number, sir.
common_mistake.right: Please recharge my number, sir.
common_mistake.why: 'Do the needful' is a very common Indian-office phrase but sounds old-fashioned and overly formal to most native speakers; a direct request like 'please recharge my number' or 'could you recharge my number' is more natural.

cloze.sentence: My balance is almost zero — I need to ____ today.

en_def: a prepaid plan that gives a fixed amount of internet data for a certain time
hi_def: डेटा पैक (एक निश्चित समय के लिए तय मात्रा में इंटरनेट डेटा देने वाला प्रीपेड प्लान)
hi_nuance: Many Indian speakers say 'net pack' instead of 'data pack' — both are understood locally, but 'data pack' or 'data plan' is the term used by telecom companies and in formal writing, while 'net pack' is colloquial slang. In American English, people usually say 'data plan', not 'pack' at all.

examples.en: I bought a new data pack because my internet ran out.
examples.hi: मैंने नया डेटा पैक ख़रीदा क्योंकि मेरा इंटरनेट ख़त्म हो गया था।

examples.en: This data pack gives 2GB per day for 28 days.
examples.hi: यह डेटा पैक 28 दिनों तक रोज़ाना 2जीबी देता है।

examples.en: Which data pack do you use for working from home?
examples.hi: वर्क फ्रॉम होम के लिए तुम कौन सा डेटा पैक इस्तेमाल करते हो?

examples.en: My data pack expired at midnight, so I had no internet this morning.
examples.hi: मेरा डेटा पैक आधी रात को ख़त्म हो गया, इसलिए आज सुबह मेरे पास इंटरनेट नहीं था।

examples.en: The company offers a special data pack for students.
examples.hi: कंपनी छात्रों के लिए एक ख़ास डेटा पैक देती है।

common_mistake.wrong: I need to recharge my net pack.
common_mistake.right: I need to recharge my data pack.
common_mistake.why: 'Net pack' is common spoken slang in India, but 'data pack' or 'data plan' is the correct term used in official telecom communication and understood internationally.

cloze.sentence: My phone shows 'low data' — I should buy a new ____ today.

en_def: the secret code needed to connect a device to a particular Wi-Fi network
hi_def: वाई-फ़ाई पासवर्ड (किसी वाई-फ़ाई नेटवर्क से डिवाइस को जोड़ने के लिए ज़रूरी गुप्त कोड)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers usually get this phrase right, but often confuse 'Wi-Fi' with 'internet' generally, asking 'what is your internet password' when they mean the Wi-Fi network's password specifically — useful to distinguish, since a phone can have mobile data (internet) without any Wi-Fi involved at all.

examples.en: Could you share the Wi-Fi password for the guest network?
examples.hi: क्या आप गेस्ट नेटवर्क का वाई-फ़ाई पासवर्ड शेयर कर सकते हैं?

examples.en: I forgot the Wi-Fi password after we changed the router.
examples.hi: राउटर बदलने के बाद मैं वाई-फ़ाई पासवर्ड भूल गया।

examples.en: The café prints the Wi-Fi password on the receipt.
examples.hi: कैफ़े रसीद पर वाई-फ़ाई पासवर्ड छाप देता है।

examples.en: Please don't share the office Wi-Fi password with visitors.
examples.hi: कृपया ऑफ़िस का वाई-फ़ाई पासवर्ड आगंतुकों के साथ साझा न करें।

examples.en: I reset the Wi-Fi password because it was too weak.
examples.hi: मैंने वाई-फ़ाई पासवर्ड रीसेट किया क्योंकि वह बहुत कमज़ोर था।

common_mistake.wrong: What is your internet password?
common_mistake.right: What is your Wi-Fi password?
common_mistake.why: 'Internet' refers to the global network in general and has no single password; the password belongs specifically to the local Wi-Fi network, so 'Wi-Fi password' is the correct, specific term.

cloze.sentence: Guests always ask for the ____ as soon as they arrive.

en_def: a feature that lets one device share its mobile internet connection with other devices
hi_def: हॉटस्पॉट (एक ऐसा फ़ीचर जिससे एक डिवाइस अपना मोबाइल इंटरनेट दूसरे डिवाइस के साथ साझा करता है)
hi_nuance: In India, 'hotspot' is almost always used to mean personal mobile hotspot (sharing phone data), but in general English it can also mean any place offering free public Wi-Fi, like a café or airport — a distinction worth keeping in mind when reading international material, where 'Wi-Fi hotspot' often refers to the public-place sense.

examples.en: I turned on my hotspot so my laptop could get internet.
examples.hi: मैंने अपना हॉटस्पॉट ऑन किया ताकि मेरे लैपटॉप को इंटरनेट मिल सके।

examples.en: My phone's hotspot only supports two devices at a time.
examples.hi: मेरे फ़ोन का हॉटस्पॉट एक बार में केवल दो डिवाइस को सपोर्ट करता है।

examples.en: The airport lounge has a free Wi-Fi hotspot for passengers.
examples.hi: एयरपोर्ट लाउंज में यात्रियों के लिए मुफ़्त वाई-फ़ाई हॉटस्पॉट है।

examples.en: Can I connect to your hotspot for a few minutes?
examples.hi: क्या मैं कुछ मिनट के लिए तुम्हारे हॉटस्पॉट से जुड़ सकता हूँ?

examples.en: Using the hotspot all day drained my phone's battery quickly.
examples.hi: पूरे दिन हॉटस्पॉट इस्तेमाल करने से मेरे फ़ोन की बैटरी जल्दी ख़त्म हो गई।

common_mistake.wrong: I gave him my hotspot.
common_mistake.right: I turned on my hotspot for him.
common_mistake.why: 'Hotspot' is a feature you switch on, not an object you physically give — the natural verb is 'turn on', 'switch on' or 'share', not 'give'.

cloze.sentence: My Wi-Fi isn't working, so let me share my phone's ____.

en_def: an image captured of exactly what is showing on a screen at a particular moment
hi_def: स्क्रीनशॉट (किसी क्षण में स्क्रीन पर दिख रही चीज़ की तस्वीर)
hi_nuance: This word is used correctly by most Hindi speakers, but many say 'take a screenshot' as 'do a screenshot' or 'click a screenshot' (confusing it with photography). The correct verb is 'take a screenshot', matching 'take a photo', not 'click' or 'do', even though 'click' is common in casual Indian speech.

examples.en: Take a screenshot of the error message and send it to me.
examples.hi: एरर मैसेज का स्क्रीनशॉट लो और मुझे भेज दो।

examples.en: I took a screenshot of the payment confirmation for my records.
examples.hi: मैंने अपने रिकॉर्ड के लिए भुगतान पुष्टि का स्क्रीनशॉट लिया।

examples.en: Can you send me a screenshot of the meeting invite?
examples.hi: क्या तुम मुझे मीटिंग इनवाइट का स्क्रीनशॉट भेज सकते हो?

examples.en: The app doesn't allow you to take a screenshot of the OTP screen.
examples.hi: यह ऐप ओटीपी स्क्रीन का स्क्रीनशॉट लेने नहीं देता।

examples.en: I attached a screenshot showing the bug in the dashboard.
examples.hi: मैंने डैशबोर्ड में दिख रही ख़राबी दिखाने वाला स्क्रीनशॉट अटैच किया।

common_mistake.wrong: I clicked a screenshot of the error.
common_mistake.right: I took a screenshot of the error.
common_mistake.why: 'Click a photo' is common informal Indian English for photography, but for screens the standard fixed verb is 'take a screenshot', not 'click'.

cloze.sentence: Can you ____ of that error so I can show it to support?

en_def: to make someone wait, usually on the phone, while you deal with something else
hi_def: होल्ड पर रखना (फ़ोन पर किसी को इंतज़ार कराना जबकि कोई और काम निपटाया जाता है)
hi_nuance: Indian call centres often say 'kindly stay on the line, I am putting you on hold', which is fine, but many Hindi speakers also say 'don't cut the call' when they mean 'please hold', mixing up 'hold' (temporary pause, connection stays) with 'cut' (ending the call completely) — these are opposite actions and shouldn't be confused.

examples.en: The support executive put me on hold for ten minutes.
examples.hi: सपोर्ट एग्ज़िक्यूटिव ने मुझे दस मिनट के लिए होल्ड पर रखा।

examples.en: Sorry, can I put you on hold while I check the system?
examples.hi: माफ़ करना, क्या मैं सिस्टम चेक करते समय तुम्हें होल्ड पर रख सकता हूँ?

examples.en: I hate being put on hold with annoying music playing.
examples.hi: मुझे होल्ड पर रखे जाना और साथ में बजने वाला बोर संगीत बिल्कुल पसंद नहीं।

examples.en: The receptionist put the call on hold and transferred it to my manager.
examples.hi: रिसेप्शनिस्ट ने कॉल को होल्ड पर रखा और मेरे मैनेजर को ट्रांसफ़र कर दिया।

examples.en: Please don't put me on hold again, I'm in a hurry.
examples.hi: कृपया मुझे दोबारा होल्ड पर मत रखना, मुझे जल्दी है।

common_mistake.wrong: Please don't cut the call, I am checking.
common_mistake.right: Please stay on hold, I am checking.
common_mistake.why: 'Cut the call' means to end/disconnect the call entirely, while 'hold' means to pause without disconnecting — these are opposite actions, so mixing them confuses the listener about whether the call is still connected.

cloze.sentence: The bank ____ me for fifteen minutes before someone finally answered.

en_def: a phone feature that alerts you to a second incoming call while you are already on a call
hi_def: कॉल वेटिंग (एक फ़ोन फ़ीचर जो पहली कॉल के दौरान दूसरी आने वाली कॉल की सूचना देता है)
hi_nuance: Hindi speakers sometimes describe this by saying 'another call is beeping', which is a fair informal description, but the technical/standard English name for the feature itself is 'call waiting' — worth using this term when talking to customer care or in a technical context, e.g. 'please enable call waiting on my number'.

examples.en: I have call waiting enabled, so I never miss important calls.
examples.hi: मेरे पास कॉल वेटिंग चालू है, इसलिए मैं कभी ज़रूरी कॉल नहीं चूकता।

examples.en: A call waiting tone beeped while I was talking to my client.
examples.hi: जब मैं अपने क्लाइंट से बात कर रहा था तब कॉल वेटिंग की टोन बजी।

examples.en: Can you switch off call waiting? It's distracting during meetings.
examples.hi: क्या तुम कॉल वेटिंग बंद कर सकते हो? यह मीटिंग के दौरान ध्यान भटकाता है।

examples.en: Without call waiting, that second call would have gone straight to voicemail.
examples.hi: कॉल वेटिंग के बिना, वह दूसरी कॉल सीधे वॉइसमेल पर चली जाती।

examples.en: Please ask the operator to activate call waiting on this SIM.
examples.hi: कृपया ऑपरेटर से कहें कि इस सिम पर कॉल वेटिंग चालू कर दें।

common_mistake.wrong: Another call is waiting me.
common_mistake.right: I have a call waiting.
common_mistake.why: 'Waiting' here describes the incoming call, not the person, so the correct construction is 'a call is waiting' or 'I have a call waiting' — you cannot say 'the call is waiting me'.

cloze.sentence: I heard a beep during the call — must be ____.

en_def: used to describe a phone call that keeps getting disconnected because of a weak signal
hi_def: कॉल ड्रॉप हो रही है (कमज़ोर सिग्नल की वजह से बार-बार कॉल कट जाना)
hi_nuance: Many Hindi speakers say 'the line is cutting' — a direct translation of 'लाइन कट रही है' — which sounds unnatural in English. The correct native phrases are 'the call is dropping' or 'the call keeps breaking up' (for choppy audio) or simply 'my call got disconnected' — 'cutting' is not used this way in standard English.

examples.en: Sorry, the call is dropping — can you hear me clearly now?
examples.hi: माफ़ करना, कॉल ड्रॉप हो रही है — क्या अब तुम मुझे साफ़ सुन पा रहे हो?

examples.en: Our video call kept dropping during the storm last night.
examples.hi: कल रात तूफ़ान के दौरान हमारी वीडियो कॉल बार-बार ड्रॉप हो रही थी।

examples.en: The call dropped three times before we finished the interview.
examples.hi: इंटरव्यू ख़त्म होने से पहले कॉल तीन बार ड्रॉप हुई।

examples.en: If your call is dropping, try moving closer to the window.
examples.hi: अगर तुम्हारी कॉल ड्रॉप हो रही है, तो खिड़की के पास आकर देखो।

examples.en: The signal is so poor here that every call drops within a minute.
examples.hi: यहाँ सिग्नल इतना कमज़ोर है कि हर कॉल एक मिनट में ड्रॉप हो जाती है।

common_mistake.wrong: The line is cutting, can you hear me?
common_mistake.right: The call is dropping, can you hear me?
common_mistake.why: 'The line is cutting' is a literal translation from Hindi and isn't natural English; native speakers say 'the call is dropping' or 'the call keeps breaking up' instead.

cloze.sentence: Hold on, ____ — let me move to a better spot.

en_def: a temporary numeric code, usually sent by SMS, used once to verify identity or confirm a transaction
hi_def: ओटीपी (एक बार इस्तेमाल होने वाला अस्थायी संख्यात्मक कोड, जो पहचान सत्यापित करने या लेन-देन की पुष्टि के लिए एसएमएस से भेजा जाता है)
